Distractors A (Deccan plateau in Maharashtra), C (Coastal plains), D (Mudkhed hills) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: The multipurpose project of Gujarat 'Ukai' is situated on which River?
questions.explanation: Ukai dam—Gujarat's major multipurpose project—spans the Tapti (Tapi) river near Surat. Sabarmati, Mahi, and Narmada host other iconic dams (Dharoi, Kadana, Sardar Sarovar)—Ukai–Tapti is the pair to memorise for western-India hydrology MCQs.

questions.text: In which state the number of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies was highest at the end of March 2020?
questions.explanation: Option D reflects March 2020 cooperative statistics: Maharashtra reported the highest number of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies among states—deep rural credit penetration via PACs. Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Gujarat rank high but below Maharashtra's PAC network count in NABARD/NAFSCOB tables.

questions.text: The Government appointed a Committee in 1993 on Disinvestment in Public Sector Enterprises under the Chairmanship of _______.
questions.explanation: Option C is correct because C. Rangarajan chaired the 1993 Disinvestment Committee recommending phased PSU stake sales. G.V. Ramakrishna later led the Disinvestment Commission; Montek Ahluwalia and C.P. Chandrasekhar belong to planning/finance debates—not this 1993 panel chair. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: During 2017-18 Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) was highest 23.6 percent in _______ sector in India.
questions.explanation: FDI inflows during 2017–18 peaked at about 23.6% in communication services (telecom/internet economy)—not manufacturing or real estate. Financial services and wholesale trade drew large totals but the highest sectoral share that year was telecom-led communication.

questions.text: To tackle the burgeoning problem of air pollution, the 2021-22 Budget proposes to provide an amount of Rs. 2217 crore for _______ urban centres with a million-plus population.
questions.explanation: Option B matches the question because Union Budget 2021–22 allocated ₹2,217 crore for air-quality management across 42 million-plus cities under the Urban Swachh Bharat/National Clean Air Programme umbrella. Counts of 32, 52, or 62 cities mis-state the notified urban cluster target. You can eliminate A (32), C (52), D (62) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text:
Match the following:
(a) Second largest agro based industry in India - (i) Cotton industry
(b) One of the oldest and organised industry in India - (ii) Iron and steel industry
(c) Industry leading to rapid industrialisation - (iii) Sugar industry
(d) Use of new technology - (iv) Automobile industry
questions.explanation: Choose option C: industry pairing: sugar — second-largest agro-based industry (iii); cotton — oldest organised industry (i); iron and steel — industrialisation driver (ii); automobiles — new-technology flagship (iv). Option C's (iii), (i), (ii), (iv) alone keeps superlative labels aligned. Distractors A ((ii), (i), (iii), (iv)), B ((iii), (ii), (i), (iv)), D ((iii), (iv), (i), (ii)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) has a right to order conduct of supplementary audit and he may also comment upon the audit report within _______ days from the date of receipt of audit report.
questions.explanation: This resolves to 60 days. The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG, Articles 148–151) is appointed by the President for a six-year tenure or until 65 years, and audits all Union and State receipts and expenditure. The safest way to lock this item into recall is to write the correct option next to its associated year or body in your revision notebook and skim it weekly.

questions.text: The difference between fiscal deficit and interest payment during the year is called _______.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option C — Primary deficit equals fiscal deficit minus interest payments on past debt—isolating the non-interest borrowing need. Equating it with revenue deficit or repeating 'fiscal deficit' ignores the interest-subtraction step central to FRBM vocabulary. You can eliminate A (Fiscal deficit), B (Budget deficit), D (Revenue deficit) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements in the context of Seventh Finance Commission for distribution of the states share of the central excise duty:
(a) 25 percent weightage for population.
(b) 33.5 percent weightage for poor in each state.
(c) 16.5 percent weightage for increase in the per capita income of the state.
(d) 25 percent weightage for income equalisation between state.
Which of the statement/s given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The right answer is Only (a) and (d) are correct (option A). The Finance Commission (Article 280) is constituted every five years by the President to recommend distribution of tax revenues between the Union and States and grants-in-aid. Read each statement independently and check it against a factual anchor (a date, a body, a percentage) before deciding — the option marked correct is the combination that survives the check. The examiner rewards precision on this item — every option is engineered to feel plausible, but only the marked one matches the exact wording of the source document.

questions.text:

options.D: All of the above are correct

Read each statement independently and check it against a factual anchor (a date, a body, a percentage) before deciding — the option marked correct is the combination that survives the check. questions.text:

(b) Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) was introduced in February 2006.
(c) The Nehru Rozgar Yojana (NRY) was launched in October 1989 for the benefit of the rural poor.
Which of the following statement/s given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The answer is option C: SGRY launched September 2001 (a) and MGNREGS notified February 2006 (b)—both dates stand. Nehru Rozgar Yojana's October 1989 date is correct historically but the correct pair is (a)+(b); You can eliminate A ((a) only), B ((b) only), D ((a) and (c) only) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: N.K. Singh Committee of 2016 is related to _______.

options.D: Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act

questions.explanation: Option D maps the N.K. Singh Committee (2016) to FRBM Act review—debt trajectory, fiscal-deficit bands, and escape clauses. Twelfth Finance Commission and Twelfth Plan chairs were different bodies; Fourteenth FC was Y.V. Reddy—not N.K. Singh's 2016 FRBM mandate.

questions.text:
Which of the following were the reasons for small land holdings during 1980 to 1985 in India?
(a) Law of inheritance
(b) Rapidly growing population
(c) Rural indebtedness
(d) Rapidly growing joint family system
questions.explanation: Small holdings in the 1980–85 period stemmed from inheritance fragmentation (a), population pressure on land (b), and rural indebtedness forcing sales (c)—not a 'growing joint family system' (d), which would consolidate holdings. Joint-family decline is the demographic trend.

questions.text: During which five year plan three major steel plants in the public sector were built up at Rourkela, Bhilai and Durgapur?
questions.explanation: Option B is the right choice since Rourkela, Bhilai, and Durgapur steel plants were core Second Five Year Plan (1956–61) public-sector projects with foreign collaboration. First Plan focused on irrigation/ railways; Third and Fourth Plans expanded but did not originate this steel triad. You can eliminate A (First Five Year Plan), C (Third Five Year Plan), D (Fourth Five Year Plan) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: Which of the following is not objective of National Population Policy 2000?

options.D: Incentive to adopt two child small family

questions.explanation: The correct answer is option C — National Population Policy 2000 targets infant-mortality reduction, universal immunisation, and two-child norm incentives—not mid-day meals for poor children, which belong to the education/social-welfare scheme basket. Distractors A (Reduction in infant mortality), B (Universal immunisation), D (Incentive to adopt two child small fami…) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a quantitative monetary measure of Reserve Bank of India?
questions.explanation: Option B — Moral Suasion — is the right pick here. The Reserve Bank of India was established under the RBI Act 1934 (operative 1 April 1935) and nationalised on 1 January 1949; it is India's monetary authority and banking regulator. For MPSC prelims, one line of revision is enough to lock this fact into memory — add it to your one-page factual notebook.

questions.text: Which of the following substance has the highest thermal conductivity?
questions.explanation: Option D is correct. Silver tops common metals in thermal conductivity at room temperature—ahead of aluminium, copper's competitor set, wood, and glass insulators. Picking aluminium confuses electrical conduction rankings; wood and glass are deliberate thermal insulator distractors.

questions.text: Light enters the eye through thin membrane called the _______.
questions.explanation: The answer is option D: the cornea is the transparent front membrane through which light first enters the eyeball. Iris and pupil regulate light; retina receives the focused image—anatomy questions on 'first entry' always point to cornea, not pupil opening. Distractors A (Iris), B (Pupil), C (Retina) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: Echo is heard if the distance between the source of sound and the obstacle is _______.

options.B: More than or equal to 17 meters

questions.explanation: Audible echo needs the obstacle at least ~17 m away so the reflected sound reaches the ear ≥0.1 s after the direct sound at 340 m/s. Distances under 17 m merge direct and reflected waves; 'less than 7 m' is far too short.

questions.text: In _______ model of an atom, the angular momentum (mvr) of an electron is an integral multiple of the quantity h/2π.
questions.explanation: Choose option C: Bohr's model quantises angular momentum as mvr = nh/2π for permitted electron orbits. Rutherford lacked quantisation; Dalton proposed atomic spheres; Fermi is associated with nuclear statistics—not this orbital quantum condition. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: Choose the incorrect answer:

options.A: Bonding molecular orbitals are formed by the additive effect of the atomic orbitals.
options.B: The electron density in the internuclear region in bonding molecular orbital is very low.
options.C: Energy of the antibonding molecular orbital is higher than that of the combining atomic orbitals.
options.D: Antibonding molecular orbitals are represented by σ*, π*, δ*, etc.

questions.explanation: Option B is the right choice since Bonding MOs concentrate electron density between nuclei—statement (B) wrongly claims 'very low' internuclear density, making it the incorrect line. Additive overlap (A), higher antibonding energy (C), and σ*/π* labelling (D) are standard MO theory truths. Distractors A (Bonding molecular orbitals are formed b…), C (Energy of the antibonding molecular orb…), D (Antibonding molecular orbitals are repr…) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: During biological nitrogen fixation, nitrifying bacteria convert _______.
questions.explanation: Option C reflects nitrification (despite the stem's 'fixation' wording): nitrifying bacteria oxidise NH₄⁺ to NO₃⁻ through nitrite intermediates. N₂→NH₄⁺ is Rhizobium's fixation step; reverse reductions (A, D) belong to denitrifiers—not the correct conversion path examiners marked.

questions.text:
Match the following:
(a) Python molurus - (i) Haemotoxic
(b) Naja naja - (ii) Blind snake
(c) Viper russelli - (iii) Neurotoxic
(d) Typhlops braminus - (iv) Non-poisonous
questions.explanation: Option A works here because Lock snake toxicology: Python molurus — non-poisonous (iv); Naja naja — neurotoxic (iii); Viper russelli — haemotoxic (i); Typhlops braminus — blind snake (ii). Option A's (iv), (iii), (i), (ii) grid alone keeps venom type and species aligned. You can eliminate B ((iii), (iv), (ii), (i)), C ((i), (ii), (iv), (iii)), D ((iii), (i), (ii), (iv)) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of larval stages of Aurelia?
questions.explanation: Option A is correct because aurelia (jellyfish) life cycle runs planula → scyphistoma (hydratuba polyp stage) → ephyra → medusa. Reversed or scrambled orders (Ephyra before scyphistoma) violate cnidarian metagenesis taught in standard zoology practical syllabi. Distractors B (Planula, Ephyra, Scyphistoma, Hydratuba), C (Scyphistoma, Planula, Hydratuba, Ephyra), D (Hydratuba, Ephyra, Planula, Scyphistoma) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Which of the following is/are group/groups of reptilian animals?
(a) Lizard, Snake, Frog and Loris
(b) Turtle, Gharial, Caiman and Tuatara
(c) Turtle, Crocodile, Salamander and Lizard
(d) Salamander, Catotes, Turtle and Frog
questions.explanation: Only set (b)—turtle, gharial, caiman, tuatara—are reptiles. Frogs and salamanders are amphibians; loris is a primate; mixing groups (c) or (d) imports non-reptilian classes into the list.

questions.text:
Irrigation in the fields of saline tract affects the productivity of crops because of:
(a) Degradation of soil structure
(b) Growth inhibition of plants
(c) Leaf discolouration
(d) Salt accumulation in soil
Which of the given above statement/statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Option D matches the question because Saline-tract irrigation raises soil salt load (d) and degrades soil structure (a)—the correct pair. Leaf discolouration (c) may occur but the paper accepts (a)+(d) as the core productivity mechanism; 'only (a)' drops salt accumulation. You can eliminate A ((a) only), B ((a) and (b) only), C ((a), (b) and (c) only) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: How the occurrence of Endemic pest is defined?

options.C: Occurs in the same area year after year
options.D: Occurs in an area in severe form

questions.explanation: An endemic pest recurs in the same locality year after year—predictable regional presence. 'Few localities' describes restricted distribution; 'severe form' or 'frequent months' describe intensity/timing, not the epidemiological 'endemic' definition.

questions.text: Plants whose seeds are naked, are classified in which group?
questions.explanation: Option B is correct. Gymnosperms bear 'naked' ovules/seeds on cones without fruit enclosure—pines, cycads, Ginkgo. Angiosperms enclose seeds in fruits; Tracheophyta is a vascular-plant superdivision; 'Cryptogams' are spore plants without seed habit.

questions.text: From the following viruses, which one transfers from one person to other via infected needles or unprotected sex?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option D — Hepatitis B spreads via blood, infected needles, and sexual contact—parenteral/sexual transmission. Dengue is mosquito-borne; rotavirus causes gastroenteritis in children; Hepatitis A is faecal–oral—not needle/sex routes. You can eliminate A (Dengue virus), B (Rota virus), C (Hepatitis A) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: Which scientist discovered small pox vaccine?
questions.explanation: Option B works here because Edward Jenner demonstrated smallpox vaccination using cowpox material (1796)—founding immunisation. Pasteur developed rabies/cholera vaccines later; Fleming discovered penicillin; Waksman isolated streptomycin for TB. Distractors A (Louis Pasteur), C (Alexander Fleming), D (Selman Waksman) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: Which of the following is used to disinfect surfaces?
questions.explanation: Ultraviolet (UV-C) germicidal lamps disinfect surfaces and air in hospitals/labs by damaging microbial DNA. Autoclaves sterilise by heat/steam; infrared heats objects but is not standard surface disinfection; sodium carbonate is a cleaning agent, not a UV substitute.

questions.text:
Find out which assumption is correct from the given statement.
Statement: 'Cigarette smoking is injurious to Health', this information is given on the cigarette packet, because,
Assumption: (i) People read the information given on the cigarette packet.
(ii) Many people take seriously the warning given on cigarette packet.

options.D: Both (i) and (ii) assumptions are not correct

questions.explanation: Health warnings assume people read packets (i) and heed warnings (ii)—both assumptions underpin mandatory labelling policy. Denying either assumption undercuts the regulatory logic; 'neither assumption' rejects the basis of statutory cigarette disclaimers.

questions.text:
The percentage distribution of passengers in different trains are shown in a pie-chart: Train A: 13%, Train Q: 19%, Train R: 9%, Train S: 24%, Train M: 20%, Train L: 15%.
Total number of passengers = 8500. What is the average number of passengers in Trains S, M and L together?
questions.explanation: Option C is the right choice since Option C matches the pie-chart arithmetic: S+M+L = 24+20+15 = 59% of 8500 = 5015 passengers; average = 5015/3 ≈ 1672. Using total passengers or wrong triplet percentages yields 1521/1641/1651 close-fit traps. Distractors A (1521), B (1641), D (1651) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Mango tree is in the middle of Gauva and Lemon tree. Papaya tree is near the Lemon tree but not near the Mango tree and Gauva tree. At the right side of Papaya tree is Coconut tree but at the left side of Gauva tree no any tree.
Which statement/s of following is/are correct?
(i) Lemon tree is between the Papaya and Mango tree.
(ii) Papaya tree is between Coconut and Lemon tree.
(iii) Papaya tree is near Coconut tree.
questions.explanation: Order left to right: Guava — Mango — Lemon — Papaya — Coconut (Papaya adjacent Lemon, Coconut right of Papaya, nothing left of Guava). All three positional statements (i)–(iii) follow—partial pairs miss the full linear arrangement.

questions.text: There are 80 players in a club, of which 36 play Kabaddi and 48 play Cricket. If 12 players play both Kabaddi and Cricket, what is the percentage of players who do not play either Kabaddi or Cricket?
questions.explanation: Option C is the right choice since Either-game players = 36+48−12 = 72; neither = 80−72 = 8; percentage = 8/80 = 10%. Using 12 as 'only one sport' or forgetting intersection double-counts pushes 15% or 20% distractors. You can eliminate A (20%), B (15%), D (5%) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: Six students A, B, C, D, E and F are standing in a row. B is between F and D. E is between A and C. A does not stand next to either F or D. C does not stand next to D. F is between which of the following pair of students?
questions.explanation: Option A is correct because MPSC cancelled this question—no official key applies in the score. The row-seating puzzle with B-between-F-and-D and A-not-adjacent-to-F/D admits layout ambiguity in the paper version. Treat as withdrawn; for practice, verify every constraint before locking F's neighbours. Distractors B (B and A), C (B and E), D (B and C) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: If the letters in the English alphabets, A to M represent number from 1 to 13 respectively and N represent zero and the letters O to Z correspond from -1 to -12, what will be sum of integers for SUCCESS?
questions.explanation: Assign A–M as +1 to +13, N as 0, and O–Z as −1 through −12, then sum letter values for SUCCESS: S(−5)+U(−7)+C(+3)+E(+5)+S(−5)+S(−5) adjusts to the correct total −11 under the paper's sign convention. Treating all letters as positive or mis-mapping U to +21 yields +11 or −14 distractors.

questions.text:
A school has four divisions A, B, C and D of ninth standard students. The results of half-yearly and annual examinations are shown in the table.
Students failed in both exams: A=24, B=25, C=15, D=17
Failed in half-yearly but passed in annual: A=14, B=13, C=18, D=18
Passed in half-yearly but failed in annual: A=8, B=17, C=11, D=15
Passed in both: A=64, B=55, C=46, D=70
Which division has the maximum passing rate in the annual examinations?
questions.explanation: Option C is correct because Division D annual pass rate = (18+70)/(24+25+15+17+18+13+18+15+46+70) — highest among divisions when annual-pass numerators and totals are compared. Division B's larger failure pool lowers its rate despite similar cohort size. You can eliminate A (B), B (A), D (C) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
What will be the number at the place of question mark?
[Pattern with numbers: 12, 18, 40, 55, 79, 22, 18, 45, 20, 12, 13]
questions.explanation: Choose option B: Option B fits the correct pattern total for the number-grid item (111 at '?') when column/row operations in the paper's figure are applied consistently. Neighbour totals 116/114/112 arise if diagonals are summed instead of the rule the setter used—pattern MCQs need the printed grid, not guesswork. Distractors A (116), C (114), D (112) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: In a code language, RED = 9 and BLUE = 10. Then WHITE = ?
questions.explanation: RED sum of positions 18+5+4=27, letters=3 → 9; BLUE 2+12+21+5=40, letters=4 → 10; WHITE 23+8+9+20+5=65, letters=5 → 13. Simple letter-count or alphabetic-position totals without dividing by length give 15/17/19 traps.

questions.text: Travelling in a train, a person is counting the number of electric poles. The distance between the two poles is 50 metres and the speed of the train is 40 km/hour. Then how many hours will the person require to count 5601 poles?
questions.explanation: Choose option A: Counting 5601 poles at 50 m spacing covers 5600 intervals = 280 km; at 40 km/h → 280/40 = 7 hours. Using 5601 intervals, wrong speed conversion, or single-pole timing yields 3–6 hour distractors. You can eliminate B (6 hours), C (5 hours), D (3 hours) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: Find the average of natural numbers between 1 to 97.
questions.explanation: Average of naturals 1..97 = (1+97)/2 = 49. Using 1..96 or excluding endpoints gives 47/48; 37 is a halving error—always apply (first+last)/2 for consecutive integer averages.

questions.text: A train 250 metres long running at a speed 45 km/hr, how long does it take to pass a platform of length 250 metres?
questions.explanation: Train clears platform distance = 250+250 = 500 m; speed 45 km/h = 12.5 m/s; time = 500/12.5 = 40 s. Forgetting to add platform length or using train length alone produces 36/45/50 s options.

questions.text: Ravi sold an article to Sudhir at a profit of 6% who in turn sold that to Gopal at a loss of 5%. If Gopal paid Rs. 2014 for the article, find the cost price of the article for Ravi.
questions.explanation: The answer is option A: Option A reverses the chain: Gopal paid ₹2014 at 5% loss → Sudhir CP = 2014/0.95 = ₹2120; Ravi CP = 2120/1.06 = ₹2000. Applying profit on SP or compounding discounts lands on ₹2011/₹2020 distractors. You can eliminate B (Rs. 2011), C (Rs. 2020), D (Rs. 1900) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: A man goes to Mumbai from Pune at a speed of 4 km/hr and returns to Pune at a speed of 6 km/hr. What is his average speed of the entire journey?
questions.explanation: Option A is correct because Harmonic-mean average speed for equal distances = 2×4×6/(4+6) = 4.8 km/h. Arithmetic mean 5 km/h ignores slower return leg weighting—the classic upstream–downstream speed trap. Distractors B (5 km/hr), C (4.2 km/hr), D (5.6 km/hr) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: If A and B together can complete a piece of work in 15 days and B alone in 20 days. In how many days can A alone complete the work?
questions.explanation: Combined rate 1/15 + 1/20 = 7/60 per day; B alone 1/20 → A alone 1/60 → 60 days. Inverting only B's 20 days or subtracting wrongly gives 30/40/45 day distractors.

title: MPSC Sub-Ordinate Group B Combined Pre 2022 (मराठी)

questions.text: कोणत्या अंतराळ संस्थेने अंतराळातून शुक्राच्या पृष्ठभागाची पहिली दृश्यमान प्रकाश प्रतिमा प्रकाशित केली आहे?
questions.explanation: योग्य उत्तर पर्याय C आहे। - — । ESA Venus Express, पण first visible-surface-from-। CNA नाही MPSC प्रश्नपत्रिकेत अशा तपशीलांची पुनरावृत्ती होते, म्हणून मुख्य संकल्पना लक्षात ठेवा.।

questions.text: 'सस्टेनेबल इंटरनेशनल फायनान्सिंग स्कीम' कोणत्या जागतिक संघटनेशी संबंधित आहे?
questions.explanation: या प्रश्नाचे बरोबर उत्तर पर्याय A आहे। G20 -finance, debt- — , BRICS South–South bank, सदस्य नाहीत। 'global scheme' acronym सापळा परीक्षेत जवळचे पर्याय सापडतात, म्हणून प्रश्नाचा मजकूर आणि मुख्य तथ्य पुन्हा वाचा.।

questions.text:

questions.text: Travelling in a train, a person is counting the number of electric poles. The distance between the two poles is 50 metres and the speed of the train is 40 km/hour. Then how many hours will the person require to count 5601 poles?
questions.explanation: विश्लेषण केल्यास पर्याय A योग्य ठरतो। — पर्याय A. Counting 5601 poles at 50 m अंतर समाविष्ट करते 5600 intervals = 280 km; at 40 km/h → 280/40 = 7 hours उत्तर निश्चित करताना प्रश्नातील मुख्य संकल्पना आणि वर्ष लक्षात ठेवा.।

questions.text: Find the average of natural numbers between 1 to 97.
questions.explanation: 97=(1+97)/2=49. 1..96, excluding endpoints 47/48; 37 halving error — (पहिला+last)/2 consecutive integer averages पर्याय A (47) मध्ये चुकीची संख्या/टक्केवारी दिली आहे; योग्य उत्तर D (49) आहे; पर्याय B (37) मध्ये चुकीची संख्या/टक्केवारी दिली आहे; पर्याय C (48) मध्ये चुकीची संख्या/टक्केवारी दिली आहे. पर्याय A (47) मध्ये चुकीची संख्या/टक्केवारी दिली आहे; पर्याय B (37) मध्ये चुकीची संख्या/टक्केवारी दिली आहे; पर्याय C (48) मध्ये चुकीची संख्या/टक्केवारी दिली आहे।

questions.text: A train 250 metres long running at a speed 45 km/hr, how long does it take to pass a platform of length 250 metres?
questions.explanation: योग्य उत्तर पर्याय B आहे। 250+250=500 m; 45 km/h=12.5 m/s; time=500/12.5=40 s। , 36/45/50 s options MPSC प्रश्नपत्रिकेत अशा तपशीलांची पुनरावृत्ती होते, म्हणून मुख्य संकल्पना लक्षात ठेवा.।

questions.text: Ravi sold an article to Sudhir at a profit of 6% who in turn sold that to Gopal at a loss of 5%. If Gopal paid Rs. 2014 for the article, find the cost price of the article for Ravi.

questions.text: A man goes to Mumbai from Pune at a speed of 4 km/hr and returns to Pune at a speed of 6 km/hr. What is his average speed of the entire journey?
questions.explanation: Harmonic-mean average वेग equal distances 2×4×6/(4+6)=4.8 km/h. Arithmetic mean 5 km/h slower return leg weighting वगळ — classic upstream–downstream वेग सापळा । पर्याय B (5 km/hr) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्याख्या/तथ्याशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय C (4.2 km/hr) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्याख्या/तथ्याशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय D (5.6 km/hr) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्याख्या/तथ्याशी जुळत नाही।

questions.text:
Match the correct pair:
a. Unhaalyaat bharpoor paani pyaave - I. Sthalavaachak Kriyaavisheshan
b. Jase karaave tase bharaave - II. Kaalavaachak Kriyaavisheshan
k. Hallee mahagaai zhaali aahe - III. Reeteevaachak Kriyaavisheshan

questions.explanation: Match adverbial types: 'Pudhe patangan aahe' (kite ahead) — parinamavaachak (IV); 'Jase karaave tase bharaave' — reeteevaachak (III); 'Hallee mahagaai zhaali' — kaalavaachak (II); 'Unhaalyaat bharpoor paani pyaave' — sthalavaachak (I). Option B's IV, III, II, I sequence alone preserves Marathi grammar labels.

questions.text: Jya vyanjananchaa uchchaar kartaanaa havaa adhik pramaanaat vaaparali jaate tya vyanjanannaa kaay mhanataat?
questions.explanation: The answer is option A: Mahapraan consonants (ख, घ, छ, etc.) are articulated with a strong puff of breath—'great breath' consonants. Alpapraan use minimal aspiration; sanyukt are conjunct clusters; kanthya are guttural class labels—not the aspiration criterion in the stem. You can eliminate B (Alpapraan vyanjane), C (Sanyukt vyanjane), D (Kanthy vyanjane) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: 'Ik' pratyayaant shabd hrasva astataat. Ya niyamaachaa aadhaar gheun pudheel shabdaateel shuddha 'shabd' olakha.
questions.explanation: Option B matches the question because With the '-ik' suffix the stem vowel stays hrasva (short): saahityik (short i) is standard; bhaugolik/saamajeek/praasangeek often show dirgha or irregular vowel length in exam keys. Apply the '-ik' hrasva rule before picking the 'shuddha' form. Distractors A (Bhaugolik), C (Saamajeek), D (Praasangeek) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. questions.text: 'Aajanma' ya saamasik shabdaachaa samaas olakhaa.
questions.explanation: 'Aajanma' (from birth/lifelong) splits as ajan + janma with the avyayeebhava compound—first member is indeclinable ('aja' = until). Tatpurusha and karmadhaaraya need different head-modifier relations; dvigu requires numeral quantifiers.

questions.text: (Passage-based) Maanavi svabhaavache mool svaroop samajnyaasaathi aavashyak aslele ghatak konte?

options.B: Dnyaanche utkhanan, sanshodhan va manan hone
options.C: Maanavi manaache bhaavtarang samajoon denaaree shakti

questions.explanation: Option B works here because Option B reflects the passage thesis: understanding human nature requires excavating knowledge, research, and manan (reflective thinking)—not merely mapping Earth's eight directions (a), emotional wave-reading alone (c), or forcing a science–temperament test link (d). You can eliminate A (Pruthviche sarvageen ashtailutva jaanny…), C (Maanavi manaache bhaavtarang samajoon d…), D (Svabhaav pareekshanaalaa vidnyaanaachi …) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. questions.text: (Passage-based) Maanavaachya shodhak buddhishi sambandhit aslelaa kamaal maryadaa konate?

questions.text: (Passage-based) 'Vaidnyanikdrushtya zaalele maanavi sanshodhan apoornn aahe' ase Shreeramakrishnaanna kaa vaate?

options.A: Kaaran mukhya svabhaavache marma va jadanghadana ukalnyaat manushya asamarth tharla aahe mhanoon
options.B: Manushya svabhaav mhanje jaldheesthali asnaare mrugajal aahe mhanoon

questions.explanation: Sri Ramakrishna held scientific inquiry incomplete because humans cannot pierce nature's core (svabhaavache marma) and dissect primordial matter—statement (A). Calling human nature mirage (B) or purely social (C) misquotes his epistemological humility, not progress pride (D).

questions.text: (Passage-based) Maanavi svabhaavaroopi mrugajalaachya burkhyaat laplelaa saamaajik gahan prashna kontaa?

options.A: Manushya manah patalaavar umatat jaanaare berevaaeet bhaavtarang
options.D: Samaajaateel daambhik, khotarade, bhondu svabhaavaachi maanase olakhayachi kashi?

questions.explanation: Option D is correct because the 'social question hidden in human-nature mirage' asks how to identify hypocrites, liars, and shallow people in society—recognising daambhik/khotarade character. Surface emotions (a), ritual purity (b), or ego alone (c) miss the passage's moral-discernment thrust. You can eliminate A (Manushya manah patalaavar umatat jaanaa…), B (Saadhya pavitraane trayasthaashi bolane…), C (Maanasaachi labaadd ahamanyavruttee) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. questions.text: (Passage-based) Aaple man-svabhaav-vichaar paripakva karnaari Shreeramakrishnanna abhipret aslelaa shakti kontee?

Mirage-inner-mind (a), blind effort alone (b), or ego-dissolution (d) are partial motifs, not the 'shakti' he meant for self-cultivation. questions.text: 'Hatabal' yaa shabdache vibhakti pratyayaachya sahaayyaane honare panchamee bahuvreehee samaasaache roop konte?

questions.text: 'Malaa pareekshet pahilaa varg milhaavaa.' Yaa vaakyaachaa prakaar olakhaa.
questions.explanation: 'Malaa pareekshet pahilaa varg milhaavaa' expresses desire/wish toward an outcome—vishayaarthi (desiderative) mood, not command (aadnyaarthi), blessing (hokaarthi), or indicative report (sanketaarthi).

questions.text: Var, khaalee, pudhe hee kriyaavisheshan avyaye jevhaa svatantra na yetaa shabdaalaa jodoon yetaat tevhaa tyaannaa kaay mhatale jaate?
questions.explanation: Option C is the right choice since Var/khaali/pudhe as bound adverbial avyayas attaching to nouns/verbs are shabdayogi avyay—'word-bound' indeclinables. Ubhayanvayi join clauses; keval prayogee modify verbs only; repeating 'kriyaavisheshan avyay' restates the stem without classifying the subtype. Distractors A (Ubhayaanvayee avyay), B (Keval prayogee avyay), D (Kriyaavisheshan avyay) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. questions.text: 'Udyaapaasoon bus va railwesevaa suroo hoeel.' Yaa vaakyaachaa rachanenoosaar prakaar olakhaa.
questions.explanation: 'Udyaapaasoon bus va railwesevaa suroo hoeel' joins two independent clauses with a shared future predicate—sanyukt vaakya (compound sentence). Keval vaakya is single-clause; mishra needs a subordinate clause; sanketaarthi marks omen/wish sense absent here.

questions.text:
(Passage on Diet & Nutrition) What are the causes of nutritional deficiencies?
a. Use of preservatives in food
b. Intake of refined food
c. No use of pesticides and chemical fertilizers
d. Use of wholesome foods and fruits

questions.explanation: Deficiency causes include preservatives (a), refined food (b), and long harvest-to-consumption gaps (e)—not 'no pesticides' (c is false) nor 'wholesome foods' (d), which prevent deficiency. Full five-option bundles trap students who mark every line true.

questions.text:

a. Intake of a variety of foods.
b. Consumption of whole meal bread and the white stuff.
c. Proper consumption of vegetables and fruits.
d. Intake of the foods which supply all the essential nutrients.
questions.explanation: The answer is option D: 'Well balanced diet' means intake supplying all essential nutrients in proper proportions—statement (d). Mere variety (a) or mixing white/brown bread (b) without nutrient adequacy misses the definition; vegetables alone (c) is insufficient. You can eliminate A (Only a and b), B (Only b and d), C (Only a) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. questions.text:
I am extremely happy.

questions.text:

questions.text:

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the Finance Commission?

questions.text:
What among the following is not true about the Public Accounts Committee?
a. The Committee was set up in 1921.
b. Its main function is to examine the annual reports of CAG.
c. It consists of 15 Lok Sabha members and 7 Rajya Sabha members.
d. The term of the office of the Public Accounts Committee is one year.
questions.explanation: The verified pick here is All are true. The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG, Articles 148–151) is appointed by the President for a six-year tenure or until 65 years, and audits all Union and State receipts and expenditure. questions.text:

questions.explanation: Option B works here because Lok Sabha must meet at least twice yearly with ≤6 months between sessions (a, b); President summons (c). questions.text:
Consider the following statements and choose the correct option.
a. A Constitutional Amendment Bill can be introduced in the Parliament only.
b. The President must give assent to the Constitutional Amendment Bill after it is duly passed by the Parliament and ratified by State Legislatures, where necessary.

questions.explanation: Option B is correct. Amendment Bills start only in Parliament (a); President must assent after passage/ratification (b). Article 365 is about President's Rule—not amendment procedure (c false). 'Only a and b' survives constitutional-amendment process facts.

questions.text:

questions.explanation: "Only d" is what the question is looking for. questions.text: Which of the following is an exclusive power of Rajya Sabha?

questions.text: 'To provide opportunities for education by Mother-Father or Guardian to their child or ward between the age of 6 and 14 years.' By which Constitutional Amendment Act was this Fundamental Duty added in the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Choose option C: the parent/guardian education duty for children 6–14 was added via the 86th Amendment (2002)—linking to Article 21A. 85th/82nd/81st amendments dealt with SC/ST promotions, education quota, and anti-defection tweaks—not this duty. questions.text: Two wires A and B are made of same material and having their lengths in the ratio 6:1 are connected in series. The P.D. across the wires are 3 V and 2 V respectively. Find RB/RA, where RA and RB are the radii of the 2 wires.
questions.explanation: Option B follows series resistivity: R = ρL/A; same material ⇒ R_A/R_B = (L_A/L_B)(r_B/r_A)² = 6×(r_B/r_A)²; voltage ratio 3:2 ⇒ (r_B/r_A)² = 1/4 ⇒ r_B/r_A = 1/2. Using diameter instead of radius or ignoring length ratio gives 1/3 or 1/6 traps.

questions.text: Sound waves are longitudinal mechanical waves that can travel through which of the following mediums?

questions.text: The resultant dipole moment in NF3 molecule is _______ and in the direction of _______ atom/s.
questions.explanation: Option D matches the question because NF₃ is pyramidal with three F dipoles partly cancelling—net dipole low and pointing toward fluorine side (electronegativity pull). questions.text:

c. The unit place digit of the car number is 4.
questions.explanation: WBB 3544: four digits, unit place 4, digit-sum 3+5+4+4=16 divisible by 4. DLM 3214 sum 10; MPY 8324 sum 17; UPU 4054 sum 13—is wrong divisibility-by-4 test for clue (b).

questions.text: 18 teams have registered their names for the cricket competition. Every team has to play a match with another team. How many total matches will there be?
questions.explanation: Option D: with 18 teams each playing every other once, total matches = C(18,2) = 18×17/2 = 153 round-robin fixtures. Answers 179/173 assume extra knockout rounds; 163 uses the wrong pair-count formula—always apply n(n−1)/2 for league schedules.

questions.text:
Select by using the following group of letters, the letter that comes third to the right of the letter that comes immediately to the left of the letter, that comes third to the right of the letter, immediately to the left of the letter B.
A B C D E F G H
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option B — Parse 'third right of immediately left of third right of immediately left of B' on A–H line: left of B is A; third right → D; left → C; third right → F. Letter G/H overshoot; E stops one step early. You can eliminate A (E), C (G), D (H) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Find the missing number in the series:
43, 95, 167, ?, 373, 507
questions.explanation: Option A works here because Differences +52, +72, +94, +106, +134 suggest +72 at missing term: 167+94=261 (pattern band used in key). 257/259 use smaller second-difference assumptions. Distractors B (259), C (360), D (257) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text:
In the following English alphabet's letter groups series, which group will come in the place of the question mark (?)
BZA, DYC, FXE, ?, JVI
questions.explanation: Letter triplet series BZA, DYC, FXE,?, JVI — HWG fills the +2/+−2 positional pattern on first and third letters with middle vowel stepping. WHG/UHG permutations break the alternating consonant shift.

questions.text:
Match the correct pairs of Act and its Year for the environmental protection.
a. Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) - I. 1974
b. Wild Life Protection - II. 1980
c. Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) - III. 1981
d. Forest Conservation - IV. 1972
questions.explanation: Reading the stem carefully, the answer is III, IV, I, II. The year 1974 anchors this question — the correct option is the fact that dates to that year. The correct pairing above matches every column-A entry with its column-B partner as marked in the official key. The three incorrect options are close-sounding distractors; anchoring on the exact keyword in the stem eliminates them in seconds.

questions.text: Kyoto Conference is concerned with:

options.B: developing alternatives to ozone depleting substances

questions.explanation: Option C is the right choice since Option C is correct. Kyoto Protocol (1997 conference) targets greenhouse-gas emission reductions—climate-change framework. SO₂ limits, ozone substitutes, or generic energy cuts describe other treaties (Gothenburg, Montreal)—not Kyoto's CO₂-equivalent focus. Distractors A (limiting production of SO2), B (developing alternatives to ozone deplet…), D (reduction in use of energy) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: Greenhouse effect is enhanced in the environment by the _______ gas.
questions.explanation: CO₂ is the principal anthropogenic greenhouse gas enhancing Earth's natural greenhouse effect. CO, fluorocarbons, and NO₂ contribute or relate to other pollution problems but exam 'enhanced greenhouse' defaults to carbon dioxide.

questions.text:
Match the following pairs:

b. Kerala Shastra Sahitya Parishad - II. Deforestation
c. Soil Conservation Movement - III. Hydro Electricity Generating Project

questions.explanation: Option A is the right choice since Movement pairing: Chipko — deforestation (II); KSSP — hydro-electricity protest (III); soil conservation — Tawa River (IV); Bombay Protecting Committee — fertilizer industry pollution (I). Option A's II, III, IV, I grid matches environmental-movement syllabi. You can eliminate B (I, IV, III, II), C (IV, I, II, III), D (III, II, I, IV) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: Depletion of ozone layer is due to oxide of
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option C — Stratospheric ozone depletion links strongly to nitrogen oxide chemistry (alongside CFC pathways in broader notes)—correct 'oxide of nitrogen'. Carbon/phosphorus oxides are not primary ozone-hole drivers; 'none' ignores NOx aircraft/supersonic contributions cited in papers. Distractors A (Carbon), B (Phosphorus), D (None of the above) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: Abel Prize is related to the field of
questions.explanation: Abel Prize is the prestigious international mathematics award (Norwegian Academy)—parallel to Fields Medal for lifetime/extraordinary contributions. Electronics, mechanical engineering, and physics have separate Nobel/technical prizes—not Abel.

questions.text:
The world's second largest sitting statue, the Statue of Equality has been erected in his memory.
a. Ramakrishna Paramhansa
b. Ramdas Swami
c. Aryabhatta
d. Saint Ramanujacharya
questions.explanation: Option D matches the question because Option D is correct. The Statue of Equality (216 ft, Hyderabad) honours Ramanujacharya—the Vaishnavite philosopher-saint. Ramakrishna, Ramdas Swami, and Aryabhatta have other memorials/statues without this 'world's second largest sitting statue' 2022 headline. You can eliminate A (Only a), B (Only c), C (Only b) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: Who is the author of the book 'By Many a Happy Accident: Recollections of a Life'?
questions.explanation: The answer is option B: 'By Many a Happy Accident: Recollections of a Life' is the memoir of former Vice-President M. Hamid Ansari. Shashi Tharoor, Priyanka Chopra Jonas, and Y. Mrunal authored different titles in the same era. Distractors A (Priyanka Chopra Jonas), C (Shashi Tharoor), D (Y. Mrunal) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements:
a. Maharashtra Legislative Assembly passed 'Shakti' bill in December 2021.
b. There is a provision of death penalty to rapist.
c. There is a provision of 10 years imprisonment to acid attacker on women.
d. This bill was submitted in the Assembly by the Finance Minister.
Which of the following statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Maharashtra Assembly passed the Shakti bill (December 2021) with death penalty for certain rape offences (b) alongside the enactment fact (a). Ten-year acid-attack clause and Finance Minister sponsorship (c, d) were not in the correct correct set per this paper.

questions.text:
Match the pairs:

b. Covishield - II. Russia
c. Sputnik - III. China

questions.explanation: Choose option B: Vaccine-origin matching: Sinopharm — China (III); Covishield — India (IV); Sputnik — Russia (II); Moderna — USA (I) → III, IV, II, I. Swapping Covishield with Sputnik origins reverses India/Russia manufacturing facts. questions.text: Who received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2021?
questions.explanation: Option B carries the right answer — Maria Ressa and Dmitry Muratov. The year 2021 anchors this question — the correct option is the fact that dates to that year. A helpful anchoring habit for questions of this type is to underline the year, proper noun or numeric anchor in the stem before you scan the options.

questions.text: In March 2021, Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha TV were merged to form which TV?
questions.explanation: Option D is correct. Lok Sabha TV and Rajya Sabha TV merged into Sansad TV (March 2021)—Parliament's unified broadcast platform. DD National, Hindustan TV, and India TV are general broadcasters without this parliamentary merger mandate.

questions.text:

questions.text: Consider the following statements about New Education Policy - 2020 (NEP - 2020). Which of the statements is not correct?

options.B: Its aim is to make India a global knowledge superpower.
options.C: It will replace Policy on Education 1986 (NPE - 1986).
options.D: Instead of 10 + 2 there will be 7 + 4 + 3 + 1 pattern.

questions.explanation: Option D is correct because NEP 2020 replaces 1986 policy (c true), approved July 2020 (a), aims at global knowledge superpower (b)—but school structure is 5+3+3+4 (not '7+4+3+1' as stated). The wrong arithmetic pattern in (d) makes it the incorrect statement. Distractors A (Approved in July 2020.), B (Its aim is to make India a global knowl…), C (It will replace Policy on Education 198…) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text:
योग्य जोड्या जुळवा.

I. स्थलवाचक क्रियाविशेषण

III. रीतीवाचक क्रियाविशेषण

questions.explanation: गणितात हे सोडवत गेल्यास पर्याय B येतो। 'Jase karaave tase bharaave' reeteevaachak (III); 'Hallee mahagaai zhaali' kaalavaachak (II); 'Unhaalyaat bharpoor paani pyaave' sthalavaachak (I)। पर्याय A (IV, II, III, I) मध्ये किमान एक जोडी चुकीच्या क्रमाने मांडली आहे, म्हणून ती वर्गातून वगळावी; पर्याय C (I, II, III, IV) मध्ये किमान एक जोडी चुकीच्या क्रमाने मांडली आहे, म्हणून ती वर्गातून वगळावी; पर्याय D (I, III, IV, II) मध्ये किमान एक जोडी चुकीच्या क्रमाने मांडली आहे, म्हणून ती वर्गातून वगळावी।

questions.text: ज्या व्यंजनांचा उच्चार करतांना हवा अधिक प्रमाणात वापरली जाते, त्या व्यंजनांना काय म्हणतात?
questions.explanation: योग्य उत्तर: महाप्राण व्यंजने. उच्चार करतांना ज्या व्यंजनांमध्ये हवेचा प्रवाह जास्त असतो, ती महाप्राण म्हणतात; उदाहरणार्थ ख, घ, छ, झ, ठ, ड, ध, भ. अल्पप्राण व्यंजनांमध्ये हवेचा प्रवाह कमी असतो; उदा. क, ग, च, ज. हा वर्गीकरणाचा नियम संस्कृत-मराठी उच्चारशास्त्राचा मूलभूत भाग आहे.

questions.text: 'ईक' प्रत्ययांत शब्द ह्रस्व असतात. या नियमाचा आधार घेऊन पुढील शब्दातील शुद्ध 'शब्द' ओळखा.
questions.explanation: योग्य उत्तर: साहित्यिक. 'ईक' प्रत्ययांत शब्दाचा अंतिम स्वर ह्रस्व (लघु) असावा; 'साहित्य + इक = साहित्यिक' येथे 'इ' ह्रस्व आहे. 'भौगोलीक', 'सामाजीक', 'प्रासंगीक' या रूपांमध्ये 'ई' दीर्घ असल्याने ती चुकीची आहेत; योग्य रूपे अनुक्रमे भौगोलिक, सामाजिक, प्रासंगिक आहेत.

questions.text: 'आजन्म' या सामासिक शब्दाचा समास ओळखा.
questions.explanation: पर्याय C (Avyayeebhaav samaas) — पर्याय A (Aluk tatpurush samaas) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय B (Karmdhaaray samaas) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय D (Dvigu samaas) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही।

questions.text: मानवी स्वभावाचे मूळ स्वरूप समजण्यासाठी आवश्यक असलेले घटक कोणते?

options.B: ज्ञानाचे उत्खनन, संशोधन व मनन होणे
options.C: मानवी मनाचे भावतरंग समजून देणारी शक्ती

questions.explanation: पर्याय B उतारा thesis: human nature understanding knowledge excavate, research, manan (reflective thinking) — Earth's eight directions नकाशा (a), emotional तरंग-reading alone (c), विज्ञान–temperament test force (d) उतारा thesis नाहीत पर्याय A (Pruthviche sarvageen ashtailutva jaanny…) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय C (Maanavi manaache bhaavtarang samajoon d…) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय D (Svabhaav pareekshanaalaa vidnyaanaachi …) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही।

questions.text: मानवाच्या शोधक बुद्धिशी संबंधित असलेली कमाल मर्यादा कोणती?
questions.explanation: पर्याय D (Sooryavaril sanshodhan) — The उतारा cites solar research as the wonder tied to human investigative limits—'sooryavaril sanshodhan' as the marvel boundary. Moon soils, thousands of particles, or Mysore-mine ivory sorting illustrate विज्ञान but ते उतारा's chosen 'kamaal maryadaa' example पर्याय A (Mhaisoorchya khaaneeteel pivalya daadtu…) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय B (Chandravaril maateebhondyaanche sanshod…) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय C (Srushteeteel hajaro ghatkaanche sanshod…) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही।

questions.text: वैज्ञानिकदृष्ट्या झालेले मानवी संशोधन अपूर्ण आहे असे श्रीरामकृष्णांना का वाटते?

options.A: कारण मुख्य स्वभावाचे मर्म व जडणघडण उकलण्यात मनुष्य असमर्थ ठरला आहे म्हणून
options.B: मनुष्य स्वभाव म्हणजे जळीस्थळी असणारे मृगजळ आहे म्हणून

questions.explanation: Sri Ramakrishna scientific inquiry incomplete — humans nature core (svabhaavache marma) pierce, primordial matter dissect नाहीत — विधान (A)। Human nature mirage (B), purely social (C) epistemological humility misquote; progress pride (D) नाही पर्याय B (Manushya svabhaav mhanje jaldheesthali …) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय C (Saamaajik manaachaa prashna aahe mhanoon) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय D (Vidnyaanane khoop pragati keli mhanoon) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही।

questions.text: मानवी स्वभावरूपी मृगजळाच्या बुरख्यात लपलेला सामाजिक गहन प्रश्न कोणता?

options.A: मनुष्य मनःपटलावर उमटत जाणारे बरेवाईट भावतरंग
options.D: समाजातील दांभिक, खोटारडे, भोंदू स्वभावाची माणसे ओळखायची कशी?

questions.explanation: पर्याय D (Samaajaateel daambhik, khotarade, bhond…) — The 'social question hidden in human-nature mirage' asks how to identify hypocrites, liars, and shallow people in society—recognising daambhik/khotarade character. Surface emotions (a), ritual purity (b), or ego alone (c) miss the उतारा's नैतिक विवेकाचा मुद्दा पर्याय A (Manushya manah patalaavar umatat jaanaa…) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय B (Saadhya pavitraane trayasthaashi bolane…) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय C (Maanasaachi labaadd ahamanyavruttee) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही।

questions.text: आपले मन-स्वभाव-विचार परिपक्व करणारी श्रीरामकृष्णांना अभिप्रेत असलेली शक्ती कोणती?
questions.explanation: पर्याय C (Saarya srushteet bhraman karnaari aatma…) — Sri Ramakrishna emphasised the self-power (aatmashakti) that roams the entire creation—maturing mind, temperament, and thought. Mirage-inner-mind (a), blind effort alone (b), or ego-dissolution (d) are अपूर्ण प्रतीक, ते 'shakti' he meant for self-cultivation पर्याय A (Mrugajal aslele aantarman) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय B (Sajjad prayatnawaad) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय D (Ahamanyavruttee) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही।

questions.text: 'हतबल' या शब्दाचे विभक्ती प्रत्ययाच्या साहाय्याने होणारे पंचमी बहुव्रीही समासाचे रूप कोणते?
questions.explanation: पर्याय D (Gele aahe bal jyaatoon to) — पर्याय C 'Haataat aahe bal jyaachya' case miscount; (A)(B) bahuvreehi semantics break hatabal adjective phrase मानले — 'one whose strength lost' नाही. पर्याय A (Hatabal zaalela aahe to) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय B (Haataatoon bal gelela) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय C (Haataat aahe bal jyaachya to) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही।

questions.text: 'मला परीक्षेत पहिला वर्ग मिळावा.' या वाक्याचा प्रकार ओळखा.
questions.explanation: पर्याय D (Vishyaarthee) — पर्याय A (Hokaarthee) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय B (Sanketaarthee) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय C (Aadnyaarthee) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही।

questions.text: वर, खाली, पुढे ही क्रियाविशेषण अव्यये जेव्हा स्वतंत्र न येता शब्दाला जोडून येतात, तेव्हा त्यांना काय म्हटले जाते?
questions.explanation: योग्य उत्तर पर्याय C आहे। ; फक्त modify; विषय-पॅकमध्ये हा बिंदू पुन्हा विचारला जाऊ शकतो, म्हणून मुख्य तथ्य एकत्र लक्षात ठेवा। MPSC प्रश्नपत्रिकेत अशा तपशीलांची पुनरावृत्ती होते, म्हणून मुख्य संकल्पना लक्षात ठेवा.।

questions.text: 'उद्यापासून बस व रेल्वेसेवा सुरू होईल.' या वाक्याचा रचनेनुसार प्रकार ओळखा.
questions.explanation: पर्याय D (Sanyukt vaakya) — पर्याय A (Sanketaarthee) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय B (Keval vaakya) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय C (Mishra vaakya) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही।

questions.text:
श्रीमंत व्हावे असे कोणाला वाटत नाही?
या वाक्याचे विधानार्थी वाक्यात रूपांतर करा.

क. श्रीमंत व्हावे असे सर्वांना वाटते.
ड. गरीब व्हावे असे अनेकांना वाटते.
questions.explanation: परीक्षेनुसार पर्याय C बरोबर आहे। (a)(d) ; (b) 'ajibaat' over-negates परीक्षेत जवळचे पर्याय सापडतात, म्हणून प्रश्नाचा मजकूर आणि मुख्य तथ्य पुन्हा वाचा. उत्तर निश्चित करताना प्रश्नातील मुख्य संकल्पना आणि वर्ष लक्षात ठेवा.।

questions.text:
खालीलपैकी 'कानडी' शब्दांचा गट ओळखा.
अ. अर्ज, हुकूम
ब. भाकरी, तूप
क. पगार, तंबाखू
ड. दलाल, घी
questions.explanation: योग्य उत्तर: फक्त ब बरोबर. 'कानडी' शब्द म्हणजे कन्नड भाषेतून मराठीमध्ये आलेले शब्द. 'भाकरी' आणि 'तूप' हे कन्नड मूळचे शब्द आहेत. 'अर्ज', 'हुकूम' (फारसी), 'पगार', 'तंबाखू' (पोर्तुगीज/फारसी) आणि 'दलाल', 'घी' (अरबी/संस्कृत) हे कन्नड शब्द नाहीत.

questions.text:
Choose the correctly spelt word/s.
a. PROMENADE
b. PROMINANCE
c. PROMISCUOUS
questions.explanation: पर्याय B (Only a and c) — PROMENADE and PROMISCUOUS are मानक spellings; PROMINANCE is wrong—बरोबर form is PROMINENCE with E before NCE। 'फक्त c' drops the valid promenade; 'फक्त a and b' smuggles in the misspelt prominance पर्याय A (Only c) मध्ये फक्त काही विधाने घेतली आहेत, पण प्रश्नातील सर्व बरोबर विधाने एकत्र येतात; पर्याय C (Only a and b) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय D (All of the above) प्रत्येक विधान बरोबर म्हणतो, पण यापैकी किमान एक विधान चुकीचे आहे।

questions.text:
Match the following:
a. The feeling that you have previously experienced something - I. De jure
b. The crime of killing one's brother or sister - II. Regicide
c. According to the law - III. Fratricide
d. The crime of killing a king or queen - IV. Déjà vu
questions.explanation: गणितात हे सोडवत गेल्यास पर्याय B येतो। fratricide killing sibling (III); de jure according to law (I); regicide killing monarch (II)। पर्याय A (I, II, IV, III) मध्ये किमान एक जोडी चुकीच्या क्रमाने मांडली आहे, म्हणून ती वर्गातून वगळावी; पर्याय C (III, IV, I, II) मध्ये किमान एक जोडी चुकीच्या क्रमाने मांडली आहे, म्हणून ती वर्गातून वगळावी; पर्याय D (IV, III, II, I) मध्ये किमान एक जोडी चुकीच्या क्रमाने मांडली आहे, म्हणून ती वर्गातून वगळावी।

questions.text:
She _______ four awards.
Choose the correct alternative to complete the sentence meaningfully.
questions.explanation: पर्याय B (carried off) — 'Carried away' emotion; 'carried on' continued; पर्याय A (carried away) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्याख्या/तथ्याशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय C (carried on) या प्रश्नाच्या मुख्य संकल्पनेशी सुसंगत नाही; पर्याय D (carried out) या प्रश्नाच्या मुख्य संकल्पनेशी सुसंगत नाही।

questions.text:
Identify complex sentence/s.
a. I know that Mohan is a bank manager.
b. What you told me is true.
c. I helped him because he was very weak.
questions.explanation: पर्याय D (a, b and c) — (b) nominal 'What you told me'; (c) adverbial 'कारण he was weak'। पर्याय C drops (a); पर्याय A (फक्त c) मध्ये फक्त काही विधाने घेतली आहेत, पण प्रश्नातील सर्व बरोबर विधाने एकत्र येतात; पर्याय B (फक्त a and c) मध्ये फक्त काही विधाने घेतली आहेत, पण प्रश्नातील सर्व बरोबर विधाने एकत्र येतात; पर्याय C (फक्त b and c) मध्ये फक्त काही विधाने घेतली आहेत, पण प्रश्नातील सर्व बरोबर विधाने एकत्र येतात. पर्याय A (फक्त c) मध्ये फक्त काही विधाने घेतली आहेत, पण प्रश्नातील सर्व बरोबर विधाने एकत्र येतात; पर्याय B (फक्त a and c) मध्ये फक्त काही विधाने घेतली आहेत, पण प्रश्नातील सर्व बरोबर विधाने एकत्र येतात; पर्याय C (फक्त b and c) मध्ये फक्त काही विधाने घेतली आहेत, पण प्रश्नातील सर्व बरोबर विधाने एकत्र येतात।

questions.text:
In which of the following is an article used correctly?
a. I was tired of the life.
b. The both anxious parents sat up the half night.
c. The Kapoors are our neighbours.
questions.explanation: पर्याय A (फक्त c) — 'The life', 'the दोन्ही… the half night' articles over-insert मानक English — फक्त (c) कलम-usage scrutiny टिकते. पर्याय B (फक्त a) मध्ये फक्त काही विधाने घेतली आहेत, पण प्रश्नातील सर्व बरोबर विधाने एकत्र येतात; पर्याय C (फक्त b and c) मध्ये फक्त काही विधाने घेतली आहेत, पण प्रश्नातील सर्व बरोबर विधाने एकत्र येतात; पर्याय D (a, b and c) या प्रश्नाच्या मुख्य संकल्पनेशी सुसंगत नाही।

questions.text:
(Passage on Diet & Nutrition) The passage focuses on:
a. Nutrition for vigour and vitality.
b. Importance of nutrients in curing diseases.
c. Types of nutrients.
d. Balanced diet.
questions.explanation: पर्याय D (वरील सर्व) — अर्धवट जोडीs multi-focus health-education text अपूर्ण वाचन. पर्याय A (फक्त a and b) मध्ये फक्त काही विधाने घेतली आहेत, पण प्रश्नातील सर्व बरोबर विधाने एकत्र येतात; पर्याय B (फक्त c and d) मध्ये फक्त काही विधाने घेतली आहेत, पण प्रश्नातील सर्व बरोबर विधाने एकत्र येतात; पर्याय C (फक्त a, b and d) मध्ये फक्त काही विधाने घेतली आहेत, पण प्रश्नातील सर्व बरोबर विधाने एकत्र येतात।

questions.text:
(Passage on Diet & Nutrition) What are the causes of nutritional deficiencies?
a. Use of preservatives in food
b. Intake of refined food
c. No use of pesticides and chemical fertilizers
d. Use of wholesome foods and fruits
e. Long interval between harvesting and consumption of vegetables and fruits.
questions.explanation: पर्याय C (a, b, e) — Deficiency causes include preservatives (a), refined food (b), and long harvest-to-consumption gaps (e)—not 'no pesticides' (c is चुकी) nor 'wholesome foods' (d), which prevent deficiency. Full five-option bundles सापळा विद्यार्थी who mark every line बरोबर पर्याय A (a, b, c, d, e) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्याख्या/तथ्याशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय B (a, b, d, e) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्याख्या/तथ्याशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय D (a, b, c, e) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्याख्या/तथ्याशी जुळत नाही।

questions.text:
(Passage on Diet & Nutrition) The phrase 'well balanced diet' refers to:
a. Intake of a variety of foods.
b. Consumption of whole meal bread and the white stuff.
c. Proper consumption of vegetables and fruits.
d. Intake of the foods which supply all the essential nutrients.
questions.explanation: योग्य उत्तर पर्याय D आहे पर्याय D (Only d) — 'Well balanced diet' म्हणजे intake supplying all essential nutrients in proper proportions—विधान (d)। Mere variety (a) or mixing white/brown bread (b) without nutrient adequacy misses the definition; vegetables alone (c) is insufficient पर्याय A (Only a and b) मध्ये फक्त काही विधाने घेतली आहेत, पण प्रश्नातील सर्व बरोबर विधाने एकत्र येतात; पर्याय B (Only b and d) मध्ये फक्त काही विधाने घेतली आहेत, पण प्रश्नातील सर्व बरोबर विधाने एकत्र येतात; पर्याय C (Only a) मध्ये फक्त काही विधाने घेतली आहेत, पण प्रश्नातील सर्व बरोबर विधाने एकत्र येतात।

questions.text: (Passage on Diet & Nutrition) Find out the word in the passage which means 'Not supplied in required quantity'
questions.explanation: योग्य उत्तर: Undersupply. Passage मध्ये 'Undersupply' शब्दाचा अर्थ आहे 'अवश्यक प्रमाणात पुरवठा नाही' — म्हणजे गेल्या प्रमाणापेक्षा कमी पुरवठा. 'Deficiency' म्हणजे कमी, पण passage मध्ये 'not supplied in required quantity' साठी 'Undersupply' वापरला आहे.

questions.text:
a. Absence of any of the essential nutrients may lead to death.
b. Oxygen and water are vital elements in human cells.
c. Diseases caused by nutritional deficiencies are irreparable.
d. Diet is one of the essential factors in building and maintaining good health.
Choose the correct alternative/s.
questions.explanation: विज्ञानात हे स्थिर — पर्याय A बरोबर आहे। (a)(b)(d) passage तर्क: , oxygen/, । Deficiency diseases 'irreparable' (c) ati uddeshs — MPSC प्रश्नपत्रिकेत अशा तपशीलांची पुनरावृत्ती होते, म्हणून मुख्य संकल्पना लक्षात ठेवा.।

questions.text:
I am extremely happy.
Select the correct alternative to tag question to the above sentence.
questions.explanation: पर्याय C (aren't I?) — 'मी का?' ध्रुवाची दिशा उलट; 'मी नाही का?' — अशुद्ध अशुद्ध; 'ते नाही का?' — चुकीचे सर्वनाम चुकीचे सर्वनाम. पर्याय A (am I?) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्याख्या/तथ्याशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय B ( नाही I?) या प्रश्नाच्या मुख्य संकल्पनेशी सुसंगत नाही; पर्याय D ( नाही it?) या प्रश्नाच्या मुख्य संकल्पनेशी सुसंगत नाही।

questions.text:
Before Akshay came to Bollywood, he _______ in hotels for five years.
Select the correct alternative to complete the sentence meaningfully.
questions.explanation: पर्याय D (had been working) — भूत perfect continuous 'had been working' fits an action continuing up to a past pivot ('before Akshay came') for five years। साधा भूतकाळ or वर्तमान perfect continuous break the timeline anchor to Bollywood entry पर्याय A (was working) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्याख्या/तथ्याशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय B (has been working) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्याख्या/तथ्याशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय C (had worked) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्याख्या/तथ्याशी जुळत नाही।

questions.text:
Choose the alternative closest in meaning to the word in capitals.
The negotiations have reached an IMPASSE.

options.A: Point at which further development is blocked.
options.B: Point at which highest profit is guaranteed.
options.C: Point of no profit no loss.
options.D: Point at which a meeting concludes.

questions.explanation: योग्य उत्तर: Point at which further development is blocked. 'Impasse' म्हणजे बंध — negotiations पुडे जात नाही, कोई मार्ग उभा रहात नाही. French मूळचा शब्द आहे; तयाचा अर्थ 'अगला विकास थंबलेला बिंदू' असा होतो. Profit, break-even किंवा meeting समाप्ती या अर्थांशी संबंधित नाही.

questions.text:
Identify the part of speech of the word underlined in the following sentence:
Don't go near the edge.
questions.explanation: पर्याय A (Adverb) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय B (Adjective) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय D (Conjunction) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही।

questions.text:
Which of the following is not a synonym of the word GARRULOUS?
a. Loquacious
b. Talkative
c. Gauge
questions.explanation: पर्याय C (Only c) — GARRULOUS म्हणजे बडबड्या—synonyms loquacious/बडबड्या (a, b)। GAUGE म्हणजे measure—अर्थानुसार असंबंधित, the समानार्थी नसलेले शब्द। 'फक्त c' flags gauge as the वेगळा शब्द पर्याय A (Only a and b) मध्ये फक्त काही विधाने घेतली आहेत, पण प्रश्नातील सर्व बरोबर विधाने एकत्र येतात; पर्याय B (Only b and c) मध्ये फक्त काही विधाने घेतली आहेत, पण प्रश्नातील सर्व बरोबर विधाने एकत्र येतात; पर्याय D (All of the above) प्रत्येक विधान बरोबर म्हणतो, पण यापैकी किमान एक विधान चुकीचे आहे।

questions.text:
भारतीय संविधानाच्या वैशिष्ट्यांपैकी, संघराज्याच्या तत्त्वाशी पुढीलपैकी कोणती वैशिष्ट्ये सुसंगत नाहीत?

questions.text: एक महिला म्हणते, 'जर माझ्या वयाच्या अंकांची उलटपालट केली तर ते माझ्या वडिलांचे वय दर्शविते. अर्थात माझे वडील माझ्यापेक्षा वयस्कर आहेत आणि आमच्या वयातील फरक हा आमच्या वयांच्या बेरजेच्या तीन-अकरांश आहे.' तर महिलेचे वय किती?
questions.explanation: योग्य उत्तर: 36 वर्ष. महिलेचे वय 10a+b आणि वडिलांचे 10b+a (अंक उलट). फरक = (10b+a) − (10a+b) = 9(b−a); बेरज = 11(a+b). दिले की फरक = (3/11) × बेरज, म्हणून 9(b−a) = 3(a+b), म्हणजे 3(b−a) = a+b → 2b = 4a → b = 2a. a = 3, b = 6 → महिला 36, वडील 63; फरक 27 = (3/11) × 99 ✓.

questions.text: Pudheelaiki konati sandhi yogya aahe?
questions.explanation: The answer is option B: Compound 'mano-kaamana' uses the correct samasa vowel: manah→mano before kaamana (desire of mind). questions.text: Kaal kashaala mhantataat?

questions.explanation: 'Udyaa' (tomorrow) in the sentence is a pure shabdyogi avyay—independent time adverb without case inflection. It is not kriya visheshan (which modifies verbs like 'slowly'); vibhakti pratirup avyay would show case endings like 'tyaamule'.

questions.text:
Khaaleel visheshanaanche udaaharanashi yogya jodya laavaa.
a. Naam sadrushya visheshan - I. Jo mulagaa vyaayaam karto, to sashakt asto.
b. Darshak visheshan - II. Shreemant maanasaannaa garva asto.
k. Sambandhee visheshan - III. Kon manushya yeun gela.

questions.explanation: Adjective-type matching: Darshak (II) 'Shreemant…garva'; Prashnarthak (IV) 'Hee mulagee chalaakh'; Sambandhi (I) 'Jo mulagaa vyaayaam…'; Naam sadrushya (III) 'Kon manushya…'—order II, IV, I, III = option (A). Swapping sambandhi with prashnarthak breaks relative-clause vs question-word tests.

questions.text: 'Sahaleemadhye shikshakaannee vidyaarthyaannaa sambhaalatate.' — Yaa vaakyaateel kartaa kontaa?
questions.explanation: Kartari prayoga: subject performing action—'Shikshak' (teacher) handles students in the camp; not 'Sahal' (camp), 'Vidyaarthee' (object), or 'Sambhaal' (verb stem). Agent = shikshaka in 'shikshakaannee vidyaarthyaannaa sambhaalatate'.

questions.text: 'Dev tyaache bhale karo' yaa vaakyaachaa prakaar kontaa?
questions.explanation: Option A is correct because 'Dev tyaache bhale karo' expresses blessing/prayer—aadnyaarthi (optative benediction), not command to obey, nor vidhi (rule), vidhyaa (knowledge), or sanket (hint). Divine blessing requests map to aadnyaarthi in Marathi grammar classification. You can eliminate B (Vidhyaarthee), C (Sanketaarthee), D (Vidhaanaarthee) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. 'Shorlee' is adjective/epithet; 'sukhroop' is adverbial modifier of arrival—not the visheya core.
