questions.explanation: Option A works here because Under Hazardous Waste (Management, Handling and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2008, the Ministry of Environment and Forests (now MoEFCC) is nodal for transboundary movement and transit permission through India. questions.text:
Identify the correct statement/s from the following regarding Food Security Bill, 2013.
A. The Bill provides food safety benefits to the 50% of the urban population and 75% of the rural population.
B. Beneficiaries will be provided rice at Rs. 3/-kg, coarse grains at Re. 1/-kg and wheat at Rs. 2/-kg per month.

options.A: Both A and B are correct
options.B: Both A and B are incorrect

questions.explanation: Both statements are marked incorrect in the official key: (A) says 'food safety' rather than statutory 'food security' entitlements, and misframes NFSA coverage language; (B) distorts how subsidised grain quantities/pricing are legally structured under the National Food Security Act framework. Treat 'both wrong' as the exam stand—not partial credit on familiar ₹3/₹2/Re 1 figures alone.

questions.text: The term sustainable development first came into prominence in the World Conservation Strategy presented in _________.
questions.explanation: The term 'sustainable development' gained global policy prominence in the IUCN–UNEP–WWF 'World Conservation Strategy' (1980). The Brundtland Report (1987) popularised the definition later; Rio (1992) was the Earth Summit—different milestones on the same concept arc.

questions.text: What is India's position in the Sustainable Development Goals Index released in 2020?
questions.explanation: Option A matches the question because india ranked 117th on the Sustainable Development Goals Index in the 2020 assessment—mid-lower tier among tracked countries that year. Double-digit ranks like 17th or 40th, or a deep 125th, do not match that edition's published scoreboard. You can eliminate B (17th), C (40th), D (125th) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: "Economic growth is the increase in output only" whose statement was this?
questions.explanation: Choose option B: Charles P. Kindleberger articulated a narrow 'growth as output increase' view in development economics discourse—contrasting broader welfare definitions. Edison, Gorwala, and Schumpeter are associated with innovation/creative destruction or Indian administrative reports, not this specific output-only growth quote. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements and choose the correct option regarding Indian economy.
A. Considering the economic changes in India after globalisation, 'Trickle Down Theory' is precisely applicable to Indian economy.
B. The high growth rate of Indian economy after globalisation, especially since 2005, poses question about applicability of the 'Trickle Down Theory'.

options.C: Both statements A and B are correct
options.D: Both statements A and B are incorrect

questions.explanation: Post-liberalisation high GDP growth with persistent inequality and lagging human-development indicators led many analysts to question naive 'trickle-down' assumptions—statement B captures that scepticism. Statement A wrongly treats trickle-down as 'precisely applicable' to India after globalisation, overstating automatic poverty reduction from growth alone.

questions.text: "About 40% of the population of the developing world did not benefit from economic growth during the 1950's and 1960's." Who made this statement?
questions.explanation: World Bank President Robert McNamara highlighted that roughly 40% of the developing world's population saw little gain from growth in the 1950s–60s—fuel for redistribution and basic-needs lending agendas. Kindleberger wrote on growth/trade; Dreze on Indian nutrition rights; 'Robert Clover' is not the standard attribution.

questions.text: Which one of the following National Mission was not included in the National Climate Action Program?
questions.explanation: Option D works here because National Action Plan on Climate Change (2008) lists eight missions—Solar, Enhanced Energy Efficiency, Sustainable Habitat, Water, Green India, Himalayan, Strategic Knowledge, and Agriculture—under MoEFCC. National Health Mission is a health delivery programme outside this climate mission bundle. Distractors A (National Solar Mission), B (National Sustainable Habitat Mission), C (National Water Mission) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Which of the following is/are reason/s for the existence of poverty even after seven decades of Independence in India?
A. More dependency of Economy on the agricultural sector.
B. Shortage of employment opportunities in manufacturing sector.
C. High growth rate of agriculture in comparison with developed countries.

options.A: Statements A and C are correct
options.B: Statements A and B are correct

questions.explanation: Persistent poverty links to heavy dependence on low-productivity agriculture (A) and insufficient labour absorption in manufacturing (B). Statement C is weak: India's agriculture has not outpaced developed-country farm productivity in a way that explains poverty—high rural dependency without industrial jobs is the sharper diagnosis.

questions.text:
Program/s implemented under the Integrated Child Development Services Scheme _________.
A. Nutrition supplemental program
B. Health check-up
C. Worker's training
D. Gender inequality
questions.explanation: The answer is option C: ICDS core services include supplementary nutrition (A) and health check-ups (B)—Anganwadi frontline package. Worker training appears in broader ICDS administration but 'gender inequality' is not a programme component; You can eliminate A (Only A, C), B (Only C, D), D (A, B and C) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. questions.text:
As per the 2011 Census, 13% of the total urban population of the country was living in which of the following cities in 2011?
a. Mumbai
b. Chennai
c. Kolkata
d. Delhi
questions.explanation: Option B matches the question because Census 2011 urban concentration: Mumbai, Kolkata, and Delhi together housed about 13% of India's urban population—mega-city gravity without Chennai in that specific share bracket for the correct combination. Partial pairs (Mumbai–Delhi only, or adding Chennai) misstate the three-city aggregate the question cites. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: As per the 2011 Census, India's population percentage is _________ of the total Global population.
questions.explanation: India's 2011 population was about 121 crore against ~700 crore world total—roughly 17.5% of global population, reinforcing demographic weight in SDG and climate negotiations. Shares of 2.4%, 25%, or 31.9% mis-scale India's one-sixth-plus presence.

questions.text:
Which of the following statement/s is/are correct in relation to India's National Population Policy, 2000?
A. Stabilizing the population of the country by 2050 with maximum two children norm.
B. Universal immunization.
C. Reduction of infant mortality rate below 30% per thousand.

options.A: Statements A, B and C are correct
options.B: Statements A and C are correct

questions.explanation: Option D is the right choice since National Population Policy 2000 lists universal immunisation among its social-sector goals—statement B stands. Statement A misstates stabilisation year/norm details (policy targets 2045, not a simple 2050 two-child statute); statement C garbles IMR as '30% per thousand' instead of per-1000-live-births phrasing—so only B survives. You can eliminate A (Statements A, B and C are correct), B (Statements A and C are correct), C (Only statement A is correct) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements:
A. Gender Development Index is a composite index of health, education, empowerment and labour market.
B. When the above four factors are considered together, inequality in women and men has adverse impact on Human Development Index.

options.C: Both A and B are correct
options.D: Both A and B are incorrect

questions.explanation: Gender Development Index (GDI) adjusts human-development dimensions for gender gaps in health, education, empowerment, and labour participation. Gender inequality directly drags composite HDI when women's outcomes lag—both statements describe standard UNDP logic, not competing alternatives.

questions.text:
Which of the following was the main objective of the 20 point programme announced on 26 June, 1975?
A. To improve the standard of living.
B. To help the people living below the poverty line (Poverty alleviation).

options.C: Both A and B are correct

questions.explanation: Option C is correct because indira Gandhi's Twenty Point Programme (26 June 1975) bundled poverty alleviation for the poorest with broader standard-of-living improvements—employment, housing, land reforms, and price control strands. Neither objective alone captures the programme; the Emergency-era package explicitly pursued both uplift and anti-poverty targeting. You can eliminate A (Only A is correct), B (Only B is correct), D (None of the above) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. questions.text: The ratio of lengths to radii of two rods of same material is 1 : 2 and 2 : 3. If temperature difference between two ends of the rod is same, then what will be the ratio of heat flow?
questions.explanation: For steady conduction in the same material, heat flow Q = kAΔT/L with k and ΔT identical for both rods, so Q ∝ r²/L. Given L₁:L₂ = 1:2 and r₁:r₂ = 2:3, Q₁/Q₂ = (r₁/r₂)² × (L₂/L₁) = (4/9) × (2/1) = 8/9. Options like 3:2 or 4:3 forget the inverse length factor or square only one radius.

questions.text:
In the network of resistances shown below, Current through the battery will be _________.
[Circuit with 1Ω, 2Ω, 2Ω, 3Ω, 4Ω resistors and 2V battery]
questions.explanation: Reduce the mixed network of 1 Ω, 2 Ω, 2 Ω, 3 Ω and 4 Ω stepwise to equivalent resistance 2 Ω across the 2 V source—then I = V/R = 1.0 A. Treating all five resistors in series (12 Ω) or mis-merging parallel branches inflates current to 1.5 A, 3.5 A or 4.0 A distractors.

questions.text: Which physical quantity conserved during collision?
questions.explanation: Choose option B: in an isolated collision, total linear momentum is conserved even when kinetic energy is not (inelastic case). Mass of individual bodies may combine chemically but is not the conserved dynamical quantity tested here; time and length have no collision conservation law. You can eliminate A (Mass), C (Time), D (Length) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: Which of the following confirms that the universe is not static but expanding?

options.A: Red shift in the light coming from distant galaxies
options.B: Blue shift in the light coming from distant galaxies
options.C: Bending of light while passing near to the Black hole

questions.explanation: Option A is the right choice since Hubble's observation of red shift in spectra from distant galaxies means light is stretched as sources recede—direct evidence of cosmic expansion. Blue shift would imply approach; gravitational bending near black holes is lensing; constancy of c is a separate postulate of special relativity. Distractors B (Blue shift in the light coming from dis…), C (Bending of light while passing near to …), D (Constancy of velocity of light) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: Neutrino particle is emitted in the process of _________.
questions.explanation: Β-decay converts a neutron to a proton with emission of an electron and an antineutrino (Pauli postulated the neutrino to balance energy–momentum). α-decay ejects a helium nucleus; γ-decay is electromagnetic with no neutrino; X-rays are not a nuclear decay channel.

questions.text: What is the effect of increase in temperature on viscosity of gases?
questions.explanation: Unlike liquids, gas viscosity rises with temperature because faster molecules transfer more momentum across layers during collisions. The 'viscosity decreases on heating' rule applies to liquids where intermolecular cohesion weakens—reversing that logic is incorrect for gases.

questions.text: Stomata will open if there is accumulation of the following element in the guard cells _________.
questions.explanation: Option B is correct because Light triggers K⁺ influx into guard cells; the osmotic pull draws water in, turgor increases and stomata open. Mg, Fe and Zn are essential micronutrients but not the ion whose accumulation directly drives the opening mechanism in standard stomatal physiology. Distractors A (Magnesium), C (Iron), D (Zinc) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: Citrus canker is caused by which type of pathogen?
questions.explanation: Citrus canker is a bacterial disease caused by Xanthomonas citri (formerly X. axonopodis pv. citri)—raised lesions on leaves, twigs and fruit. Fungal rots, viral mosaic and nematode galls produce different symptom patterns on citrus.

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding Spirogyra algae?
a. It is commonly called as Pond scum.
b. It grows in Marine water.
c. Its cell consist spiral shaped chloroplast.
d. It belong in family Zygnemataceae.
questions.explanation: Option C matches the question because Spirogyra is freshwater 'pond scum' with characteristic spiral chloroplasts and belongs to Zygnemataceae. Statement (b) is incorrect—it is a freshwater filamentous alga, not a marine species; options including (b) misplace its habitat. questions.text:
The categories of sclereids are _________.
a. Macrosclereids
b. Osteosclereids
c. Tracheids
d. Asterosclereids
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Choose option C: Macrosclereids, osteosclereids and asterosclereids are recognised categories of sclereids—thick-walled supportive sclerenchyma cells. Tracheids are elongated xylem water-conducting cells, not a sclereid type; pairing them with sclereids confuses tissue systems. questions.text: Which of the following sets of hormones regulate menstrual cycle?
questions.explanation: The ovarian–uterine cycle is orchestrated by hypothalamic GnRH driving pituitary FSH/LH pulses, with ovarian estrogen and luteal progesterone completing the loop. Testosterone, corticosterone, cortisol and dihydrotestosterone belong to androgen/stress axes—not the core menstrual regulatory quartet.

questions.text: Flowers, leaves and seeds of which plant are used to prepare a narcotics 'Marijuana'?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option A — Marijuana (cannabis) is prepared from flowers, leaves and seeds of Cannabis sativa. Nicotiana tabacum yields tobacco; Papaver somniferum is the opium poppy; Mentha spicata is spearmint—none are the cannabis narcotic source. You can eliminate B (Nicotiana tabacum), C (Opium Poppy), D (Mentha Spicata) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
The main objective/s of "Human Genome Project 1990" was/were _________.
a. To identify 20,000 to 25,000 genes in human.
b. To determine the sequence of 5 billion base pairs in DNA.
c. To incorporate new genomic knowledge into research and medicine.
d. To develop cloning of animals.
questions.explanation: Option C works here because the Human Genome Project's formally stated core target was mapping and identifying roughly 20,000–25,000 human genes—statement (a). The human diploid sequence is about 3 billion base pairs, not 5 billion (b); broad medical application (c) and animal cloning (d) were collateral or outside the primary 1990 mandate the official answer accepts as 'only a'. Distractors A (Only b and d), B (Only a and c), D (Only b) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: In prokaryotic genetic code, which is the initial code for N-formyl methionine?
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic translation initiates with N-formylmethionine encoded by the start codon AUG (fMet-tRNA). TTG, CUG and GGC are not the standard bacterial initiator codon in textbook genetic code tables—though eukaryotes also use AUG for Met without formylation.

questions.text:
Which of the following options does not involve use of carbon in any form for energy production?
A. Wood
B. Biogas
C. Geothermal source
D. Coal
questions.explanation: The answer is option C: Geothermal energy taps Earth's internal heat—no carbon combustion or biomass carbon cycle. Wood, biogas and coal all release or store carbon in their energy pathways; only the geothermal route is carbon-free among the listed sources. You can eliminate A (Both A and B), B (Both B and C), D (Only D) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text:
Which chemical bond is formed between Mg and Cl atoms during formation of compound MgCl₂?
a. Covalent bond
b. Ionic bond
c. Coordinate covalent bond
d. Metallic bond
questions.explanation: Magnesium (metal) transfers electrons to chlorine (non-metal), forming Mg²⁺ and Cl⁻ held in an ionic lattice—classic electron-transfer bonding in MgCl₂. Pure covalent sharing suits non-metal pairs; coordinate covalent and metallic bonding do not describe this salt.

questions.text: Which of the following is used as a substitute for wool in the production of commercial fibers?
questions.explanation: Polyacrylonitrile (acrylic/ORlon) mimics wool warmth and feel in commercial fibres. Dacron is polyester; Teflon is polytetrafluoroethylene; caprolactam is the nylon-6 monomer—not the acrylic wool substitute.

questions.text:
Which of the following medicine can be classified as both Analgesics and Antipyretics?
A. Veronal
B. Benadryl
C. Penicillin
D. Paracetamol
questions.explanation: Option D is the right choice since Paracetamol (acetaminophen) lowers fever and relieves pain—dual antipyretic and analgesic action. Veronal is a barbiturate sedative; Benadryl is an antihistamine; penicillin is an antibiotic without routine antipyretic use. You can eliminate A (Only A), B (Both A and D), C (Both B and C) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Match the correct pairs:
A. Monosaccharide - i. Raffinose
B. Disaccharide - ii. Starch
C. Trisaccharide - iii. Glucose
D. Polysaccharide - iv. Sucrose

options.A: A – iii, B – ii, C – i, D – iv
options.B: A – ii, B – i, C – iii, D – iv
options.C: A – iv, B – iii, C – ii, D – i
options.D: A – iii, B – iv, C – i, D – ii

questions.explanation: The correct answer is option D — Carbohydrate tiering: glucose is a monosaccharide; sucrose a disaccharide; raffinose a trisaccharide; starch a polysaccharide—A–iii, B–iv, C–i, D–ii. Mixing starch with monosaccharide or raffinose with disaccharide slots breaks standard biochemistry classification. questions.text: The isotopes of hydrogen and their respective mass ratio are _________.
questions.explanation: Hydrogen isotopes in ascending mass order are protium (¹H), deuterium (²H) and tritium (³H)—mass ratio 1:2:3. Reordering tritium first or swapping deuterium/protium positions misstates nuclear mass numbering.

questions.text: Which of the following Constitution Amendment Acts provided for the formation of the 'Metropolitan Planning Committee'?
questions.explanation: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 (Nagarpalika Act) inserted provisions for Metropolitan Planning Committees in urban agglomerations. The 73rd Amendment covers Panchayats; the 42nd and 44th Amendments deal with other constitutional changes—not metropolitan planning.

questions.text:
Identify the incorrect pair/s of the various Committees constituted under the Indian Constituent Assembly and its Chairmans.
A. Steering Committee – Rajendra Prasad
B. Advisory Committee – Vallabhbhai Patel
C. Central Rights Committee – J. B. Kripalani
D. Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee – Jawaharlal Nehru
questions.explanation: The answer is option C: Steering Committee (Rajendra Prasad) and Advisory Committee (Vallabhbhai Patel) pairings are correct. Central Rights Committee was chaired by Vallabhbhai Patel—not J. B. Kripalani (C)—and the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee was chaired by Kripalani—not Nehru (D). Options retaining A/B as wrong miss these swapped chairmanship facts. Distractors A (A and C), B (B and D), D (A and B) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Select the correct statement/s from the following.
A. The Vice-President shall hold office for a term of five years from the date on which he enters upon his office.
B. A Vice-President may, by writing under his hand addressed to the President, resign his office.
C. A Vice-President may be removed from his office by a resolution of House of the People passed by a majority of all the then members of the House of People and approved by the Council of States.
questions.explanation: Article 67: the Vice-President holds office for five years (A) and may resign by writing to the President (B)—both correct. Removal requires a Rajya Sabha-led process with special majorities, not a simple Lok Sabha resolution as (C) suggests; hence only A and B stand.

questions.text:

A. Article 335 is related to Representation of the Anglo-Indian Community in the Legislative Assembly.
B. Grants if any, were made for the benefit of the Anglo-Indian Community in respect of education in the financial year ending on the 31st March, 1948, the same shall be given for the first three financial years after the commencement of the Constitution.
C. During every succeeding period of three years, the grants may be less 10%, than that, for the immediately preceding period of three years.
questions.explanation: Choose option A: article 335 governs claims of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in services—it does not deal with Anglo-Indian representation in legislatures (Articles 331/334 zone). Statements (B) and (C) on educational grants to the Anglo-Indian community align with transitional constitutional provisions; (A) is the false pairing. You can eliminate B (Only B and C), C (Only C), D (All of the above) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. questions.text:
Which of the following are related to Article 1 to 4 of Part I of the Constitution of India?
a. The union and its territory
b. About the Fundamental Rights
c. About the Justice
d. Regarding duties
questions.explanation: Option C is the right choice since Part I, Articles 1–4 exclusively cover the Union and its territory (names, admission, formation of new states). Fundamental Rights occupy Part III; 'Justice' appears in the Preamble; Fundamental Duties sit in Part IV-A—none belong to Articles 1–4. Distractors A (Only b and d), B (Only c and a), D (Only a and b) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. questions.text: Identify the States without special status under Article 371 and its Sub-Articles of the Constitution of India.
questions.explanation: Article 371 and its sub-articles grant special provisions to states like Nagaland, Assam, Manipur, Sikkim, Mizoram and others. Tripura and Jharkhand operate under the general state framework without an Article 371 special-status package in the standard constitutional map.

questions.text: The First Lok Adalat Camp after Independence was held in which State in 1982?
questions.explanation: Option B works here because the first Lok Adalat camp after Independence was organised in Gujarat in 1982 (Junagadh/Bhavnagar district initiative), later scaled nationally. Maharashtra popularised Lok Adalats through the permanent Legal Services Authority route, but the inaugural post-Independence camp credit goes to Gujarat. You can eliminate A (Maharashtra), C (Andhra Pradesh), D (Punjab) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. A. House Committee
B. Committee on Chief Commissioner's Provinces
C. Adhoc Committee on Citizenship
D. Adhoc Committee on Supreme Court
questions.explanation: Option A is correct because Dr B. Pattabhi Sitaramayya chaired the Constituent Assembly House Committee and the Committee on Chief Commissioner's Provinces—pair A. questions.text: The 'National Commission for Protection of Child Rights' (NCPCR) in India was established in which year?
questions.explanation: NCPCR was established in March 2007 under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005. 2001 and 2005 pre-date statutory creation; 2010 post-dates the notified commission—2007 is the establishment year to remember.

questions.text: The 'Protection of Children from Sexual Offences' (POCSO) Act was enacted in India in which year?
questions.explanation: Option B matches the question because the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act was enacted in 2012 to define and penalise sexual offences against minors. Earlier child-protection frameworks existed, but the dedicated POCSO statute is the 2012 Act—not 2009, 2015 or 2018. You can eliminate A (2009), C (2015), D (2018) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. questions.text: When was the National Commission for Women established in India?
questions.explanation: This maps to "1992". The National Commission for Women is a statutory body established under the NCW Act 1990 to review safeguards for women and recommend legislation. In MPSC PYQ analysis, this item type accounts for the largest cluster of 'easy marks lost due to misreading' — slow down the stem, and the option leaps out.

questions.text:
Which of the following functions were performed by Constituent Assembly on January 24, 1950?
A. Adopted the National Flag
B. Adopted the National Anthem
C. Adopted the National Song
D. Elected Dr. Rajendra Prasad as a First President of India
questions.explanation: For this question, the correct option reads: Only B, C, D. The President of India is the head of state, elected indirectly through an electoral college via a single-transferable-vote proportional-representation system. The Constituent Assembly first met on 9 December 1946; it adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949 (Constitution Day) and it came into force on 26 January 1950. The examiner rewards precision on this item — every option is engineered to feel plausible, but only the marked one matches the exact wording of the source document.

questions.text:
Select the correct statements from the following.
A. The Constituent Assembly was constituted in November, 1946 under the Cabinet Mission Plan.
B. Cabinet Mission rejected the idea of two Constituent Assemblies.
C. The Cripps Proposal was accepted by the Muslim League.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option A — statement A: the Constituent Assembly was constituted in November 1946 under the Cabinet Mission Plan—correct. B: the Mission insisted on one Constituent Assembly for India (rejecting two assemblies)—correct. C is incorrect: the Muslim League rejected the Cripps Proposal in 1942, not accepted it. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: In which country, the concept of Modern Constitutionalism was started?
questions.explanation: Option A works here because Modern constitutionalism—written constitution, separation of powers, popular sovereignty, judicial review—crystallised with the American Revolution and the U.S. Constitution (1787). England evolved uncodified conventions; France's modern constitutional cycle followed 1789; India adopted its framework much later. Distractors B (England), C (France), D (India) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text:
Identify the correct statement/s from the following.
A. A person who holds, or who has held office as President shall, subject to the other provisions of the Constitution, be eligible for re-election to that office.
B. No person shall be eligible for election as President unless he is qualified for election as a member of the Council of the States.
questions.explanation: Article 58(1) explicitly permits re-election of a person who has held the office of President. Article 58(3) requires Lok Sabha eligibility—not Rajya Sabha (Council of States) as statement B claims—so only A is correct.

questions.text:
Which of the following statement is correct?

questions.text:
What is the meaning of 'guillotine' in the Indian Budget Process?
a. Raising taxes to fill Government deficits.
b. Remaining budgetary demands for grants are put to vote without further discussion.

questions.explanation: Choose option A: in parliamentary budget procedure, 'guillotine' means the Speaker puts all remaining Demands for Grants to vote together without further clause-by-clause debate once the allotted time expires—statement (b). It is not a tax hike, RBI crisis tool, or automatic rejection at Parliament's end. questions.text:
मुघलकालीन न्यायव्यवस्थेतील शिक्षा आणि शिक्षेचे स्वरूप यांच्या अचूक जोड्या जुळवा.
स्तंभ 'अ' (शिक्षा):
अ. हद्द
ब. ताझीर
क. किसास
ड. तशहीर
स्तंभ 'ब' (शिक्षेचे स्वरूप):
i. जशास तसे
ii. मानहानी, धिंड काढणे
iii. ताकीद, समज वा हद्दपार
iv. मृत्युदंड, हातपाय तोडणे

questions.text: Which Act was described by Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru as 'a new charter of Slavery'?
questions.explanation: The answer is option C: Jawaharlal Nehru attacked the Government of India Act, 1935 as a 'new charter of slavery' because it entrenched colonial control—provincial autonomy on paper, but veto power, princely-state safeguards, and no real self-rule. Morley–Minto (1909) and Montagu–Chelmsford (1919) drew other epithets; Rowlatt (1919) was the 'black' repressive law—not Nehru's 1935 phrase. You can eliminate A (The Morley-Minto Reforms Act, 1909), B (The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms Act, 1919), D (Rowlatt Act, 1919) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:

questions.explanation: Option C matches the question because the greased Enfield cartridges of 1857 were issued at company arsenals where sepoys trained on the new rifle—Ambala, Sialkot, and Dum Dum are the standard trio in Maharashtra history syllabi. Calcutta (Fort William) was the political capital, not one of the three named rifle-training centres in most textbook lists. Partial sets dropping Dum Dum or Sialkot miss the complete deployment chain. Distractors A ((a), (b) and (c)), B ((b) and (d)), D ((a), (b) and (d)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: The District Local Board was established during the period of which Viceroy?
questions.explanation: Lord Ripon (1880–84) is the 'Father of Local Self-Government' in India; his 1882 resolution expanded district and municipal boards, including District Local Boards for rural administration. Lytton rolled back Ripon's liberalism; Curzon centralised; Wellesley predates the Ripon-era local-board framework.

questions.text: 'Famine Code' was prepared in 1883 on the recommendation of which of the following Commissions?
questions.explanation: Option A is the right choice since the Indian Famine Code of 1883 flowed directly from the recommendations of the Famine Commission headed by Sir Richard Strachey (1880)—standardising relief, works, and mortality reporting after recurring droughts. George Campbell and James Lyall chaired later famine inquiries; MacDonald belongs to a different policy era. Strachey + 1883 Famine Code is the pair to lock. You can eliminate B (George Campbell Commission), C (MacDonald Commission), D (Sir James Lyall Commission) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

His legislature speech—'I am a Nationalist first, a Nationalist second, and a Nationalist last'—is quoted in standard biographies of the pre-1940 Jinnah. Azad, Iqbal, and Sir Syed each miss one of the two stem markers.

questions.text:
Match the following:
(a) 1899 'Gurakhi' (Mumbai) - (i) A.B. Kolhatkar
(b) 1906 'Bhala' (Pune) - (ii) Gir
(c) 1907 'Hari Kishore' (Yavatmal) - (iii) Shri L.N. Joshi
(d) 1909 'Deshsevak' (Nagpur) - (iv) Bhopatkar
questions.explanation: Option C is correct because anchor the editors to dates and places: 1899 'Gurakhi' (Mumbai) → Shri L.N. Joshi; 1906 'Bhala' (Pune) → Bhopatkar; 1907 'Hari Kishore' (Yavatmal) → Gir; 1909 'Deshsevak' (Nagpur) → A.B. Kolhatkar. That yields a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i. Swapping Kolhatkar with Bhopatkar or Gir breaks the chronology of Marathi nationalist journalism. You can eliminate A (a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i), B (a-iv, b-i, c-iii, d-ii), D (a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: What was the Strachey Commission about?
questions.explanation: The answer is option C: the Strachey Commission (1880) was appointed to frame famine/drought relief policy after the Great Famine of 1876–78—not education, health, or child-marriage reform. Its report underpinned the 1883 Famine Code. Students who recall 'Strachey' only from Q5 should connect both questions to the same drought-relief mandate. Distractors A (Educational Reforms), B (Health Improvement), D (Prevention of Child Marriage) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: Who among the following was the first president of the 'All India Trade Union Congress' established in 1920?
questions.explanation: Lala Lajpat Rai presided over the inaugural session of the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) at Bombay in 1920. Tilak died that year and was never AITUC president; Shripad Dange and Ashok Mehta led the body in later decades. First-president MCQs almost always test the 1920 founding chair, not later communist or socialist heads.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements:
(a) The latitudinal extension of Maharashtra is less than the longitudinal extension.
(b) The Tropic of Cancer Passes through Maharashtra.
(c) The east-west length of Maharashtra is about 800 k.m.
(d) The area of Maharashtra is 3,07,713 sq. k.m.
Which of the statement/s given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Maharashtra runs roughly 720 km north–south (latitudinal span) versus ~800 km east–west (longitudinal span)—so (a) holds. The Tropic of Cancer passes through Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, and Tripura, not Maharashtra—(b) is incorrect. Official area 3,07,713 sq km and ~800 km east–west width make (c) and (d) correct; only (a), (c), and (d) survive.

questions.text:
Arrange the following mountain peaks in descending order of height.
(a) Makalu (b) Nandadevi (c) Annapurna (d) Badarinath
questions.explanation: Option C is the right choice since Height order among the four: Makalu (~8,485 m) tops Annapurna I (~8,091 m), then Nandadevi (~7,816 m), with Badrinath (~6,150 m) far lower—it is a pilgrimage peak, not an 8,000-er. Descending sequence is (a)–(c)–(b)–(d). Options placing Nandadevi above Makalu or Badrinath mid-list confuse Himalayan hierarchy. Distractors A ((d), (a), (b), (c)), B ((b), (d), (c), (a)), D ((c), (b), (a), (d)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: India has the longest border with which of the following country?
questions.explanation: India's longest international land border is with Bangladesh (~4,096 km)—longer than China, Pakistan, Nepal, or Myanmar segments. Nepal and Bhutan borders are substantial but shorter; Pakistan ranks third among neighbours by length. 'Longest border' prelims almost always expect Bangladesh, not the more politically salient Pakistan line.

questions.text:
Match the following districts of Maharashtra and its percentage of Urban population as per the Census 2011.
(a) Ahilyanagar - (i) 25.47
(b) Yavatmal - (ii) 18.98
(c) Satara - (iii) 21.59
(d) Latur - (iv) 20.10
questions.explanation: Option C works here because Work from Census 2011 urban-population percentages correct to the grid: Ahilyanagar pairs with (iv), Yavatmal with (iii), Satara with (ii), Latur with (i)—the a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i combination alone is internally consistent. Options mirroring alphabetical district order (a-i, b-ii…) look tidy but mis-assign Yavatmal and Latur figures. You can eliminate A (a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii), B (a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv), D (a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: Which of the following script is used in Santhali language?
questions.explanation: Option B is correct because Santhali (Munda family) is written in Ol Chiki, invented by Pandit Raghunath Murmu in 1925 and later included in the Eighth Schedule. 'Billu' and 'Kota' are distractor script names; Braille is a tactile system for the visually impaired, not a Santhali language script. Distractors A (Billu), C (Brail), D (Kota) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text:
Match the following:
Column A - Column B
(a) Bhandara - (i) Yashwant Lake
(b) Nandurbar - (ii) City of Lakes
(c) Udaypur - (iii) City of Gates
(d) Ch. Sambhaji nagar - (iv) District of Lakes
questions.explanation: Maharashtra's sobriquets pair thus: Bhandara → 'District of Lakes' (Wainganga basin water bodies); Nandurbar → Yashwant Lake (Toranmal belt); Udaypur (Nanded area) → 'City of Lakes'; Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) → 'City of Gates'. The a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii grid matches; swapping Aurangabad with Bhandara is the common trap.

questions.text:
Observe the following statements:
(a) As per the recommendation of Famine Commission, Agricultural Department was established in June 1881.
(b) Maharashtra Agricultural Commissioner Office is at Mukundnagar, Pune.
(c) Krushi Bhushan award is given in the name of Ex-Chief Minister.
questions.explanation: Option B matches the question because Krushi Bhushan is a Maharashtra state award named after former Chief Minister Vasantrao Naik—recognising progressive farmers; statement (c) alone is correct. Statement (a) about the 1881 Agricultural Department after the Famine Commission is broadly historical but not the correct sole truth here; (b) misplaces the Commissionerate (Pune, not Mukundnagar). Do not merge (a) with (c) unless the paper explicitly accepts both. You can eliminate A (Only Statement (a) is correct.), C (Statement (a) and (c) are correct.), D (Statement (b) and (c) are correct.) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
According to the Maharashtra Co-operative Act, 1960 which of the following is/are not the purpose of audit of Co-operative societies?
(a) To check whether all the books of account are maintained by the Co-operative societies registered under the Co-operative societies Act.
(b) To check whether the management of Co-operative societies is in accordance with the Co-operative Act and the principles of Co-operation.
(c) In case of mal practices in the Co-operative society, making the directors liable and imposing financial penalties.
(d) To detect errors and irregular transactions in the accumulated expenditure of Co-operative societies.
questions.explanation: Maharashtra Co-operative Societies Act audit aims at verifying accounts, statutory compliance, and detecting irregularities—not adjudicating malpractices or imposing penalties on directors (that is prosecution/ registrar action). Statement (c) alone falls outside audit's defined purpose; (a), (b), and (d) describe legitimate audit objectives.

questions.text: As per the Economic survey of Maharashtra 2023-24 _________ is the largest contributor of own tax revenue of the state.
questions.explanation: Maharashtra Economic Survey 2023–24 identifies GST as the largest single component of the state's own tax revenue—reflecting post-2017 subsumed indirect taxes. State VAT on sales/trade now sits inside GST; standalone 'Tax on Sales' or 'Tax on Social Services' no longer tops the own-revenue table.

questions.text:
Match the Indian Industrial Institutions and its year of establishment.
(a) Industrial Finance Corporation of India (IFCI) - (i) 1964
(b) Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) - (ii) 1948
(c) National Small Industries Corporation - (iii) 1954
(d) National Industrial Development Corporation - (iv) 1955
questions.explanation: The answer is option B: IFCI (1948), IDBI (1964), NSIC (1955), and NIDC (1954) anchor industrial-finance chronology: a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii. Swapping IFCI with IDBI dates (1948 vs 1964) is the classic trap—IFCI was India's first development financial institution after Independence; IDBI came later as apex term-lending bank. You can eliminate A (a-i, b-iii, c-iv, d-ii), C (a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i), D (a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. questions.text:
Which is/are the correct statements about India Employment Report 2024?
(a) The report was released on 1 March 2024.
(b) The report was jointly prepared by ILO and Institute for Human Development.
(c) The report highlighted the increasing uncertainties in the labour market due to fast changing technologies.
questions.explanation: Option C matches the question because india Employment Report 2024 was jointly released by ILO and the Institute for Human Development (IHD), stressing tech-driven labour-market uncertainty. The 1 March release date in statement (a) does not match the correct pair; (b) and (c) together capture authorship and theme. Distractors A ((a) and (b)), B ((a) and (c)), D (Only (a)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: According to Economic Survey of Maharashtra 2023-24, Maharashtra State ranks _________ with 27% share in all India in Organic Agriculture Production.
questions.explanation: Maharashtra Economic Survey 2023–24 places the state second nationally in organic agriculture production with about a 27% share of India's output—after the leader (Madhya Pradesh in most rankings). 'First' or 'fifth' misinterpret headline rankings; 'third' is a near-miss distractor for students who recall MP–Maharashtra–Rajasthan ordering.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements:
(a) Reserve Bank of India was established in the year 1935.
(b) Major 14 Commercial banks in India were nationalized in July 1959.
(c) State Bank of India was established in July 1955.
(d) The head office of Reserve Bank is at Mumbai.
Which of the above statement/s is/are correct?
questions.explanation: "(a), (c) and (d)" is the fact the question is pointing at. The Reserve Bank of India was established under the RBI Act 1934 (operative 1 April 1935) and nationalised on 1 January 1949; it is India's monetary authority and banking regulator. Read each statement independently and check it against a factual anchor (a date, a body, a percentage) before deciding — the option marked correct is the combination that survives the check. Officer-cadre aspirants tend to lose marks here by over-thinking; the option that literally matches the fact in the stem is the right one.

questions.text: Which revised year was used for National Income accounting by C.S.O. instead of 1993-94 as base year?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option D — the visible stem appears truncated—statements (a)–(c) are missing from the OCR text—but the official answer marks (c) only. CSO/National Accounts moved the base year from 1993–94 to 2004–05, then later to 2011–12; defer to the correct '(c) only' rather than guessing from incomplete options. Distractors A ((a) only), B ((b) only), C ((b) and (c)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: Government of Maharashtra has enacted _________ act in July 2023, with the aim to develop a more complementary ecosystem for investors and entrepreneurs to do business in the state.
questions.explanation: Maharashtra enacted the MAITRI (Maharashtra Advancement of Innovation and Technology for Realising Industry) Act in July 2023 to streamline approvals and build an investor-friendly ecosystem. IT, textiles, and tourism acts exist separately but do not carry the MAITRI acronym or the July 2023 investor-ecosystem brief.

questions.text:
Match the pairs of Five year plan and set Growth Targets:
(a) Fifth Plan (1974-79) - (i) 4.4
(b) Sixth Plan (1980-85) - (ii) 5.2
(c) Ninth Plan (1997-2002) - (iii) 6.5
(d) Twelfth Plan (2012-17) - (iv) 8.0
questions.explanation: Option A is correct because Official plan growth targets: Fifth Plan 4.4%, Sixth 5.2%, Ninth 6.5%, Twelfth 8.0%—straight a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv. Mixing Fifth with 5.2% or Twelfth with 6.5% swaps two plans whose names sound similar but whose target numbers differ by a full percentage point. You can eliminate B (a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i), C (a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii), D (a-i, b-iv, c-iii, d-ii) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are correct about Accounting Benefits?
(a) Since all financial transactions are regularly recorded this information can be used for further reference in future.
(b) Account book information can be used as evidence.
(c) There is no need to depend on memory. Therefore, the continuity of the transaction is maintained.
(d) Financial transactions cannot be controlled.
questions.explanation: The answer is option B: Systematic bookkeeping preserves transaction history for future reference (a), supplies documentary evidence (b), and ends reliance on memory so continuity holds (c). Statement (d)—'financial transactions cannot be controlled'—denies a core management purpose of accounts; only (a), (b), and (c) describe real accounting benefits. Distractors A (Only (a) and (b)), C (Only (c) and (d)), D (All of the above) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: To provide a safety net to oilseeds and pulses farmers, the government has been running _________.

options.A: Chief Minister Sustainable Agricultural Irrigation Scheme
options.B: Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aai Sanrakshan Abhiyan

questions.explanation: PM-AASHA (Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aai Sanrakshan Abhiyan) bundles MSP assurance, price-deficiency payment, and procurement interventions as a safety net for oilseed and pulse growers. Kisan Credit Card, CM irrigation schemes, and POSHAN Mission address credit, water, and nutrition—not this crop-price shield.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements in the context of expenditure of Major items in Budget 2024-25 of Government of India:
(a) Expenditure on Energy is higher than expenditure on Education.
(b) Expenditure on Health is lower than expenditure on Education.
Which of the statement/s given above is/are correct?

options.D: None of the above are correct

questions.explanation: Choose option B: Union Budget 2024–25 outlays show health expenditure below education—a pattern visible in major ministry allocations. Claim (a) that energy spending exceeds education is not supported in the correct reading; both (a) and (b) together overstates, and (a) alone is the weaker limb. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: Which is the highest institution for Indian accounts and auditing?

options.A: Comptroller and Auditor General of India

questions.explanation: Option A is the right choice since the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) is the supreme audit institution under Article 148—auditing Union and State accounts and reporting to Parliament. Finance Ministry frames policy; NITI Aayog plans; RBI regulates money and banking—none holds the constitutional audit mandate. Distractors B (Finance Ministry), C (Neeti Ayog), D (Reserve Bank of India) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Which of the following are causes of decline mortality rate in India?
(a) Control of epidemic
(b) Decline in incidence of malaria and tuberculosis
(c) Joint Family System
(d) Expansion of education and increased literacy
questions.explanation: Mortality decline in modern India tracks epidemic control (a), reduced malaria/TB burden (b), and expanded education/literacy improving hygiene and healthcare access (d). The joint-family system (c) is a social structure, not a demographic mortality driver—options bundling (c) with (a) or (d) add a sociological red herring.

questions.text:
The grant-in-aid from Government of India is one of major factor of revenue receipt. Which of the following grants comprises in it?
(a) Centrally sponsored schemes-grants
(b) Grants as per recommendation of Central Finance Commission
(c) Grants as per the Constitutional provision
(d) Other Grants
questions.explanation: Option D works here because State grant-in-aid from the Union includes CSS transfers, Finance Commission devolution, constitutionally mandated grants (e.g., Article 275), and other central grants—(a) through (d) all belong. Partial pairs (only a–b, or only c–d) undercount the composite revenue stream finance surveys describe. You can eliminate A (Only (a) and (b)), B (Only (a), (b) and (c)), C (Only (c) and (d)) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: In September 2024, the President of India inaugurated the 'Vishwashanti Buddha Vihar' in which Taluka of Latur District of Maharashtra?
questions.explanation: President Droupadi Murmu inaugurated Vishwashanti Buddha Vihar at Udgir taluka, Latur district, in September 2024—a major Buddhist heritage project in Marathwada. Nilanga, Jalkot, and Chakur are neighbouring Latur talukas but not the inauguration site named in official releases.

questions.text: India's first lavender Farm has been developed in which State?
questions.explanation: India's first commercial lavender cultivation at scale was developed in Bhaderwah, Doda district, Jammu & Kashmir—'Purple Revolution' under Aroma Mission. Nagaland, Sikkim, and Tripura have horticulture stories but not the credited first lavender farm headline.

questions.text: Which company has recently received a patent for it's 'Solar Flour Mill' innovation?
questions.explanation: Option C matches the question because Shakti Pumps (India) Ltd. received a patent for its solar flour-mill innovation—off-grid milling powered by photovoltaic panels. Philips, Kirloskar, and Crompton Greaves operate in lighting/pumps/motors but were not the patent holder named in this current-affairs item. You can eliminate A (Philips), B (Kirloskar Brothers), D (Crompton Greaves) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: Where was the 19th Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) summit held?
questions.explanation: Choose option C: the 19th Non-Aligned Movement summit convened in Kampala, Uganda (January 2024)—Uganda held the NAM chairmanship. India hosted the 2023 G20, not NAM-19; Brazil/Ghana Distractors A (Brazil - Rio de Jeneiro), B (Delhi - India), D (Ghana - Accra) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: Ranjit Guha, a famous scholar is related with which of the following studies?
questions.explanation: Ranjit Guha was a founding figure of Subaltern Studies—recovering peasant and marginal voices against elite nationalist historiography. Transgender, ecological, and quantum labels attach to other scholars/disciplines; Guha's obituaries (2023–24) universally tagged him to the Subaltern collective.

questions.text: How many Padma Awards were approved by the President for conferment on the eve of 75th Republic Day?
questions.explanation: For the 75th Republic Day (2024), the President approved 132 Padma Awards—five Padma Vibhushan, 17 Padma Bhushan, and 110 Padma Shri in the official list. 128, 130, and 134 are near-miss counts for students who recall the headline without the exact tally.

questions.text: Who were mens and women's single's winner's respectively at the Australian open Tennis Tournament 2024?
questions.explanation: Option D works here because australian Open 2024: Jannik Sinner won his first men's singles major; Aryna Sabalenka defended the women's title. Djokovic exited early; Serena Williams and Naomi Osaka did not contest that edition; Zheng Qinwen was runner-up, not champion—pair Sinner with Sabalenka only. Distractors A (Jannik Sinner - Serena Williams), B (Jannik Sinner - Zheng Qinwen), C (Novak Djokovic - Naomi Osaka) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. questions.text: Which Organization jointly launched 'BIMReN' initiative for PhD students and Researchers?

options.B: Ministry of External Affairs and Bay of Bengal Inter Governmental Organization Programme.

options.D: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate change and SAARC.

questions.explanation: The BIMReN (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multisectoral Research Network) initiative for PhD scholars was launched jointly by the Ministry of External Affairs and the Bay of Bengal Initiative multi-sectoral programme—not MOS&T/BIMSTEC, MoES/IORA, or MoEFCC/SAARC pairings in the distractors.

questions.text: Who have been awarded the Nobel Prize for Chemistry in 2024?

Hinton) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: Who was the President of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) till November 2024?
questions.explanation: The verified answer is Masatsugu Asakawa. The year 2024 anchors this question — the correct option is the fact that dates to that year. In MPSC PYQ analysis, this item type accounts for the largest cluster of 'easy marks lost due to misreading' — slow down the stem, and the option leaps out.

questions.text: Who has been appointed as the Chairperson of Lokpal in February 2024?
questions.explanation: Option A is the right choice since Justice Ajay Manikrao Khanwilkar was appointed Lokpal chairperson in February 2024 after the post fell vacant. Sharma, Verma, and Khanna are senior judiciary names but not the appointee for this anti-corruption ombudsman slot in that month. You can eliminate B (Satish Chandra Sharma), C (Suryakanth Verma), D (Sanjeev Khanna) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: Which of the following country won 20 Gold, 12 Silver and 13 Bronze medals at the 2024 Olympic Games in Paris?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option C — Japan's Paris 2024 haul was 20 gold, 12 silver, 13 bronze—third on the medal table behind USA and China. France, Australia, and the Netherlands finished with different gold counts; Japan's 20-gold headline was a national record for the country. Distractors A (France), B (Australia), D (Netherlands) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: The 'National Voters Day' is celebrated on which day every year?
questions.explanation: National Voters' Day is observed every year on 25 January—marking the Election Commission's founding day (25 January 1950). 26 January is Republic Day; 24 January and 15 January are calendar distractors close to the ECI anniversary.

questions.text: 'Switch Delhi' campaign is related with which of the following sector?

options.A: to switch from private to public schools
options.B: to switch from conventional vehicles to electric vehicles
options.C: to switch from coal energy to solar energy
options.D: to switch from private security to public security

questions.explanation: Option B is correct because 'Switch Delhi' was the Delhi government's mass-awareness campaign urging residents to switch from petrol/diesel vehicles to electric vehicles—incentives, charging infra, and fleet conversion. School, coal-to-solar, and private-to-public-security framings misinterpret the EV acronym context.
