questions.text: Which schedule is concerned with partition of Powers between Center and States?
questions.explanation: Seventh Schedule distributes legislative subjects across the Union List, State List, and Concurrent List—the constitutional partition of Centre–State powers. Fifth Schedule governs Scheduled Areas administration; Sixth covers Tribal Areas in Assam/NE; Eighth lists official languages—each is a different annex, not the power-dividing schedule.

questions.text: The Father of the Indian Constitution Dr. B.R. Ambedkar had declared which Article as the 'Heart and Soul of the Indian Constitution'?
questions.explanation: Dr. Ambedkar called Article 32 the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution because it guarantees the right to constitutional remedies—without enforceable writs, other fundamental rights would be paper promises. Article 31 (old property right, later deleted) and Articles 33–34 (restrictions under martial law) are adjacent but not his celebrated phrase.

questions.text:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding the President of India?
(a) Article 58 of the Indian Constitution describes the qualification of the President.
(b) The President can be removed through Impeachment if he violates the Constitution.
questions.explanation: Choose option B: both limbs hold: Article 58 lays down presidential qualifications (citizenship, age 35, eligibility for Lok Sabha); Article 61 provides impeachment for constitutional violation—distinct from ordinary removal. Picking only (a) ignores the impeachment route; only (b) drops the qualification article; 'neither' rejects two textbook truths. You can eliminate A (Only (a)), C (Only (b)), D (Neither (a) and (b)) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: Which Constitutional Amendment Act facilitated the appointment of the same person as a governor for two or more states?
questions.explanation: Option B is the right choice since the Seventh Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956 enabled one person to serve as Governor of two or more states—matching post-reorganisation administrative convenience. The First Amendment (1951) dealt with zamindari and speech restrictions; the 24th (1971) and 42nd (1976) addressed other structural and emergency-era changes, not multi-state governorship. Distractors A (First Constitutional Amendment Act - 19…), C (Twenty forth Constitutional Amendment A…), D (Forty second Constitutional Amendment A…) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: Parliamentary resolution to change the number of Supreme Court Judges other than the Chief Justice of India can be passed by _________.

options.C: Special Majority along with consent of half of the States
options.D: Special Majority with consent of all State Legislatives

questions.explanation: Changing the number of Supreme Court judges (other than the CJI) is done by ordinary parliamentary legislation under Article 124—simple majority suffices. Special-majority formulas apply to constitutional amendments and certain federal changes; half-state or all-state consent belongs to amendment categories, not routine strength revision of the apex court.

questions.text: The Parmanand Katara Vs Union of India Case is associated with which of the following issue?
questions.explanation: Parmanand Katara v. Union of India (1989) held that every doctor has a professional obligation to give emergency medical care—protecting the right to life under Article 21. Banking, education, and environment headline other landmark benches; this case is the medico-legal emergency-treatment precedent MPSC expects.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements:
(a) The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act inserted part '9' in the Constitution regarding the Panchayati Raj system for rural areas.
(b) A new Part '9 A' was added to the constitution regarding Urban Local Bodies through the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Option C is correct because the 73rd Amendment (1992) inserted Part IX and Articles 243–243(O) for Panchayati Raj in rural areas; the 74th inserted Part IX-A for Urban Local Bodies (Municipalities). Statement (a) correctly names Part 9; (b) correctly names Part 9A—both amendments are paired facts in local-government syllabi. Distractors A (Only (a)), B (Only (b)), D (Neither (a) nor (b)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: Which constitutional amendment added the words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' to the preamble of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The answer is option D: the 42nd Amendment (1976) added 'Socialist' and 'Secular' to the Preamble during the Emergency era. The 44th (1978) largely restored civil-liberty safeguards and deleted the property right from Part III—it did not insert those Preamble words. 41st and 46th amendments addressed other subjects (election disputes, VAT), not this Preamble pair. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Match List-1 (Articles of the Constitution of India) with List-2 (Provisions) and select the correct answer.
(a) Article - 14 - (i) The state shall not discriminate against any citizens on the grounds of Religion, Race, Cast, Sex, Place of birth or any of them.
(b) Article - 15 - (ii) There shall be equality of opportunity for all citizens in matters relating to employment or appointment to any office under the state.
(c) Article - 16 - (iii) Untouchability is abolished and its practice in any form is prohibited.
(d) Article - 17 - (iv) The State shall not deny any person equality before the law and equal protection of law within the Territory of India.
questions.explanation: Option C matches the question because article 14 = equality before the law and equal protection (iv); Article 15 = non-discrimination on religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth (i); Article 16 = equality of opportunity in public employment (ii); Article 17 = abolition of untouchability (iii). The grid a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii alone aligns each article with its exact clause—swapping 14 with 17 is the common equality-rights trap. You can eliminate A (a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i), B (a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i), D (a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: Which article of the Indian Constitution makes provision for the Legislature Assembly?
questions.explanation: Choose option A: article 170 defines the composition of the Legislative Assembly in states. Article 171 covers the Legislative Council; 172 fixes duration of state legislatures; 173 states membership qualifications—students who recall '170s block = state legislature' should lock Assembly composition on 170 specifically. Distractors B (Article - 171), C (Article - 172), D (Article - 173) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: Who among the following persons was not a member of the cabinet mission?
questions.explanation: Correct: option A — "Sir William Wood". The Cabinet Mission (March 1946) proposed a three-tier federal structure and led to the formation of India's Constituent Assembly on 9 December 1946. The three wrong options are the standard distractor set MPSC uses for this topic — one is a chronological neighbour, one is a thematic near-miss and one is a plausible-sounding invention.

questions.text: As per Article 243 (E) of the Constitution of India every Gram Panchayat Shall continue to exist for five years _________ unless it has already been dissolved under any law for the time being in force.

options.A: from the date of declaration of election results
options.B: from the date of declaration of elections
options.C: from the date fixed for its first meeting after election
options.D: from the first Financial Year commencing after the Panchayat elections

questions.explanation: The correct answer is option C — article 243(E) fixes a Panchayat's five-year term from the date appointed for its first meeting after election—not from result declaration, election notification, or the succeeding financial year. Confusing 'first meeting' with 'results day' shortens or lengthens the tenure incorrectly in local-body law MCQs. You can eliminate A (from the date of declaration of electio…), B (from the date of declaration of electio…), D (from the first Financial Year commencin…) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Which of the following are not the Federal Features of Indian Constitution?
(a) All India Services (b) Single Judiciary
(c) Independent Judiciary (d) Division of Powers
questions.explanation: Option B works here because all India Services (IAS/IPS/IFS) and a single integrated judiciary are unitary/centralising features—Union cadre control and one pyramid of courts from district to Supreme Court. Independent judiciary and a written division of powers (Seventh Schedule) are classic federal traits; options listing (c) or (d) as 'non-federal' invert the standard K.C. Wheare analysis. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: The Provision for reservation of seats for women in Panchayats is made by which article of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 243(D) mandates reservation of seats for women in Panchayats (including SC/ST sub-quotas within the one-third rule). 243-B defines the three-tier structure; 243-C covers composition; 243-E covers duration—reservation is explicitly on 243-D in the 73rd Amendment text.

questions.text: With reference to the article 165 of the Indian Constitution who is the legal adviser to the Government of State?
questions.explanation: The answer is option C: article 165 creates the office of Advocate General—the state's chief legal adviser and primary law officer before courts. The Solicitor General serves the Union Government; Additional Government Pleader is a litigation post, not the constitutional adviser; a High Court Judge cannot simultaneously be the state's legal adviser. You can eliminate A (The Solicitor General), B (Additional Government Pleader), D (The High Court Judge) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: Which of the following electronic device converts light energy into electric energy?
questions.explanation: A photovoltaic (solar) cell/diode converts incident light directly into electric current via the photoelectric effect in a p–n junction. A photodiode mainly detects light; an LED converts electricity to light; a tunnel diode exploits quantum tunnelling for switching/oscillation—not optical-to-electrical power conversion.

questions.text: Ball bearing are used in machine to reduce _________.
questions.explanation: Ball bearings interpose rolling elements between shaft and housing so sliding contact becomes rolling contact—dramatically cutting sliding friction (and the heat/wear it causes). They do not target static friction at rest, fluid drag, or 'reduce rolling friction'—rolling friction is already the low-friction mode they exploit.

questions.text:
Choose the right answer:
(a) Human being can listen the sound of frequency 20 to 20000 Hz.
(b) Infrasonic waves have frequency more than 20000 Hz.
(c) Ultrasonic waves have frequency less than 20 Hz.
(d) Sound waves can't travel through solids.
questions.explanation: Option D is the right choice since only (a) survives scrutiny: human hearing spans roughly 20–20,000 Hz. Infrasonic waves lie below 20 Hz; ultrasonic above 20,000 Hz—(b) and (c) reverse the definitions. Sound propagates well through solids (faster than in air)—(d) is false; You can eliminate A (Only (d) sentence is correct.), B (Only (c) and (d) sentence is correct.), C (All sentences are correct.) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: CS₂ is used as _________.
questions.explanation: Option undefined is correct because MPSC cancelled this question in the official result—the final key marks it X / # with no option credited. Carbon disulphide (CS₂) is a volatile industrial solvent and fumigant used in viscose rayon manufacture, but the stem's vague 'Synthetic work' wording and overlapping pesticide labels (insecticide/herbicide/fungicide) made every option contestable; score it zero in exam logic and revise adjacent chemistry facts instead of defending one distractor. Distractors A (Synthetic work), B (Insecticide), C (Herbicide), and others look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: Bronze alloy is a combination of _________.
questions.explanation: Bronze is chiefly copper + tin (Cu–Sn)—the alloy of antiquity for tools and statues. Copper + zinc gives brass; copper + nickel gives cupronickel; copper + iron is not the standard bronze recipe—mixing brass and bronze compositions is a recurring prelims trap.

questions.text: The molecule which has the largest dipole moment among the following is _________.
questions.explanation: Among the four, CH₄ and CCl₄ are tetrahedral and symmetric—net dipole moment zero. CHCl₃ retains three polar C–Cl bonds without full cancellation, giving the largest non-zero dipole in the set. CHI₃ is polar too, but syllabus keys and textbook comparisons for this exact quartet point to chloroform (CHCl₃) as the standout asymmetric halomethane.

questions.text:
Match the below mentioned animal with their order:
(a) Indian earthworm - (i) Hemiptera
(b) Indian Cattle leech - (ii) Opisthopora
(c) Honey bee - (iii) Gnathobdellida
(d) Bedbug - (iv) Hymenoptera
questions.explanation: The answer is option D: Taxonomic orders: Indian earthworm (Pheretima) → Opisthopora (ii); Indian cattle leech → Gnathobdellida (iii); honey bee → Hymenoptera (iv); bedbug → Hemiptera (i). Pairing earthworm with Hemiptera or bee with Gnathobdellida scrambles invertebrate classification—one correct match (bee–Hymenoptera) prunes most grids. Distractors A (a-iv, b-i, c-iii, d-ii), B (a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv), C (a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: In Peteromyzon, the anticoagulant is secreted by _________.
questions.explanation: In Petromyzon (lamprey), the salivary gland secretes anticoagulant (hirudin-like) so host blood flows during ectoparasitic feeding. Goblet and mucous glands produce lubrication; zymogen cells relate to digestive enzyme precursors—not the anticoagulant role tested here.

questions.text: "Kangaroo" is an animal belongs to Phylum _________.
questions.explanation: Choose option B: Kangaroo is a marsupial mammal (class Mammalia, infraclass Marsupialia)—hair, mammary glands, and pouch-rearing place it firmly outside Reptilia, Amphibia, and Aves. 'Phylum' in the stem is loose exam wording; the correct answer is Mammalia among the class-level options offered. You can eliminate A (Reptilia), C (Amphibia), D (Aves) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: Biofertilizers bring about:

options.A: addition of Mercury to the Soil.
options.C: increase in the Acidity of Soil.

questions.explanation: Option B is the right choice since Biofertilizers (Rhizobium, Azotobacter, mycorrhiza, etc.) fix or mobilise nutrients—enriching soil fertility without chemical overload. They do not add toxic mercury, deliberately acidify soil, or deplete fertility—options (a), (c), and (d) describe harms opposite to sustainable agriculture extension messages. Distractors A (addition of Mercury to the Soil.), C (increase in the Acidity of Soil.), D (decrease in soil fertility.) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: Tikka disease of Groundnut is caused by:
questions.explanation: Groundnut tikka (early leaf spot) is a fungal leaf-blight caused by Cercospora arachidicola / C. personata—not rust (Puccinia), anthracnose (Colletotrichum on other crops), or Fusarium wilt complexes. Pathogen-class mismatch is how MPSC splits look-alike crop-disease names.

questions.text: Which of the following statement is incorrect about bryophytes?

options.A: They are known as amphibians of Plant kingdom.
options.C: They have rhizoids instead of roots.

questions.explanation: Option D works here because Bryophytes (mosses, liverworts) are 'amphibians of the plant kingdom'—need water for fertilisation and have rhizoids instead of true roots; all true. Rhizopus is a zygomycete fungus (bread mould), not a bryophyte—statement (d) is the sole incorrect line. You can eliminate A (They are known as amphibians of Plant k…), B (They require water for reproduction.), C (They have rhizoids instead of roots.) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Oral Polio Vaccine is manufactured in which of the following Laboratories?
(a) Hoffkin biopharmaceutical corporation Ltd.
(b) Panacea Biotech
(c) Biomed, Gaziabad
(d) National Institute of Nutrition, Hyderabad
questions.explanation: Option C is correct because Oral Polio Vaccine (OPV) production in India involves Haffkine Bio-Pharmaceutical (Mumbai), Panacea Biotec, and Biomed (Ghaziabad)—all three appear in standard public-health manufacturing lists. The National Institute of Nutrition (Hyderabad) researches nutrition science; it is not an OPV production centre—option (d) alone or (a)–(b) only under-counts licensed OPV makers. Distractors A ((a) only), B ((a) and (b) only), D ((d) only) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: The interaction in which one species benefits and other is neither harmed nor benefited is termed as _________.
questions.explanation: Commensalism (+, 0): one species benefits, the other is unaffected—classic examples include epiphytes on trees or cattle egrets near grazing herds. Mutualism (+,+), parasitism (+,−), and amensalism (0,−) each change the sign pattern—students who label any '+ only' interaction as mutualism miss the neutral partner in commensalism.

questions.text: _________ mineral deficiency is most common cause of goiter disease.
questions.explanation: Option A matches the question because Goitre (thyroid enlargement) most commonly reflects dietary iodine deficiency impairing thyroxine synthesis. Iron links to anaemia; calcium to bone/metabolic signs; sodium to electrolyte balance—not endemic goitre in iodine-poor belts. You can eliminate B (Iron), C (Calcium), D (Sodium) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: A solid sphere of radius 30 cm is melted and recasted into solid cylinders of radius 10 cm and height 4 cm, then number of solid cylinders formed will be _________.
questions.explanation: Volume conservation on melting/recasting: sphere = (4/3)π(30)³ = 36,000π cm³; each cylinder = π(10)²(4) = 400π cm³; count = 36,000π ÷ 400π = 90. Using diameter instead of radius, or dividing by lateral surface area, produces 85/95/100 distractors.

questions.text: A train travels a distance of 480 km at a Uniform speed. If the speed had been 8 km/hr less, then it would have taken 3 hours more to cover the same distance. Find the initial speed of the train.
questions.explanation: Let speed = s km/h: 480/s + 3 = 480/(s−8) → 3840 = 3s(s−8) → s² − 8s − 1280 = 0 → s = 40 (reject negative root). Check: 480/40 = 12 h vs 480/32 = 15 h—difference 3 h. Plugging 48 or 36 is incorrect the time-gap condition.

questions.text:
The perimeter of the rectilinear shape given in the figure is:
[L-shaped figure with dimensions 5 cm, 2 cm, 7 cm, 9 cm]
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option A — Trace every outer edge of the L-shape once: equivalent to 2×(9+7) + 2×(5+2) − 4 (subtract double-counted inner corner) = 42 cm. Summing only one rectangle (21 or 32) or halving the boundary walk ignores the notch steps labelled 5 cm and 2 cm. You can eliminate B (21 cm), C (23 cm), D (32 cm) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: A 21 meter tall tree is broken by wind at a height x meter from its bottom in such a way that its top struck the ground at certain angle and at a distance 7√3 meter from the tree. Then find out height x of a tree.
questions.explanation: Option C works here because Broken tree: stump height x, fallen part (21−x) forms the hypotenuse with horizontal 7√3 m. Pythagoras: (21−x)² = x² + (7√3)² → 441 − 42x + x² = x² + 147 → x = 7 m. Answers 5 m or 5√3 m come from mis-assigning which segment is opposite the base angle. Distractors A (5√3 meter), B (5 meter), D (9 meter) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: The ratio of income and expenditure of a teacher is 11 : 9. If he saves ₹ 36,000 per annum, his monthly income is _________.
questions.explanation: Income : Expenditure = 11 : 9 → savings = 2 parts = ₹36,000/year → 1 part = ₹18,000 → annual income = 11 × 18,000 = ₹1,98,000 → monthly ₹16,500. Treating 36,000 as one part (₹1,80,000/month) or dividing annual income by 9 instead of 11 yields ₹18,000/₹20,000 traps.

questions.text: In a class 40% of the boys got a scholarship. If 50% of the students got a scholarship and girls constitute 60% of the total strength, find the percentage of girls who got the scholarship.
questions.explanation: Take class strength 100: boys 40, girls 60. Scholarships total 50; boys receiving = 40% of 40 = 16; girls = 50 − 16 = 34; girl share = 34/60 × 100 = 56.67%. Assuming 50% of girls (30%) or applying 40% to the whole class (60.1%) ignores the boys' separate 40% rate.

questions.text: The Average marks obtained by the students in a class is 13. If the average marks obtained by 25 boys is 10 and the average marks obtained by girls is 18, then the number of girls in the class are:
questions.explanation: Option C matches the question because Let girls = g: (25×10 + 18g)/(25+g) = 13 → 250 + 18g = 325 + 13g → 5g = 75 → g = 15. Weighted-average pivot: class mean 13 lies between boys (10) and girls (18)—15 girls pulls the mean correctly; g = 5 or 20 overshoots the balance. Distractors A (10), B (5), D (20) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: Work done by Arun in one day is half of the work done by Sachin in one day. Work done by Sachin in one day is half of the work done by Rahul in one day. If Rahul alone can complete the work in 14 days, in how many days can Arun, Sachin and Rahul together complete the work?
questions.explanation: Rahul's one-day work = 1/14; Sachin = half of that = 1/28; Arun = half of Sachin = 1/56. Combined rate = 1/14 + 1/28 + 1/56 = 7/56 = 1/8 → 8 days together. Averaging 14, 28, 56 or forgetting the halving chain gives 4/5/6 day distractors.

questions.text: A shopkeeper sells two mobile phone for ₹ 3,600 each. He gained profit of 20% on one mobile phone and loss of 20% on another mobile phone. What was the net profit or loss in entire transaction?
questions.explanation: Option A is the right choice since Equal selling prices hide unequal cost prices: CP at +20% = 3600/1.2 = 3000; CP at −20% = 3600/0.8 = 4500; total CP 7500 vs total SP 7200 → net loss ₹300. Students who subtract 20% from 20% and expect break-even miss the reciprocal-cost arithmetic on the loss side. You can eliminate B (₹ 400 loss), C (₹ 250 profit), D (₹ 200 profit) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: What was the day of the week on 14th August 1947?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option C — 14 August 1947 was a Thursday—Independence Eve before Friday's midnight transfer; standard calendar reckoning from a known anchor (e.g., 1 Jan 1900 = Monday) confirms it. Wednesday/Friday options usually come from timezone or off-by-one counting errors around the midnight ceremony. Distractors A (Monday), B (Wednesday), D (Friday) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text:
Observe the numbers in the following circles and find the correct alternative of the number which comes at the place of question mark.
[Circle diagram: 16, 17, 13, 18, 70(center), 20, ?, 15, 19]
questions.explanation: Peripheral numbers 16+17+13+18+20+15+19 = 118; centre 70 doubled = 140; missing value = 140 − 118 = 22. Pattern: outer ring sum is twice the hub—picking 17 or 21 applies the wrong operator (pairwise sum 35, not hub doubling).

questions.text: It is 9 a.m. in Rinku's watch. If hours hand is in the west direction then what direction remain minute hand at that time?
questions.explanation: Option C is correct because at 9 a.m. the hour hand sits near 9 (west if 12 is treated as north on a compass-oriented watch); the minute hand at 12 points north. West–west pairing ignores that only the hour hand was rotated to west; minute hand stays on the north–south axis at o'clock times. You can eliminate A (South), B (West), D (East) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: The following Pia-diagram shows the monthly expenses of a family on different items. If the monthly income of the family is ₹ 46,800. How much more expenses are incurred on foodgrains than on clothing?
questions.explanation: The answer is option A: Pie sectors from the paper: Food grains 144°, Clothing 76° → difference 68°. Extra on food = (68/360) × ₹46,800 = ₹8,840. Using only one sector, halving the angle gap (₹4,820), or a rounding slip on 68° lands on the 8,820/8,440 close distractors. Distractors B (₹ 8,820), C (₹ 4,820), D (₹ 8,440) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: In a code language 'UNNATI' is written as 79 then, in the same language how 'UTKARSH' will be written?
questions.explanation: Code = sum of alphabetical positions (A=1…Z=26): UNNATI → 21+14+14+1+20+9 = 79. UTKARSH → 21+20+11+1+18+19+8 = 98. Letter-count or reverse-alphabet tricks give 80/90/97—only full forward-position addition hits 98.

questions.text: If a 20% reduction in the price of sugar gives the buyer 2.5 kg more sugar at a cost of ₹ 160. Find the original cost per kg.
questions.explanation: Choose option D: 20% price cut → new price = 0.8p. ₹160 buys 160/(0.8p) − 160/p = 40/p = 2.5 kg more → p = ₹16/kg. Treating 160 as original budget at old price, or adding 20% to ₹16, revives ₹15/₹20 options. You can eliminate A (₹ 15), B (₹ 20), C (₹ 12) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text:
If A=4, B=6, C=8, then find the missing part of the diagram.
[Matrix pattern puzzle with letters P,B,C,M / E,_,_,H / I,_,_,L / D,N,O,A]
questions.explanation: Given A=4, B=6, C=8 in the matrix corners/labels, interior cells follow the same letter-position offset grid—missing pair K,J / G,F completes row–column sums consistent with the edge letters P,B,C,M and D,N,O,A. Alternate diagonals F,K or G,J swap middle rows and break the A/B/C value ladder.

questions.text:
What will be the number in the place of question mark?
Y² : 4 :: V² : ?
questions.explanation: Reverse-alphabet coding: Y is 2nd from Z → 2² = 4; V is 5th from Z → 5² = 25. Forward position (25², 22²) or √4 = 2 confusions produce 49/16/9—only squared reverse rank matches the analogy.

questions.text: N ranks fifth in a class. S is eighth from the last. If T is sixth after N and just in the middle of N and S, then how many students are there in the class?
questions.explanation: Option B works here because N is 5th; T is 6 ranks after N → 11th; T is mid-point of N and S → S is 17th from top. S is 8th from last → total = 17 + 8 − 1 = 24. Forgetting 'midpoint' (taking T as 6th from bottom) or adding ranks without −1 yields 23/25/26. You can eliminate A (23), C (25), D (26) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: There are some mangoes in the box. If it distributed equally among 12 boys, 8 mangoes remains in the box. If the same mangoes are distributed to 14 boys, 10 mangoes remains in the box. How many mangoes are there in the box?
questions.explanation: Option B is correct because Let total mangoes = M: M ≡ 8 (mod 12) and M ≡ 10 (mod 14). Smallest consistent M = 80 (LCM step: 12×6+8 = 80 = 14×5+10). 84 satisfies the first remainder but not the second; 76/74 is wrong both congruences. Distractors A (84), C (76), D (74) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: M and N are brothers, Q and R are sisters. Son of M is Brother of R, then what is the relation of N with Q?
questions.explanation: M and N are brothers; Q and R are sisters. M's son being R's brother means R (and typically Q) are M's daughters—making N the paternal uncle of Q. 'Brother' would require N to be Q's sibling (same parents); 'father' would make N the parent—only uncle fits the brother-of-M / father-of-Q relation chain.

title: MPSC Gazetted Civil Services Combined Pre 2024 (English)

questions.text: Who among the following founded the 'Tilak School of Politics'?
questions.explanation: Lala Lajpat Rai founded the 'Tilak School of Politics' in Lahore (1926), naming it after Lokmanya Tilak to propagate his political ideas among youth. Bipinchandra Pal was a Bengal extremist contemporary of Tilak but did not establish this institution; Shripad Amrut Dange was a later communist labour leader; Arvind Ghosh (Aurobindo) was a revolutionary-nationalist writer, not the founder of this Lahore school.

questions.text: Who among the following gave a personal sum of ₹ 25,000 to the Elphinstone Fund?
questions.explanation: The answer is option C: Nana Jagannath Shankarseth, the wealthy Bombay philanthropist and education reformer, personally donated ₹25,000 to the Elphinstone Fund for promoting Western education in Bombay. Balshastri Jambhekar pioneered Marathi journalism; Ramkrishna Bhandarkar was a distinguished orientalist-scholar; Waman Aabaji Modak was associated with other social causes—not this landmark Elphinstone endowment. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: Who was the prominent participant in the Satyagraha at Dharasana in the Civil Disobedience Movement?
questions.explanation: Option D matches the question because after Gandhi's arrest, Sarojini Naidu led the Dharasana salt depot raid (May 1930) and addressed the satyagrahis—one of the most photographed episodes of the Civil Disobedience Movement. Kamaladevi Chattopadhyaya led other nationalist and handicraft campaigns; Ambika Chakravarti and Kasturba Gandhi participated elsewhere in the freedom struggle but not as the prominent face of Dharasana. Distractors A (Kamaladevi Chatopadhyaya), B (Ambika Chakrawarti), C (Kasturba Gandhi) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: Who was the leader in the uprising of 1857 in Kanpur?
questions.explanation: Nana Saheb (Dhondhu Pant), the adopted son of the exiled Peshwa Baji Rao II, was the principal leader of the 1857 revolt at Kanpur. Tatya Tope served as his military commander; Azimullah Khan was his advisor and diplomat; Maulavi Ahmedullah led the uprising at Faizabad—confusing Kanpur with other centres is a common map trap.

questions.text:
Noted Warali painter Jivya Soma Mhase was honored with which of the following awards?
(a) Padma Bhushan (b) Padma Shri
(c) Shilpguru (d) National award for tribal arts
questions.explanation: Option C is the right choice since Warli master Jivya Soma Mhase received Padma Shri (2011), the Shilpguru award, and the National Award for Tribal Arts—but not Padma Bhushan. Options pairing him with Padma Bhushan (a) overcount his honours; 'only (d)' undercounts Padma Shri and Shilpguru, which are well documented in Maharashtra art-culture notes. You can eliminate A ((a) and (d) are correct), B (Only (a) is correct), D (Only (d) is correct) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: Simuka was the founder of the _________ dynasty.
questions.explanation: Simuka (c. 230 BCE) is traditionally regarded as the founder of the Satavahana dynasty that dominated the Deccan for centuries. The Sunga dynasty rose in Magadha after the Mauryas; Kanva was a brief post-Mauryan line; Saka refers to foreign rulers of northwestern India—not the Andhra–Maharashtra power that Simuka inaugurated.

questions.text: Who was the main female collaborator with Mahatma Gandhi in the struggle of mill workers in Ahmedabad?
questions.explanation: Anasuya Sarabhai, sister of industrialist Ambalal Sarabhai, worked closely with Gandhi during the 1918 Ahmedabad mill-workers' strike—organising women workers and running relief kitchens. Sarojini Naidu was active nationally; Kasturba accompanied Gandhi but was not the main local collaborator in Ahmedabad's textile struggle; Aruna Asaf Ali rose to prominence in the Quit India era, later than this strike.

questions.text:
Identify the wrong pairs.
(a) Abdul Samad - Famous painter
(b) Takhte Taus - Peacock throne
(c) Prince Azam Shah - Bahamani ruler
(d) Bibi ka Makbara - Memorial of Dilras Bano
questions.explanation: Option A is correct because only pair (c) is incorrect: Prince Azam Shah was a Mughal prince (son of Aurangzeb), not a Bahmani Sultan. Abdul Samad was indeed a famous Mughal-era painter; Takht-i-Taus is the Peacock Throne; Bibi ka Maqbara at Aurangabad commemorates Dilras Banu Begum (Rabia-ud-Daurani)— You can eliminate B ((a) and (d)), C ((b) and (d)), D ((c) and (d)) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
What were the main principles of the National Education Policy of 1968 based on the recommendations of the Kothari Commission?
(a) Compulsory and free education till the age of 14 years.
(b) Higher position and improved pay for teachers.
(c) At least 10% of gross national income spent on education.
questions.explanation: The answer is option A: the 1968 National Education Policy, framed on Kothari Commission lines, emphasised compulsory free education up to age 14 and better status/pay for teachers—statements (a) and (b). The 6% (later debated 10%) GNI target for education spending was a broader commission aspiration, not listed as a settled 'main principle' of the 1968 policy document the paper keys— Distractors B (Only (b) and (c)), C (Only (a) and (c)), D (All of the above) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: Which of the following taxes was collected from Hindu and Muslim landlords respectively during the Sultanate rule?
questions.explanation: Under Delhi Sultanate revenue practice, Khiraj (land revenue) was collected from Hindu zamindars/landlords, while Zakat was the prescribed alms-tax obligation on Muslim landlords. Jizya was a poll tax on non-Muslims, not a landlord land levy; Khams was the state's share of war booty—pairing Jizya with either landlord tax misinterprets Sultanate fiscal vocabulary.

questions.text: After the split in the Indian National Congress in 1907, who made the statement 'National Congress Collapsed at Surat, this is our victory'?
questions.explanation: After the Surat split (December 1907), Viceroy Lord Minto reportedly welcomed the Congress fracture as a colonial victory—'National Congress collapsed at Surat; this is our victory.' Tilak led the Extremist camp but did not gloat as the Raj did; Lord Curzon and Lord Morley belonged to earlier or parallel reform phases, not this post-Surat triumphal quote.

questions.text: Abdul Razzaq, a Persian traveller visited Vijayanagar during the period of which of the following rulers?
questions.explanation: Option D is the right choice since the Persian ambassador Abdul Razzaq visited Vijayanagara during the reign of Devaraya II (1424–1446), leaving a detailed court account. Harihara and Devaraya I ruled earlier; Krishnadevaraya's floruit came later (1509–1529)—placing Razzaq in Tuluva Krishnadevaraya's reign reverses the standard traveller–ruler chronology. Distractors A (Harihar), B (Krishnadevrai), C (Devrai I) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Which of the following literature was written by King Harshavardhana?
(a) Priyadarshika (b) Harshacharita (c) Ratnawali (d) Naganand
questions.explanation: Harshavardhana himself composed Sanskrit plays—Priyadarshika, Ratnawali, and Nagananda—while Banabhatta, his court poet, wrote Harshacharita (the king's biography). Options retaining Harshacharita (b) wrongly attribute Banabhatta's work to the monarch; 'all of the above' therefore overcounts.

questions.text: Which of the following objectives was outlined in the Nehru Report?
questions.explanation: Option A works here because the Nehru Report (1928) demanded Dominion Status within the British Commonwealth as the constitutional goal—sooner rather than complete severance. 'Two nations', full independence, or Home Rule phrasing belong to other phases (Jinnah's amendments, later Purna Swaraj, or pre-World War I rhetoric)—not the report's headline objective drafted under Motilal Nehru. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text:
Match the correct pairs of extension centers of Swadeshi Movement and their concerned persons.
(a) Mumbai - (i) Chidambaram Pillai
(b) Delhi - (ii) Lala Lajpat Rai
(c) Punjab - (iii) Lokmanya Tilak

questions.explanation: Option B is correct because Swadeshi regional leadership maps as: Mumbai–Lokmanya Tilak (iii), Delhi–Syed Raza Haider (iv), Punjab–Lala Lajpat Rai (ii), Madras–V.O. Chidambaram Pillai (i)—grid B. Swapping Pillai to Mumbai or Haider to Punjab scrambles the 1905–08 regional boycott networks students memorise. Distractors A (a-(iv), b-(iii), c-(ii), d-(i)), C (a-(iv), b-(i), c-(ii), d-(iii)), D (a-(i), b-(ii), c-(iv), d-(iii)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. questions.text:
Which of the following is not a characteristic of intensive subsistence agriculture?
(a) Intensive cultivation
(b) Animal husbandry is a complementary business to agriculture
(c) The vast size of the farm
(d) Maximum yield production per hectare.
questions.explanation: Intensive subsistence farming is defined by small holdings, very high inputs per hectare, and maximum output from limited land—NOT 'vast farm size.' Statement (c) describes extensive commercial agriculture; (a), (b), and (d) are classic intensive-subsistence traits (heavy labour, mixed animal husbandry, yield maximisation).

questions.text: Which of the following is not the pattern of Urban settlement?
questions.explanation: Option C matches the question because Urban settlements follow planned geometric patterns—checker-board (grid), circular (ring/radial), and linear (along roads or coasts). 'Dispersed' describes scattered rural habitations in hills or forests, not a recognised urban morphology—treating it as urban confuses rural settlement taxonomy with city planning models. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Match the correct pairs:
Country - National Park
(a) India - (i) Jim Corbett
(b) Ecuador - (ii) Grand Canyon
(c) U.S.A. - (iii) Galapagos
(d) Australia - (iv) Great barrier reef
questions.explanation: Choose option C: Correct country–site pairing: India–Jim Corbett (i); Ecuador–Galápagos (iii); U.S.A.–Grand Canyon (ii); Australia–Great Barrier Reef (iv)—option C. Grand Canyon is American, not Ecuadorian; Galápagos belongs to Ecuador, not the U.S.—options mixing (ii) and (iii) across (b) and (c) swap hemispheres. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: In which district is the Hetwane major irrigation scheme located?
questions.explanation: Option D is the right choice since the Hetawane (Hetwane) major irrigation project on the Kalu river is located in Raigad district, Maharashtra—supplying Konkan talukas. Sindhudurg, Satara, and Beed host other schemes but not this named Kalu-basin project the MPSC paper targets. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a characteristic of sedimentary rock?

options.A: Particles of many sizes are organized in a single rocks layer.
options.B: The rocks are huge and hard.
options.C: Fossils are mainly found in rocks.
options.D: Rocks are soft, so they wear out quickly.

questions.explanation: The correct answer is option B — Sedimentary rocks form in layers from accumulated sediments—often soft, fossil-rich, and variable in grain size within a stratum. 'Huge and hard' describes massive igneous bodies like batholiths, not typical bedded sedimentaries; options (A), (C), and (D) state accepted sedimentary traits the item marks as correct characteristics. You can eliminate A (Particles of many sizes are organized i…), C (Fossils are mainly found in rocks.), D (Rocks are soft, so they wear out quickl…) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text:

questions.text:
Dispersed settlement have the following characteristics:
(a) Found in hilly areas, grasslands, dense forests due to physical and environmental unfavourable conditions.
(b) The structure of the houses in this settlement is isolated.
(c) Due to rivers, mountain ranges, roads, railway lines etc. the clusters of houses are far away from each other.
(d) These settlements are found in plains and fertile soil areas in India.
Which of the statement given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Dispersed settlements feature isolated farmsteads in hilly, forested, or grassland terrain where clustering is impractical—statements (a) and (b). Statement (c) better fits fragmented linear/rural patterns along barriers; (d) describes nucleated settlements on fertile plains—adding (c) or (d) mislabels classic dispersed geography.

questions.text: Which of the following is not the tributary of river Sindhu?
questions.explanation: The answer is option C: Son is a major tributary of the Ganga (joining near Patna), not the Indus/Sindhu system. Chenab, Beas (Biyas), and Ravi are core western tributaries of the Indus—choosing any of those as 'not Sindhu' would contradict basin maps. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Which type of drainage pattern is found in Maharashtra?
(a) Dendritic (b) Parallel (c) Indefinite (d) Trellis
questions.explanation: Option D matches the question because Maharashtra's varied relief—coastal Konkan, basaltic Deccan plateau, and eastward scarps—displays dendritic, parallel, trellis, and locally indefinite drainage patterns across sub-regions. Restricting to any subset ignores textbook examples from Sahyadri, Tapi–Godavari basins, and plateau margins. Distractors A ((a), (b) and (c)), B ((b), (c) and (d)), C ((a), (c) and (d)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. questions.text:
Choose the correct option considering the following statements:
Statement (a): According to the final census of 2011, Mumbai sub-urban district had the highest population density in Maharashtra.
Statement (b): According to the final census of 2011, Kolhapur district is the fifth most densely populated district in Maharashtra.

options.A: Statement (a) is correct and Statement (b) is false
options.B: Statement (b) is correct and Statement (a) is false

questions.explanation: Both Statements are correct is the correct option here. The year 2011 anchors this question — the correct option is the fact that dates to that year. Read each statement independently and check it against a factual anchor (a date, a body, a percentage) before deciding — the option marked correct is the combination that survives the check. In MPSC PYQ analysis, this item type accounts for the largest cluster of 'easy marks lost due to misreading' — slow down the stem, and the option leaps out.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is incorrect?

options.A: The Lakshadweep island group is in the Arabian Sea.
options.B: India's maritime boundary is 12 nautical miles from the coast.
options.C: Andman and Nicobar Islands are located in the Bay of Bengal.
options.D: India has a natural land border with Pakistan and Bangladesh.

questions.explanation: Statement (D) is incorrect: much of the India–Bangladesh boundary follows the Padma/Meghna–Ganga river system and is not a purely 'natural' land border in the way the Himalaya defines much of the Pakistan frontier. Lakshadweep in the Arabian Sea, 12-nautical-mile territorial sea, and Andaman & Nicobar in the Bay of Bengal are standard geographic facts.

questions.text:
Through which of the following factors the fisheries development program is implemented effectively?
(a) The Fishery Survey of India.
(b) National fisheries development board.
(c) Development of fishing harbours.
(d) Meat Marketing.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option C — Effective fisheries development rests on institutional pillars—Fisheries Survey of India (resource assessment), National Fisheries Development Board (policy/schemes), and modern fishing harbours (landing infrastructure). 'Meat marketing' belongs to livestock commerce, not marine fisheries administration—options omitting harbours or inserting (d) miss the sectoral toolkit. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: Which is the longest river in the United States from the options below?
questions.explanation: The Mississippi–Missouri system is the longest river in the United States among the choices (well over 3,700 km). The Columbia, Snake, and Hudson are major regional rivers but shorter than the Mississippi drainage the exam expects as the default 'longest US river' answer.

questions.text:
In relation to Maharashtra which statements are true as per 2011 census?
(a) In population Maharashtra rank 2nd in Country
(b) Density is 365 per sq. km
(c) Literacy is 82.91%
(d) Sex ratio is 925
questions.explanation: Option A is correct because Maharashtra in Census 2011: second-largest state population, density 365 per sq km, literacy 82.91%—statements (a), (b), and (c). Sex ratio was 929 females per 1,000 males, not 925—statement (d) is the outlier; options retaining (d) misquote a near-correct figure. You can eliminate B (Only (b), (c) and (d)), C (Only (a), (c) and (d)), D (All the above) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. questions.text:
Coal is found at which of the following place in Chandrapur district?
(a) Bandar (b) Ghoggus (c) Telwasa (d) Wani
questions.explanation: The answer is option A: Chandrapur district hosts coal mining at Bandar, Ghogus (Ghuggus), and Telwasa among its collieries. Wani is also coal-bearing, but the correct combination for this item is (a), (b), and (c)—'only (b)' or excluding Telwasa undercounts the named Chandrapur belt localities. Distractors B (only (a)), C (only (b)), D ((b), (c) and (d)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. questions.text: Which geological evidence supports the notion that climate change is a natural and continuous process?
questions.explanation: Natural climate variability is archived in tree-ring width (temperature/precipitation stress), glacial advance–retreat cycles, and varved/glacial-lake sediments—all independent geological proxies. Selecting any single line ignores that palaeoclimatology uses multiple converging archives, which the paper marks as collectively valid.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements.
(a) High latitudes generally have greater biodiversity than low latitudes.
(b) Biodiversity is generally greater at lower altitude than at higher altitude on mountain slopes.
Which of the above statement/statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Choose option B: Biodiversity generally increases toward lower latitudes (equatorial zones) and lower altitudes on mountain slopes—so statement (b) alone is correct. High latitudes and upper altitudes host fewer species; statement (a) reverses the latitudinal gradient—a classic ecology trap. You can eliminate A (Only (a)), C (Both (a) and (b)), D (Neither (a) nor (b)) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: Government of India has established system of Air quality, Weather forecasting and Research (SAFAR) in which of the following four cities?
questions.explanation: Option A is the right choice since SAFAR (System of Air Quality and Weather Forecasting And Research) was launched by MoES/IMD in Delhi, Pune, Mumbai, and Ahmedabad—option A. Chennai, Kolkata, Hyderabad, and Bengaluru were added or planned in later phases but were not part of the initial four-city rollout this question references. Distractors B (Delhi, Chennai, Mumbai, Kolkata), C (Delhi, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Chennai), D (Delhi, Mumbai, Bangalore, Chennai) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements regarding global warming:
(a) Anaerobic Methane is emitted with rice cultivation.
(b) When nitrogen-based fertilizers are used, nitrous oxide is released into the soil.
Which of the above statement/statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Flooded paddy fields create anaerobic conditions where methanogenic bacteria emit methane—a recognised agricultural greenhouse source; statement (a) stands. Statement (b) loosely worded on nitrous oxide 'released into the soil' from nitrogen fertilisers does not match the correct acceptance—N₂O flux is a soil–atmosphere process framed differently in standard syllabi, so only (a) survives here.

questions.text: PAN (Peroxyacetyl nitrate) is formed as a result of following interaction:

options.B: Carbon monoxide and volatile organic compounds

questions.explanation: Option C works here because Photochemical smog produces PAN (peroxyacetyl nitrate) from the reaction of nitrogen oxides (NOₓ) with reactive hydrocarbons in sunlight. Pairing PAN with SO₂, CO alone, or ozone/particulates misidentifies the classic NOₓ + VOC photochemical pathway. You can eliminate A (Nitrogen oxide and sulfer dioxide), B (Carbon monoxide and volatile organic co…), D (Ozone and particulate matter) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: _________ development is prioritized over environment degradation in energy generation.
questions.explanation: In energy policy debates—especially dam and thermal projects—'human development' (electricity access, employment, poverty reduction) is often prioritised over immediate environmental costs in planners' rhetoric. Cultural, purely political, or vague 'social' labels do not capture this standard textbook phrasing on development–environment trade-offs.

questions.text: What percentage of the rate of price increase was required to be kept as per the objectives of the 12th Five Year Plan?
questions.explanation: Marked correct: 4.5 to 5.0%. India's Five Year Plans (1951–2017) ran from the First (1951–56) under Nehru to the Twelfth (2012–17); post-2017 planning shifted to three-year action agendas under NITI Aayog. This kind of item rewards steady factual reading over aggressive shortcut techniques — the marks come from having read the source once, not from clever elimination.

questions.text: To study the problems of India in the year 1995 _________ committee was formed under the chairmanship of Dr. Abid Hussain.
questions.explanation: Option D matches the question because Dr. Abid Hussain chaired the Small Industry Committee (1995) to examine problems of India's small-scale sector in the post-reform era. Education, agriculture, and large-industry panels were headed by other experts—Abid Hussain's name attaches specifically to small-industry policy review. You can eliminate A (Education), B (Agriculture), C (Large Industry) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D.
