questions.text: The Employees Provident Fund Act was made in _________.
questions.explanation: Choose option B: the Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act was enacted in 1952—establishing the EPF framework for organised-sector workers. 1950 predates the statute; 1960 and 1981 mark amendments or related labour laws, not the original EPF Act year. Distractors A (1950), C (1960), D (1981) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text:
Perspective Planning refers _________.
(a) Long run planning for 20 to 25 years.
(b) Long range targets are set in-advance for a period of 15, 20 or 25 years.
(c) One plan for entire period of 15 to 20 years.
(d) Broader Objectives and targets are achieved within one or two years.
questions.explanation: Perspective planning sets long-range targets 15–25 years ahead as a broad directional framework—statement (b) alone. Statement (a) overlaps but (c)'s 'one plan for entire period' and (d)'s one–two year operational horizon describe different planning horizons—not the definitional core of 'perspective' planning in Indian planning vocabulary.

questions.text:
Education for women reduces fertility due to _________.
(a) Education improves work opportunity for women.
(b) Educated women want their own children to be educated.
(c) Education and literacy make women more receptive to information about contraception.
(d) Improving economic condition of women.
questions.explanation: Demographic literature emphasises that female education and literacy increase receptivity to family-planning information and contraceptive use—statement (c) alone in the correct answer. Better jobs (a), schooling aspirations for children (b), or broad economic improvement (d) may correlate with fertility decline but are not the singled-out causal channel this item tests.

questions.text:
Food security includes following stages:
(a) Adequate availability of food grains to all.
(b) Adequate availability of food grains and pulses to all.
(c) Adequate availability of food grains, pulses, milk and vegetables to all.
(d) Adequate availability of food grains, pulses, milk products, vegetables, fruits, meat and fish etc.
questions.explanation: Option D works here because Food security progresses from basic grain availability through pulses, milk, vegetables, to a full dietary basket including fruits, meat, and fish—stage (d) captures the comprehensive definition. Narrower stages (a)–(c) describe incomplete security ladders; the paper treats the widest formulation as correct. Distractors A (Only (d)), B ((a) and (b)), C ((a), (b) and (c)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
According to Gunnar Mirdal the role of Govt. in economic development should be as follows:
(a) Effecting the spread effect by neutralizing backward effect.
(b) Neutralizing spread effect by effecting the backward effect.
(c) Effecting spread effect and backward effect.
(d) Neutralizing spread effect and backward effect.
questions.explanation: Option A is correct because Gunnar Myrdal argued that government should spread development from advanced to backward regions—neutralising the 'backwash' (polarisation) effect through deliberate spread effects. Options swapping spread/backwash roles or pairing both effects without neutralisation misstate Myrdal's cumulative causation policy prescription. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: Gaurav Dutt and Martin Ravalin said that Poverty Gap Index is calculated for which of the following reasons?

options.A: How much calories deficit needs to be made up to eliminate poverty?
options.B: How much income would be needed to cover the deficit to eliminate poverty?
options.C: How much increase in per capita income will be required to eliminate poverty?

questions.explanation: The answer is option B: the Poverty Gap Index (FGT₁) measures the aggregate income shortfall below the poverty line—i.e., how much money would be needed to lift all poor households to the threshold. Calorie-deficit or per-capita growth formulas describe other poverty metrics (Poverty Gap vs. Poverty Gap Index context with Deaton/Datt/Ravallion lineage)—not this income-gap interpretation. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: When was the 'Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao' campaign launched for the protection and empowerment of the girl child as per the last revised statistics of child sex Ratio in India?
questions.explanation: Option C matches the question because 'Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao' was launched on 22 January 2015 from Panipat, Haryana, amid concern over declining child sex ratio. 2016 and 2018 dates post-date the scheme; 25 January 2015 is a near-miss distractor off by three days. Distractors A (22 January 2016), B (22 January 2018), D (25 January 2015) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text:
Relative poverty depends on following factors:
(a) The human body needs calories every day.
(b) Income is necessary to meet basic needs.
(c) Comparing two income groups, the lower income group comes in poverty.
(d) Poverty is the condition of not being able to meet the basic needs.
questions.explanation: Relative poverty is defined by comparing income/consumption across groups—the lower group falling below a societal norm—statement (c) alone. Absolute poverty links to calorie needs (a) and basic-needs thresholds (d); income necessity (b) describes absolute, not relative, framing.

questions.text:
According to Higins Population growth can be _________.
(a) A motivator for autonomous investment in developed countries.
(b) A motivator for induced investment in under-developed countries.
(c) A motivator for only induced investment in developed countries.
(d) Demotivate for autonomous investment in a developed countries.
questions.explanation: Option C is the right choice since Higgins held that population growth can stimulate autonomous investment in developed economies (market size, innovation demand)—statement (a) alone. Induced investment in underdeveloped countries (b) or mixed developed-country induced paths (c) and (d) do not match his dual-economy investment typology the official answer selects. You can eliminate A ((a) and (b)), B (only (d)), D ((b) and (c)) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: The largest share of allocation in the Seventh Five Year Plan went to the:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option C — the Seventh Five Year Plan (1985–90) allocated the largest share of public outlay to the energy sector—power, coal, petroleum—reflecting India's infrastructure push of that decade. Agriculture, industry-only, or transport-without-energy combinations do not match the plan's sectoral priority ranking. Distractors A (Agriculture and Communication Sector), B (Industrial and Communication Sector), D (Transport and Communication Sector) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: Who has criticized that economics is a Kuber worshiping science?
questions.explanation: Option C works here because the paper keys 'Karlail and Raskin' (transliteration of Karl Marx and John Ruskin) as critics who mocked economics as a 'Kuber-worshipping' (wealth-idolising) science. Ricardo/Malthus were classical economists; Keynes/Marx pairings or Chamberlin/Robinson name industrial-organisation figures—not this specific moral critique attributed to Marx–Ruskin in Maharashtra economics notes. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: In a Society where the income distribution is excessive _________ the handful individual there has unlimited money.
questions.explanation: Option B matches the question because When income distribution is highly skewed—asymmetric—a few individuals hold disproportionate wealth while the mass remains at lower tiers. 'Equality' and 'abundance' contradict extreme concentration; 'deficiency' describes shortage, not lopsided distribution—the asymmetry term captures inequality geometry. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: A particle thrown up has zero velocity but how much will be the acceleration?

options.C: Equal to acceleration due to gravity

questions.explanation: At the highest point of vertical throw, instantaneous velocity becomes zero—but acceleration remains the downward gravitational field (~9.8 m/s²) throughout the flight unless air drag is modelled separately. Velocity and acceleration are different kinematic quantities; zero speed does not cancel the force of gravity. Options claiming zero acceleration confuse 'momentarily at rest' with 'no force'; infinity and 'one' have no physical basis in standard free-fall near Earth's surface.

questions.text: Which one of the following is not an application of Bernoulli equation?
questions.explanation: Bernoulli's principle links pressure, velocity and height in a flowing fluid—all three listed devices exploit that relationship. An aspirator uses a high-velocity jet to lower pressure and draw fluid; a Venturi meter/pump measures or utilises the pressure drop in a constriction; Torricelli's law (speed of efflux) is Bernoulli applied at a tank orifice. Because each option is a valid application, 'None of the above' is the correct reading: there is no non-application among A, B and C.

questions.text: At room temperature (300k), what is the significant contribution wavelength for the thermal radiation emitted by a body?
questions.explanation: Choose option B: Wien's displacement law gives peak emission wavelength λ_max ≈ 2.898×10⁻³/T (metre-kelvin). At 300 K, λ_max ≈ 9.7 µm (~9550 nm)—deep infrared, not visible light. 500 nm and 1500 nm sit in the visible/near-IR window where a 300 K blackbody radiates far less intensely; 3000 nm is closer but still short of the true thermal peak for room-temperature bodies. You can eliminate A (500 nm), C (1500 nm), D (3000 nm) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Which of the following sentence is wrong?
(I) Atomic nucleus is made up of protons and neutrons.
(II) Proton has a positive charge.
(III) Electron has a negative charge.
(IV) Neutron has a positive charge.
questions.explanation: Option D is the right choice since statements (I)–(III) are textbook facts: the nucleus contains protons and neutrons; protons carry positive charge; electrons carry negative charge. Only (IV) is incorrect—the neutron is electrically neutral, not positively charged. Pairing (III) with (II) or isolating (I) would condemn correct statements; the single wrong clause is the neutron charge error. Distractors A ((III) and (II)), B ((II) and (I)), C (Only (I)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text:
Say whether following sentences are true or false:
(I) For propagation of sound medium is necessary.
(II) Unit of frequency of sound is Hertz.
(III) Loudness of sound is expressed in decibel unit.
questions.explanation: All three assertions about sound are standard: mechanical waves need a material medium; frequency is measured in hertz; and loudness/intensity level is commonly expressed in decibels (a logarithmic scale). Restricting truth to (I)–(II) or (II) alone under-counts correct physics; claiming all three false contradicts basic acoustics taught from NCERT onward.

questions.text: Which of the following wavelengths are used to study the crystal structure of material?
questions.explanation: Crystal lattice spacings are on the order of angstroms (≈0.1–1 nm), so X-rays—with comparable wavelengths—produce diffraction patterns usable in Bragg's law analysis. UV and IR wavelengths are too long for routine crystallography; gamma rays penetrate without giving the same structured diffraction information in standard lab setups. X-ray crystallography is the classic tool for material structure determination.

questions.text: Leaf Blight of wheat is caused by infection of which of the following fungus?
questions.explanation: Option B is correct because Wheat leaf blight is associated with Alternaria triticina, producing characteristic leaf-spot/blight lesions. Uromyces tritici causes rust, not blight; Ustilago nuda causes loose smut of barley/wheat; Helminthosporium (Bipolaris) sativum is linked to leaf spot but the standard MPSC pairing for 'leaf blight of wheat' is Alternaria triticina—memorise fungus–disease tables carefully. Distractors A (Uromyces tritici), C (Ustilago nuda), D (Helminthosporium sativum) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: Which division of Plantae is called amphibians of plant kingdom?
questions.explanation: Bryophytes (mosses, liverworts) are called amphibians of the plant kingdom because they need water for fertilisation and thrive in moist habitats, yet they are land plants lacking true vascular tissue. Pteridophytes have vascular systems; gymnosperms and angiosperms are fully terrestrial seed plants—none carry that 'amphibian' label in textbook phytogeography.

questions.text:
With respect to structure of DNA, following four statements are made. Choose the two relevant statements.
(a) DNA is made of two long chains of nucleotides coiled in a helix around a central axis.
(b) DNA is made of two long chains of nucleoside coiled around a central axis.
(c) The two chains are complimentary to each other so that Adenine is always paired with Thymine and cytosine with Guanine.
(d) The two chains are not complimentary to each other where Adenine is paired with uracil and cytosine with Guanine.
questions.explanation: Option C matches the question because Correct DNA description: two antiparallel polynucleotide chains (nucleotides, not nucleosides alone) wound in a double helix, with complementary base pairing—adenine with thymine, cytosine with guanine. Statement (b) wrongly says 'nucleoside' chains; (d) introduces uracil (RNA base) and denies complementarity. Only (a) plus (c) capture the Watson–Crick model tested here. You can eliminate A (Only (a) and (b) is relevant.), B (Only (b) and (d) is relevant.), D (Only (c) and (d) is relevant.) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are correct about the cell theory of Schleiden and Schwann?
(a) All living things are composed of one or more cells.
(b) New cells are formed from the pre-existing cells.
(c) There are basic similarities in chemical composition and metabolic functions of cells.
(d) The activity of an organism is collective activities and interactions of its cellular structures.
questions.explanation: Choose option D: Modern cell theory extends Schleiden–Schwann with all four planks: organisms are cellular; cells arise from pre-existing cells (Virchow); biochemical/metabolic unity; and organismal activity reflects collective cell behaviour. Stopping at (a)–(b) or omitting (d) overlooks the full doctrine MPSC keys expect—'All of the above' is the complete set. Distractors A ((a) and (b)), B ((a), (b) and (c)), C ((a), (c) and (d)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: Which of the following animals belong to same class?
questions.explanation: Torpedo (ray), Pristis (sawfish), Hippocampus (seahorse) and Anabas (climbing perch) all belong to Class Pisces—traditional 'fish' grouping in school-level taxonomy. Ichthyophis is an amphibian (caecilian); Calotes is a reptile—options mixing them with fish break the class boundary. Cartilaginous versus bony subdivisions still sit under Pisces in exam framing.

questions.text: Which plants extract/latex is used to prepare a narcotics called Heroin?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option A — Heroin (diacetylmorphine) is refined from opium latex obtained from Papaver somniferum—the opium poppy. Coca yields cocaine; Cannabis yields cannabinoids; bajra (pearl millet) is a food crop with no narcotic latex—each distractor points to a different drug plant or non-drug crop. You can eliminate B (Coca plant), C (Hemp plant), D (Bajra) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Match the following to express general resemblance between bones and girdle fore limbs and hind limbs.
(a) Shoulder joint - (i) Tibio-fibula
(b) Humerus - (ii) Knee
(c) Elbow - (iii) Femur
(d) Radio-ulna - (iv) Hip joint
questions.explanation: Option A works here because Homologous limb pairs share structural correspondence: shoulder joint ↔ hip joint (ball-and-socket girdle joints); humerus ↔ femur (single long proximal limb bone); elbow ↔ knee (hinge joints); radius–ulna ↔ tibia–fibula (paired forearm/shin bones). Option A encodes exactly that forelimb–hindlimb homology map; scrambled pairings swap girdle and segment identities. Distractors B (a-(iii), b-(ii), c-(iv), d-(i)), C (a-(ii), b-(iv), c-(i), d-(iii)), D (a-(i), b-(ii), c-(iv), d-(iii)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Which of the following statements is true?
(a) The adult human skeleton consists of 208 bones.
(b) Vertebrae and facial bones are irregular type of bones.
questions.explanation: The adult human skeleton has 206 bones—not 208—so statement (a) is false. Vertebrae and many facial bones (e.g., sphenoid, ethmoid, mandible in part) are classified as irregular bones because their shapes do not fit long, short, flat or sesamoid categories. 'Both correct' or '(a) only' retains the wrong bone count.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements:
Rate of a chemical reaction is _________.
(a) proportional to the concentration of reactants.
(b) decreases on increasing the concentration of reactants.
(c) increases on increasing the temperature.
(d) decreases on increasing the temperature.
questions.explanation: The answer is option C: Collision theory and the Arrhenius equation both say: higher reactant concentration raises collision frequency and thus rate (a); higher temperature increases kinetic energy and successful collisions, also raising rate (c). Statements (b) and (d) invert these relationships—rate does not fall when concentration or temperature rises under normal conditions. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text:
Which chemical compound is used to neutralize the acidity of soil increased due to excessive use of Chemical Fertilizers?
(a) Potash (b) Lime water (c) Milk of magnesia (d) Ammonium hydroxide
questions.explanation: Repeated nitrogenous fertiliser use acidifies soil; agricultural practice neutralises acidity with lime—calcium hydroxide (slaked lime/lime water), a base that raises pH. Potash is a fertiliser, not a neutraliser; milk of magnesia and ammonium hydroxide are not standard field liming agents in Indian agronomy keys—lime is the textbook corrective.

questions.text:
Which of the following pair/pairs of metal/metals can be extracted from their ores by using cyanide complex solutions?
(A) Cu and Au (B) Co and Ag (C) Au and Ag (D) Na and Hg
questions.explanation: Gold and silver are leached from low-grade ores using alkaline cyanide solutions (MacArthur–Forrest process)—Au and Ag form soluble cyano complexes. Copper cyanide leaching is less standard; cobalt/sodium and mercury pairs do not match the classic noble-metal cyanidation pairing tested in metallurgy MCQs.

questions.text:
Identify the type of following chemical reaction.
2KClO₃(s) → 2KCl(s) + 3O₂ ↑
(a) Exothermic reaction (b) Displacement reaction (c) Decomposition reaction (d) Photochemical reaction
questions.explanation: Option A is the right choice since 2KClO₃ → 2KCl + 3O₂ is thermal decomposition of a single compound into simpler products—no element displacement occurs. It is endothermic in setup (often MnO₂-catalysed heating), not a photochemical channel in the usual lab sense. Labelling it displacement or exothermic/photochemical mis-classifies the reaction type. You can eliminate B (Only (b)), C (Only (a) and (d)), D (Only (a)) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
From the following which isotope is called as heavy hydrogen?
(a) Protium (b) Deuterium (c) Tritium (d) None of the above
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option B — Deuterium (²H or D) has one proton and one neutron—twice the mass of ordinary protium (¹H)—hence 'heavy hydrogen.' Tritium (³H) is heavier still but is radioactive; protium is the lightest isotope. Exam keys conventionally reserve 'heavy hydrogen' for deuterium, not tritium or protium. Distractors A (Only (c)), C (Only (d)), D (Only (a) and (c)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: _________ is used to estimate the presence of unsaturation in oils and fats.
questions.explanation: Iodine value (or iodine number) measures grams of iodine absorbed per 100 g fat—directly reflecting double-bond (unsaturation) content in oils and fats. Saponification value estimates average molecular mass via alkali hydrolysis; acid value tracks free fatty acids; viscosity is a physical flow property—not a chemical unsaturation index.

questions.text:
Who among the following are members of a Committee that recommends the appointment of the Chief Information Commissioner?
(A) Prime Minister
(B) Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha
(C) Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha
(D) Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister.
(E) Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.explanation: Under Section 12(3) of the RTI Act, the Chief Information Commissioner is recommended by a committee of the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, and one Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM. Rajya Sabha LoP and the Lok Sabha Speaker are not on this recommending panel—options adding C or E over-expand membership.

questions.text: Which Article in the Constitution of India provides for the Post of Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)?
questions.explanation: The answer is option A: article 148 establishes the office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India and defines appointment conditions. Article 343 covers the official language; Articles 266–267 govern Consolidated and Contingency Funds; Article 248 is residuary legislative power—none create the CAG post. Distractors B (Article 343), C (Article 266), D (Article 248) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements regarding 'Kesavanand Bharati' Case:
(A) This case was heard by the Constitution Bench of 13 judges headed by Chief Justice of India A.N. Ray.
(B) In Seven-Six majority, the bench outlined the basic structure doctrine.
(C) This case changed the decision of Golaknath case.
(D) This case seems to be the instance of judicial activism.
questions.explanation: In Kesavananda Bharati (1973), a 13-judge bench led by CJI Sikri (not Ray as chair) delivered a 7:6 verdict entrenching the basic structure doctrine, effectively modifying Golaknath and marking bold judicial review—statements (B), (C) and (D). Statement (A) errs on the bench headship detail, so the trio B–C–D is the accepted combination.

questions.text: The Contingency Fund of India has been placed at the disposal of which authority among the following?

options.A: Comptroller and Auditor General of India

questions.explanation: Choose option B: article 267 places the Contingency Fund of India at the President's disposal for urgent unforeseen expenditure, later recouped via Parliament. The CAG audits accounts but does not control the fund; Parliament authorises replenishment; the PM has no standalone constitutional custody of this corpus. You can eliminate A (Comptroller and Auditor General of India), C (Parliament of India), D (Prime Minister of India) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding the 'Bommai Case' in reference to the Emergency in the State?
(A) The 'Bommai Case' Judgement was delivered by the Supreme Court in 1994.
(B) States can appeal to the Supreme Court when President's rule is introduced in the States.
(C) If President's Rule is imposed without valid reason/s the Supreme Court can quash the decision of the Central Government.
(D) An order to dissolve a State Assembly requires the approval of the Parliament.
questions.explanation: Option B is the right choice since S.R. Bommai (1994) affirmed that states may approach the Supreme Court against President's Rule, the Court can quash mala fide imposition, dissolution of an Assembly under Article 356 needs parliamentary approval, and the judgment itself was delivered in 1994—all four statements align with the landmark federalism ruling. Distractors A (Only (C) and (D)), C (Only (B), (C) and (D)), D (Only (A), (B) and (C)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: Identify the incorrect pair:

options.A: July 22, 1947 - Adoption of National Flag by the Constituent Assembly.
options.B: January 24, 1950 - Adoption of National Anthem by the Constituent Assembly.
options.C: January 25, 1950 - Adoption of National Calendar by the Government.
options.D: January 26, 1950 - Adoption of National Emblem by the Government.

questions.explanation: National Flag: 22 July 1947; National Anthem: 24 January 1950; National Emblem (Lion Capital): 26 January 1950. The Saka National Calendar was adopted later (1957), not on 25 January 1950—pair C is the incorrect date-event match the question seeks.

questions.text:
Consider the following statement/s regarding constitutional amendment/s in India and Choose the correct option/s.
(A) Dadra and Nagar Haveli territories were included in India as per the 10th Amendment.
(B) The territories of Diu, Daman and Goa were included in India as per the 11th Amendment.
(C) Legislature was established in Union Territories as per the 15th Amendment.
(D) The state of Meghalaya was created as per the 22nd Amendment.
questions.explanation: Option D works here because 10th Amendment (1961) integrated Dadra and Nagar Haveli; 22nd Amendment (1969) gave Meghalaya full statehood/autonomous status pathway. Goa, Daman and Diu came via the 12th—not 11th—Amendment; the 15th Amendment adjusted High Court judges' retirement age, not establishment of UT legislatures. You can eliminate A ((A) and (C) correct), B ((B) and (D) correct), C ((B) and (C) correct) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: The Central Information Commission includes one Chief Information Commissioner and Maximum how many Information Commissioners?
questions.explanation: Option B is correct because the RTI Act caps the Central Information Commission at one Chief Information Commissioner plus up to ten Information Commissioners. Five, six or eight are distractor counts—remember '1 + maximum 10' for the central body. Distractors A (Five Information Commissioners), C (Six Information Commissioners), D (Eight Information Commissioners) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Which of the following statement/s is/are correct regarding the citizenship of India?
(A) India has single citizenship system.
(B) Citizenship Act was passed in 1955.
(C) Part 4 of the Indian Constitution provides citizenship.

options.D: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation: India follows single citizenship (no dual state and union citizenship) and the Citizenship Act was enacted in 1955. Citizenship provisions live in Part II (Articles 5–11), not Part IV (Directive Principles)—statement (C) is the false clause; (A) and (B) stand together.

questions.text: Which Articles in the Constitution provide for the electoral system in our country?
questions.explanation: Option B matches the question because articles 324–329 constitute the constitutional electoral code: Election Commission (324), conduct of elections (325–327), disqualifications (329) and related machinery. Articles 124–128 cover the Supreme Court; 256–259 and 274–279 deal with centre–state relations and finance—not the electoral framework. You can eliminate A (Articles 124 to 128), C (Articles 256 to 259), D (Articles 274 to 279) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text:
The Indian Constitution establishes a secular state, meaning:
(A) The state makes discrimination on the basis of religion in matters of employment.
(B) The state avoids preferential treatment for any particular religion.
(C) The state treats all religions equally.
(D) Freedom of faith and worship is allowed to all the people.
(E) Educational institutions, without exception, are free to impart religious instructions.
questions.explanation: Secularism in the Indian Constitution means the state stays equidistant—no religion gets preferential treatment (B), all faiths are treated equally (C), and individuals enjoy freedom of conscience and worship (D). Statement (A) reverses secularism by endorsing religious discrimination in employment; (E) wrongly universalises religious instruction in all schools—minority and Article 28 limits apply.

questions.text: Delhi was called National Capital Territory by which Constitution Amendment Act?
questions.explanation: The 69th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1991 re-designated Delhi as the National Capital Territory with an elected assembly and lieutenant governor framework. The 63rd, 91st and 93rd Amendments address other subjects (Panchayat extension, anti-defection, OBC reservations in private unaided institutions)—not Delhi's NCT status.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about First Lok Sabha:
(A) The first Lok Sabha was constituted on 17 April 1952 after India's First General Elections were held from 25 October 1951 to 21 February 1952.
(B) The first session of first Lok Sabha commenced on 13 May 1952.
(C) The first Lok Sabha lasted its Full tenure and dissolved on 1 April 1957.
(D) Shri. G.V. Mavalankar was the First Deputy Speaker of First Lok Sabha.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option B — india's first general elections ran October 1951–February 1952; the first Lok Sabha was constituted on 17 April 1952 and its first session opened 13 May 1952—statements (A) and (B). Claims that it dissolved only after a full term ending 1 April 1957 or that G.V. Mavalankar was Deputy Speaker misstate tenure/Speaker facts—he was the first Speaker. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Consider the following provision/s with respect to various 'National Commissions' in India.
(A) 'National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes' was established under Article 339 of the Constitution of India.
(B) The 'National Commission for Women' was established under the 'National Commission for Women Act' 1990.
(C) The 'National Commission for Minorities' was established under the 'National Commission for Minorities Act' 1992.
(D) On 27th December 1993 an ordinance was passed to establish the 'National Human Rights Commission'.
questions.explanation: Option D works here because the National Commission for Women was created under the NCW Act, 1990; the National Commission for Minorities under the NCM Act, 1992. The SC/ST national commission flows from Articles 338/338A—not Article 339; NHRC was established by the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993—the December 1993 ordinance narrative is not the paired correct statutory fact set here. Distractors A ((A) and (C)), B ((B) and (D)), C ((A) and (D)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: Which article empowers the High Courts to issue directions for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights?
questions.explanation: Option A is correct because article 226 empowers High Courts to issue writs for enforcement of Fundamental Rights and for 'any other purpose' within their territorial jurisdiction—the primary HC writ remedy. Articles 133, 135 and 143 concern appeals, jurisdiction transfer and advisory opinions, not this enforcement power. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: Karpoori Thakur was recently in news. Which of the following is not true about him?

options.A: He is also known as 'Jan Nayak'.
options.B: He was First non-congress Chief Minister of Bihar.
options.C: He was born in 1924, in a village in Samastipur District.
options.D: He won State Assembly election in 1952 from Samastipur Constituency.

questions.explanation: Karpoori Thakur ('Jan Nayak') was Bihar's first non-Congress CM, born 1924 in Samastipur district—but his maiden assembly victory in 1952 was from Tajpur, not Samastipur constituency. Options A–C are biographical staples; the 1952 seat detail in (D) is the false statement.

questions.text: Which is the India's rank in global hunger Index 2023?
questions.explanation: Option B matches the question because in the Global Hunger Index 2023, India ranked 111th among 125 countries—reflecting child wasting, stunting and undernourishment components. Rank 100, 101 or 123 are near-miss distractors from adjacent years or misremembered reports. Distractors A (100), C (101), D (123) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Consider the correct statements regarding new Parliament building:
(a) The interior design of Lok Sabha in the new Parliament is based on the theme of National Animal Lion.
(b) The design of Rajya Sabha is based on the theme of India's National Flower Lotus.
(c) The new Parliament building was inaugurated on 28th May, 2023.
(d) The historic Ashok Chakra has been installed beside the speaker of Lok Sabha.
questions.explanation: Working through the options, Statements (b), (c) are correct. is the correct one. The year 2023 anchors this question — the correct option is the fact that dates to that year. Read each statement independently and check it against a factual anchor (a date, a body, a percentage) before deciding — the option marked correct is the combination that survives the check. Add this correct option to your active-recall flashcard deck; MPSC repeats the underlying fact in some form every two to three prelim cycles.

questions.text:
Identify the correct statements regarding Asian Games - 2023.
(a) This competition was held in Hangzhou, China.
(b) Shooter Lovelina Borgohain played a role of flag bearer for India at the time of inauguration.
(c) India got 4th position with 28 gold medals.
(d) India got total 107 medals in this competition.
questions.explanation: Option D is the right choice since Hangzhou hosted the 2023 Asian Games where India finished fourth with 28 golds and 107 medals overall. Flag-bearer details in (b) are incorrect (Lovelina Borgohain was not the cited inaugural flag bearer)—eliminate options retaining (b) and keep (a), (c), (d). You can eliminate A ((a), (b), (c)), B ((a), (b), (d)), C ((b), (c), (d)) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. questions.text:
Select the correct statements:
(a) The Nobel Peace Prize, 2023 was awarded to Narges Mohammadi.
(b) Narges Mohammadi is a champion of equality and women's rights.
(c) In 2004, Narges Mohammadi joined the Defenders of Human Right Center founded by Shirin Ebadi.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option A — the 2023 Nobel Peace Prize went to Iranian activist Narges Mohammadi for fighting oppression of women—statements (a) and (b). While she did join Shirin Ebadi's Defenders of Human Rights Center, the exam key accepts only (a) and (b) as the verified pair—do not over-select (c) when the option set restricts to two clauses. questions.text: Which space agency helps India in tracking the Solar Mission Aditya - L1?
questions.explanation: ISRO partnered with the European Space Agency (ESA) for deep-space tracking support during the Aditya-L1 solar mission—leveraging ESA's ground-station network. NASA, JAXA and Roscosmos were not the highlighted tracking collaborator in official mission briefings for this item.

questions.text:
Select the correct statements (Padma Awards 2024):
(a) 30 of the awardees in it are women.
(b) 6 Padma Vibhushan award were declared.
(c) 17 Padma Bhushan and 110 Padma Shri awards were declared.
questions.explanation: Option C is correct because Padma Awards 2024: 30 women among awardees (a); 17 Padma Bhushan and 110 Padma Shri declared (c). Six Padma Vibhushan (b) overstates the Vibhushan count—pair (a) with (c), not the inflated Vibhushan figure. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: Bar Council of India's 'International Lawyers Conference 2023' was inaugurated in which City?
questions.explanation: The answer is option A: Bar Council of India's International Lawyers Conference 2023 was inaugurated at New Delhi—aligning with central legal-institution events. Mumbai, Kolkata and Bengaluru were not the stated inaugural venue for this BCI conference. Distractors B (Mumbai), C (Kolkata), D (Bengaluru) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. questions.text:
Match the country and the Operations undertaken to protect Indian Nationals Abroad.
(a) Operation Ajay - (i) Ukraine
(b) Operation Ganga - (ii) Israel
(c) Operation Devishakti - (iii) Sudan
(d) Operation Kaveri - (iv) Afghanistan
questions.explanation: Evacuation codenames pair as: Operation Ajay (Israel), Operation Ganga (Ukraine), Operation Devi Shakti (Afghanistan), Operation Kaveri (Sudan)—mapping a-(ii), b-(i), c-(iv), d-(iii). Mixing Ukraine with Israel or Sudan with Afghanistan scrambles the 2022–2023 crisis-response chronology.

questions.text:
Recently, Odisha Chief Minister has launched Mukhyamantri Sampoorna Pushti Yojana. What is/are the primary objective/s of the scheme?
(a) To promote higher education for girls.
(b) Improve maternal and child nutrition in the State.
(c) To provide employment opportunities for adolescent girls.
(d) Boosting agricultural production in rural area.
questions.explanation: Choose option B: Mukhyamantri Sampoorna Pushti Yojana (Odisha) targets complete nutrition—improving maternal and child nutrition through supplementary feeding and related interventions. Higher education for girls, adolescent employment and generic farm productivity are different scheme objectives. You can eliminate A (Only (a) is correct.), C ((a) and (d) are correct.), D ((c) and (d) are correct.) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text:
Match the following pairs:
(a) Dr. Nitin Karmalkar Committee - (i) For implementation of National Education Policy - 2020 in Maharashtra

questions.text:
Women Reservation Bill - 2023, consider the following statements:
(a) Narishakti Vandan Adhiniyam officially the Constitutional (128th amendment) bill - 2023 is a bill introduced in the Parliament of India.
(b) The Women reservation bill was introduced by PM Narendra Modi in Lok Sabha on 10th Sept. 2023.
(c) This legislation seeks to allocate 30 percent of the seats in Lok Sabha and State legislative assemblies for women.
(d) The bill was the first that was considered in the new Parliament building.
questions.explanation: Option A works here because Narishakti Vandan Adhiniyam is the popular name for the Constitution (128th Amendment) Bill, 2023 on women's reservation, and it was among the first bills taken up in the new Parliament building—(a) and (d). The September 2023 introduction date and 30% reservation figure in (b)–(c) do not match the accepted facts—the bill seeks one-third (33%) seats. You can eliminate B ((a) and (b) are correct.), C ((a), (b), (c) are correct.), D ((a), (b), (c) and (d) are correct.) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

Distractors A ((a), (b), (c), (e)), C ((b), (c), (d), (e)), D ((a), (b), (c), (d)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.
