title: MPSC Sub Inspector State Excise Pre 2017 (English)

questions.text: The British Government, through the Robertson Committee started ___ for the development of transportation in India.
questions.explanation: The Robertson Committee (1901) recommended a dedicated body to coordinate India's expanding rail network; the British Government responded by creating the Railway Board in 1905—not a generic Board of Transportation or Labour. Agriculture and labour boards belong to different colonial policy streams. MPSC transport-history MCQs pair 'Robertson' with institutional birth of the Railway Board.

questions.text:
Match the following pairs:
a. Free Press Bulletin – I. Bombay
b. Free India – II. Madras
c. Dinamani – III. Calcutta
d. Sakal – IV. Pune

(A) a-I, b-III, c-II, d-IV
(B) a-IV, b-I, c-III, d-II
(C) a-III, b-II, c-I, d-IV
(D) a-I, b-II, c-III, d-IV
questions.explanation: The answer is option A: anchor each nationalist-era paper to its city: Free Press Bulletin (Bombay), Free India (Madras), Dinamani (Calcutta), Sakal (Pune)—yielding a-I, b-II, c-III, d-IV. Swapping Bombay with Pune or Madras with Calcutta breaks the standard Marathi/Madras Presidency journalism map students memorise for pre-Independence press questions. You can eliminate B (IV I III II), C (III II I IV), D (I II III IV) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: Which of the following dramas did Ratnakar Matkari write regarding the dowry system?
questions.explanation: Option D matches the question because Ratnakar Matkari's 'Agnidivya' is the drama explicitly framed around dowry exploitation in Maharashtra theatre syllabi. 'Khol Khol Pani' and 'Ashwamedh' treat other social themes; 'Maza Kai Chukla?' is a different Matkari work. Matkari dowry MCQs almost always key to Agnidivya, not his broader satirical catalogue. Distractors A (Khol Khol Pani), B (Ashwamedh), C (Maza Kai Chukla?) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: In Mumbai, the cooperative dairy work began at ___.
questions.explanation: Mumbai's cooperative dairy movement took root in the Aarey Milk Colony belt—organised collection and processing away from the crowded island city. Bandra, Colaba, and Worli were urban wards, not the planned dairy-cooperative hub the Maharashtra cooperative narrative identifies with Aarey.

questions.text: In Maharashtra, the cooperative organisations for buying and selling are known as ___.
questions.explanation: Option D is the right choice since Maharashtra's district and state-level cooperative marketing bodies funnel into the apex 'Marketing Federation' terminology used in cooperative law and economic surveys—not the longer formal names in distractors. Options (a)–(c) sound official but miss the concise label MPSC keys for buying/selling cooperatives. You can eliminate A (Cooperative Marketing Organisation), B (District Cooperative Marketing Federati…), C (State Cooperative Marketing Federation) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: Which commission promoted the 'Earn and Learn' scheme?
questions.explanation: The Radhakrishnan Commission (1948–49) on university education promoted work-study and 'Earn and Learn' schemes to widen access without full fee dependence. Mudaliar (secondary education), Kothari (1964–66), and Sargent (1944) addressed different tiers—only Radhakrishnan carries the earn-and-learn tag in standard education-history tables.

questions.text:
Match the following pairs:
a. S.N. Pendse – I. Shitu
b. G.N. Dandekar – II. Chakra
c. Bhalchandra Nemade – III. Ratha Chakra
d. Jayawant Dalvi – IV. Kosla

(A) a-II, b-III, c-I, d-IV
(B) a-III, b-I, c-IV, d-II
(C) a-I, b-IV, c-II, d-III
(D) a-III, b-II, c-I, d-IV
questions.explanation: Lock each author to his landmark novel: S.N. Pendse–Shitu, G.N. Dandekar–Chakra, Bhalchandra Nemade–Kosla, Jayawant Dalvi–Ratha Chakra. That yields a-III, b-I, c-IV, d-II. Swapping Kosla with Ratha Chakra or Shitu with Chakra is the standard Marathi-fiction match-the-pairs trap.

questions.text: The longest tunnel on Konkan Railway is at ___.
questions.explanation: Option A is correct because the Karbude tunnel on Konkan Railway (~6.5 km) was the longest on the line when commissioned—cutting through the Western Ghats between Ratnagiri and Sindhudurg. Malvan, Rajapur, and Vengurla are coastal talukas without that superlative tunnel credit in Konkan rail geography. You can eliminate B (Malvan), C (Rajapur), D (Vengurla) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Match the following pairs:
a. Imperialist School – I. Valentine Chirol
b. Cambridge School – II. Anil Seal
c. The Nationalist School – III. R.C. Majumdar
d. The Marxist School – IV. R.P. Dutt

(A) a-II, b-I, c-IV, d-III
(B) a-IV, b-III, c-II, d-I
(C) a-I, b-II, c-III, d-IV
(D) a-III, b-IV, c-I, d-II
questions.explanation: The answer is option C: Imperialist school → Valentine Chirol; Cambridge (consensus) → Anil Seal; Nationalist → R.C. Majumdar; Marxist → R.P. Dutt—straight a-I, b-II, c-III, d-IV. Swapping Cambridge with Imperialist or Marxist with Nationalist scrambles the ideological labels attached to each historian in UPSC/MPSC historiography grids. Distractors A (II I IV III), B (IV III II I), D (III IV I II) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: Name the British Governor General who transferred the Capital of India from Calcutta to Delhi.
questions.explanation: Option A matches the question because Lord Hardinge II announced the transfer of India's capital from Calcutta to Delhi in 1911; the shift was formalised with the 1912 Durbar and subsequent construction of New Delhi. Ripon is local self-government; Chelmsford and Lytton belong to other constitutional and Afghan-war eras—not the 1911 capital move. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: ___ was the founder member of the Communist Party of India.
questions.explanation: M.N. Roy was among the founding figures of the Communist Party of India (1920, Tashkent group)—a cosmopolitan Marxist before domestic trade-union leadership passed to others. N.M. Joshi led the trade-union wing; R.P. Dutt was a later Marxist theoretician; Ansari was Congress-Muslim League, not CPI genesis.

questions.text: Local self-government in modern India was started by ___.
questions.explanation: Option A is the right choice since Lord Ripon's 1882 resolution on local self-government earned him the title 'Father of Local Self-Government in India'—expanding municipal and district boards. Cornwallis codified permanent settlement; Clive and Mountbatten belong to conquest and Partition eras, predating or postdating Ripon's liberal local-board framework. Distractors B (Lord Cornwallis), C (Lord Mountbatten), D (Lord Clive) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements:
a. The Constituent Assembly of India was set up according to the provision of the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946.
b. The first session of the Constituent Assembly of India was held on 9th December, 1946.
c. The eleventh session of the Constituent Assembly of India was held between 14th November to 26th November, 1949.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All three limbs hold: the Assembly was constituted under the Cabinet Mission Plan (1946); its first session met 9 December 1946; the eleventh and final substantive session ran 14–26 November 1949 before adoption of the Constitution. Options dropping any one date or the Cabinet Mission link under-count a textbook timeline MCQ. Option A (Only a and b) conflicts with the definition, collocations, or calculation path that supports C (a, b and c); option B (Only b and c) conflicts with the definition, collocations, or calculation path that supports C (a, b and c); and option D (Only a and c) conflicts with the definition, collocations, or calculation path that supports C (a, b and c).

questions.text: Who was the founder of the Indian National Army?
questions.explanation: Option D works here because the official key credits Subhash Chandra Bose as founder of the Indian National Army narrative tested here—Bose reorganised and led the Azad Hind Fauj after Ras Bihari Bose handed leadership in 1943. Textbook nuance places Ras Bihari Bose and Mohan Singh in the 1942 genesis; defer to the correct (D) for this paper. You can eliminate A (Laxmi Sehgal), B (Lala Hardayal), C (Ras Bihari Bose) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: In the State of Maharashtra, the lowest child sex-ratio (801) is in ___ district.
questions.explanation: Option D is correct because Census 2011 placed Beed district among Maharashtra's lowest child sex ratios (~801)—reflecting Marathwada's skewed juvenile sex ratio belt. Gadchiroli, Jalna, and Akola show distress but not the specific 801 floor Beed carried in state demographic bulletins of that period. Distractors A (Gadchiroli), B (Jalna), C (Akola) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: In which year did the mineral oil and natural gas exploitation project start at Bombay High in the Arabian Sea?
questions.explanation: Offshore oil and gas production at Bombay High was inaugurated on 3 February 1974—marking India's first major offshore hydrocarbon exploitation in the Arabian Sea. The 1972 and 1976 distractors are near-miss commissioning dates students confuse with platform fabrication or first oil flow milestones.

questions.text: Maharashtra Government has undertaken 'Sant Tukaram Vangram Yojana' from ___.
questions.explanation: Option D matches the question because Maharashtra launched Sant Tukaram Vangram Yojana in 2006 to develop model villages linked to the Warkari saint's legacy—rural infrastructure and cultural tourism in selected gram panchayats. Earlier years (2000–2004) belong to other village-scheme launches; 2006 is the correct rollout in state plan documents. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Consider the statements:
a. The area occupied by the Tapi river basin in north Maharashtra has an eastward slope.
b. The area occupied by the Wardha-Wainganga river basin slopes towards the south direction.
c. The area occupied by the remaining plateau river basin slopes towards the east direction.

Which one of the above statements is NOT correct?
questions.explanation: Choose option A: statement (a) is incorrect: the Tapi river basin in north Maharashtra slopes westward toward the Arabian Sea, not eastward. Wardha–Wainganga basin slopes south; remaining Deccan plateau rivers generally slope east—making (b) and (c) correct while (a) alone is NOT correct. Distractors B (Only b), C (Only c), D (Only b and c) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Match the following pairs:
Ghats → Roads
a. Thal Ghat – I. Vengurla – Sawantwadi – Nipani
b. Bhor Ghat – II. Mumbai – Kalyan – Otur
c. Malshej Ghat – III. Mumbai – Pune
d. Amboli Ghat – IV. Mumbai – Nashik

(A) a-IV, b-III, c-II, d-I
(B) a-I, b-II, c-III, d-IV
(C) a-III, b-II, c-I, d-IV
(D) a-II, b-III, c-IV, d-I
questions.explanation: Thal Ghat serves the Mumbai–Nashik corridor (IV); Bhor Ghat the Mumbai–Pune road (III); Malshej Ghat links Mumbai–Kalyan–Otur (II); Amboli Ghat the Konkan Vengurla–Sawantwadi–Nipani route (I)—a-IV, b-III, c-II, d-I. Mixing Pune ghat with Nashik road or Konkan pass with Bhor is the classic Western-Ghat transport trap.

questions.text: What was the density of population of Maharashtra in 1960 – 1961?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option D — Maharashtra's 1961 Census density was about 117 persons/km² after state reorganisation—not 229, 339, or 310. All three numerals are You can eliminate A (229), B (339), C (310) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text:
Match the following pairs:
Tribes → Districts
a. Katkari – I. Bhandara
b. Bhil – II. Amrawati
c. Korku – III. Nandurbar
d. Gond – IV. Raigad

(A) a-IV, b-III, c-II, d-I
(B) a-III, b-II, c-I, d-IV
(C) a-II, b-I, c-III, d-IV
(D) a-I, b-II, c-III, d-IV
questions.explanation: Correct: option A — "IV III II I". Raigad Fort in the Sahyadri was chosen by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj as the capital of the Maratha state; he was coronated here on 6 June 1674. The correct pairing above matches every column-A entry with its column-B partner as marked in the official key. A helpful anchoring habit for questions of this type is to underline the year, proper noun or numeric anchor in the stem before you scan the options.

questions.text:
Arrange the following peaks in the descending order of their altitude from mean sea level:
a. Salher
b. Saptashrungi
c. Mahabaleshwar
d. Kalsubai
questions.explanation: Height ladder: Kalsubai (~1,646 m) tops Salher (~1,567 m), then Mahabaleshwar (~1,438 m), then Saptashrungi (~1,230 m)—sequence d, a, c, b. Options placing the plateau hill-station Mahabaleshwar above Salher or Saptashrungi first ignore Sahyadri peak rankings.

questions.text:
Arrange the following districts of Maharashtra in ascending order on the basis of their population density as per 2011 Census record:
a. Sindhudurg
b. Gadchiroli
c. Nandurbar
d. Dhule
questions.explanation: The answer is option C: Lowest to highest density among the four: Gadchiroli (sparse tribal east), Sindhudurg (coastal but low), Nandurbar, Dhule—order b, a, c, d. Gadchiroli's forests keep density lowest; Dhule's plain agriculture pushes it highest in the set. You can eliminate A (a, b, c, d), B (d, c, b, a), D (c, d, b, a) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: Which of the following is a tributary of River Wardha?
questions.explanation: Option A matches the question because Nirguda is a recognised left-bank tributary joining the Wardha in Vidarbha. Manyad, Sindphana, and Girja flow in other Peninsular river systems—assigning them to Wardha misplaces Wainganga–Wardha basin geography tested in Maharashtra river MCQs. Distractors B (Manyad), C (Sindphana), D (Girja) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text:
Arrange the sequence of rivers in South Konkan from North to South.
a. Vaitarna
b. Savitri
c. Ulhas
d. Vashisthi
questions.explanation: North-to-south coastal sequence: Vaitarna, Ulhas, Savitri, Vashisthi—a, c, b, d. Ulhas sits between Vaitarna and Savitri around Mumbai–Raigad; placing Savitri north of Ulhas or Vashisthi first breaks the Konkan river ordering students map from Palghar to Ratnagiri.

questions.text: How many district boundaries does the Pune district have?
questions.explanation: Pune district shares boundaries with five neighbours (Satara, Solapur, Ahmednagar, Thane/Palghar belt, Raigad—exact set varies with later splits but the correct count is five). Four or six are near-miss counts after Ahmednagar and Konkan boundary adjustments in administrative atlases. Option A (4) gives a numerical result that does not follow from the formula or data in the stem (correct: B = 5); option C (6) gives a numerical result that does not follow from the formula or data in the stem (correct: B = 5); and option D (7) gives a numerical result that does not follow from the formula or data in the stem (correct: B = 5).

questions.text:
Arrange the following layers of the Earth from the outer layer to inner layer given by Dr. R.A. Daly:
a. Barysphere
b. Asthenosphere
c. Lithosphere
d. Mesosphere
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option D — R.A. Daly's crust–mantle ordering from outside in: Lithosphere → Asthenosphere → Mesosphere → Barysphere (core)—c, b, d, a. Reversing asthenosphere with mesosphere or placing barysphere outermost inverts the plastic–rigid mantle sequence taught in geomorphology units. Distractors A (a, b, c, d), B (d, c, b, a), C (c, a, d, b) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: Quantitative methods of RBI include ___.
questions.explanation: Open Market Operations, Bank Rate, and Variable Reserve Ratio (CRR/SLR changes) are all quantitative (general) credit-control tools—directly affecting money supply and bank liquidity. Qualitative tools (margin requirements, moral suasion) sit in a separate RBI toolkit; here all three listed instruments belong in the quantitative bucket.

questions.text:
Observe the following statements:
a. Manganese deposits are found at Sindhudurg.
b. Bauxite is mainly found in laterite.
c. Chromite is mined at Mauni in Bhandara district.

Which statements are correct?

options.C: Statements b and c are correct
options.D: Statements a, b and c are correct

questions.explanation: Option D is correct because Manganese occurs in Sindhudurg district; bauxite is predominantly a laterite-hosted ore in Maharashtra; chromite is mined near Mauni, Bhandara—all three statements hold. Options isolating only (a) or only (c) under-count the state's laterite–chromite–manganese triangle in economic geology notes. You can eliminate A (Only statement a is correct), B (Only statement c is correct), C (Statements b and c are correct) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: Engineering goods occupied the first place with a share of ___ percent in India's export in 2012 – 13.
questions.explanation: The answer is option B: Engineering goods led India's export basket in 2012–13 with roughly 21.7% share—ahead of petroleum and gems in that year's trade statistics. The 28–31% band distractors inflate the headline; MPSC economy papers of this vintage key the low-20s engineering share from Commerce Ministry compilations. Distractors A (31.7%), C (28.7%), D (30.7%) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: Narasimham Committee has recommended that SLR should decline from 38.5 percent to ___.
questions.explanation: The Narasimham Committee (1991) recommended phased SLR reduction from the pre-reform 38.5% toward 25%—freeing bank funds for commercial lending. 28% and 30.5% are intermediate targets students recall from transition years; the terminal recommendation figure tested here is 25%.

questions.text: Primary deficit of Govt. of India in percent of GDP was negative in the year ___.
questions.explanation: Choose option C: india's primary deficit (fiscal deficit minus interest payments) as a share of GDP turned negative in the high-growth years 2006–07 and 2007–08—strong revenue buoyancy before the global slowdown. Later pairs (2010–11, 2012–13) saw renewed primary deficits; the negative-primary window is the pre-2008 boom pair. You can eliminate A (2007 – 08 and 2008 – 09), B (2010 – 11 and 2011 – 12), D (2012 – 13 and 2013 – 14) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
The following statements are true concerning NITI Aayog:
a. No power to allocate funds.
b. It is a think tank.
c. Imposes policies on States.
d. Consulting States while making policy.

Which are correct?
questions.explanation: Option A is the right choice since NITI Aayog is a think tank without fund-allocation power (a) and consults states (d)—it does not impose policies coercively (c). Statement (b) defines its role. Bundling (c) treats NITI like the old Planning Commission's directive plan authority—a post-2015 governance trap. Distractors B (Only a, b and c), C (Only b, c and d), D (Only a, c and d) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: The growth rate of Indian economy was ___ in 1950 – 80.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option C — india's average annual GDP growth over 1950–1980 hovered near 3.5%—the 'Hindu rate of growth' era before 1991 reforms. 2.5% understates the three-decade mean; 4–4.5% overstates it; 3.5% is the textbook planning-period average in Maharashtra state-board economy modules. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: The expenditure of the Government on law and order is classified as ___.
questions.explanation: Option B works here because Government spending on law and order is classified as unproductive (non-development) revenue expenditure—it maintains security but does not directly create capital assets or productive capacity. Calling it capital or productive expenditure mislabels police/judiciary outlays in budget classification MCQs. You can eliminate A (productive expenditure), C (capital expenditure), D (None of the above) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: When RBI raises the bank rate then there is ___.
questions.explanation: The examination key marks discourage to investment as the correct choice. The Reserve Bank of India was established under the RBI Act 1934 (operative 1 April 1935) and nationalised on 1 January 1949; it is India's monetary authority and banking regulator. The safest way to lock this item into recall is to write the correct option next to its associated year or body in your revision notebook and skim it weekly.

questions.text: When expenditure exceeds the total revenue it is called ___.
questions.explanation: When total expenditure exceeds total revenue, the budget is in deficit—a fundamental fiscal identity. Surplus is the reverse; balanced budget requires equality; neither applies when expenditure overshoots receipts.

questions.text: Which of the following programmes aims to provide employment only to the rural poor?
questions.explanation: Option A matches the question because Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) targeted self-employment for rural poor through SHGs and micro-enterprise—not urban poor (SJSRY) or educated-youth schemes. 'Rural poor only' in the stem points to the gram swarozgar yojana acronym chain. You can eliminate B (Swarnajayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana (SJ…), C (Self Employment for Educated Youth), D (None of the above) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Which of the following statement/s is/are correct?
a. The national income trends during the period of economic planning do not indicate a consistent increase.
b. Growth has taken place only in about half of the years of economic planning.
c. For almost half the period of economic planning there has been little growth or even negative growth.
d. Considering economic planning period as a whole, there has been a steady, consistent growth.
questions.explanation: Choose option A: Planning-era national income did not rise smoothly: roughly half the years saw weak or negative growth amid droughts and oil shocks (a–c). Statement (d) claiming steady consistent growth contradicts the volatile annual series—only (a), (b), and (c) capture the stop–go planning record. Distractors B (Only d), C (Only a), D (Only c) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text:
The lackluster agricultural growth since the new millennium is due to:
a. Structural weakness
b. Low level of public investment
c. Unbalanced fertilizer use
d. Small size of agricultural holding
questions.explanation: Post-2000 agricultural slowdown stems from structural weaknesses, low public investment, and unbalanced fertiliser use—all in (a)–(c). Small holdings (d) are chronic but the correct bundle emphasises macro structural and investment failures over farm-size alone.

questions.text:
For which of the following industries is licensing compulsory?
a. Cigarettes
b. Alcohol
c. Industrial explosives
d. Defence equipments
questions.explanation: Cigarettes, alcohol, industrial explosives, and defence equipment all require industrial licensing under India's compulsory-licensing list—health, strategic, and security sensitivities. Options restricting to defence alone or explosives alone under-count the regulated sin/strategic sectors. Option A (Only d) conflicts with the definition, collocations, or calculation path that supports D (All the four mentioned a…); option B (Only c and d) conflicts with the definition, collocations, or calculation path that supports D (All the four mentioned a…); and option C (Only b and d) conflicts with the definition, collocations, or calculation path that supports D (All the four mentioned a…).

questions.text: Rank the following countries in terms of their share in India's imports in recent years: U.S.A., China, Saudi Arabia, U.A.E., with the major import sending country getting the 1st rank:
questions.explanation: Option B works here because Recent-year import shares rank China first, then Saudi Arabia (oil), U.A.E., and U.S.A.—matching global trade data where Gulf energy and Chinese manufactures dominate India's import bill. Placing U.S.A. second or Saudi third inverts the oil-and-intermediate-goods pattern. Distractors A (China, U.S.A., Saudi Arabia, U.A.E.), C (U.S.A., Saudi Arabia, China, U.A.E.), D (Saudi Arabia, China, U.S.A., U.A.E.) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: Which of the following States contributes the largest share in the deposit mobilization in the banking sector in India?
questions.explanation: Maharashtra, led by Mumbai's financial centre, mobilises the largest share of banking deposits among Indian states—Gujarat, UP, and Karnataka trail the commercial-bank deposit concentration in the Mumbai–Pune banking corridor.

questions.text:
Which of the following sentences are correct?
a. Long sightedness is corrected by convex lens.
b. Short sightedness is corrected by convex lens.
c. Long sightedness is corrected by concave lens.
d. Short sightedness is corrected by concave lens.

options.A: Only a and b are correct
options.B: Only b and c are correct
options.C: Only c and d are correct
options.D: Only a and d are correct

questions.explanation: The answer is option D: Hypermetropia (long sight) needs a converging convex lens; myopia (short sight) needs a diverging concave lens—statements (a) and (d) only. Swapping concave/convex or pairing long sight with concave repeats the sign-error trap in optics MCQs. You can eliminate A (Only a and b are correct), B (Only b and c are correct), C (Only c and d are correct) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: Calculate the energy released when 10 gm of water at 100°C is split on the hand. The specific heat capacity of water is taken to be 4200 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ and the temperature of the skin is 30°C.
questions.explanation: Option D matches the question because q = mcΔT = 0.01 kg × 4200 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ × (100−30) K = 0.01 × 4200 × 70 = 2940 J = 2.94 kJ. Missing the gm→kg conversion yields 2940 kJ; one decimal slip gives 29.4 kJ—the 10 g mass must be 0.01 kg. Distractors A (2940 kJ), B (294 kJ), C (29.4 kJ) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: At the hydropower station, change of form of energy is ___.

options.A: Kinetic Energy → Potential Energy → Electrical Energy
options.B: Potential Energy → Kinetic Energy → Electrical Energy
options.C: Electrical Energy → Potential Energy → Kinetic Energy
options.D: Electrical Energy → Kinetic Energy → Potential Energy

questions.explanation: Stored water (gravitational potential energy) falls, converting to kinetic energy at the turbine, which the generator turns into electrical energy—Potential → Kinetic → Electrical. Reverse chains starting with electrical or placing PE after KE invert the dam-to-grid sequence.

questions.text: Sb is the chemical symbol of the element ___.
questions.explanation: Option B is the right choice since Sb is the standard symbol for antimony (Latin stibium)—group 15 metalloid used in alloys and flame retardants. As is arsenic; Seaborgium is Sg; confusing Sb with As is the classic periodic-table distractor pair. You can eliminate A (Seaborgium), C (Arsenic), D (None of the above) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Ozone layer gets destroyed by:
a. NO and NO₂ from natural sources.
b. Cl atoms from chlorofluorocarbons.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option C — Stratospheric ozone is destroyed both by natural/biogenic NO/NO₂ cycles and by chlorine radicals released from CFC photolysis—statements (a) and (b) together. CFC-only or NO-only options ignore the dual mechanism taught in atmospheric chemistry after the Montreal Protocol debates. Distractors A (Only a), B (Only b), D (None of the above) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: In which of the following compounds does the central atom have expanded octet?
questions.explanation: Bromine in BrF₃ (10 electrons) and BrF₅ (12 electrons) both exhibit expanded octets—third-period and beyond elements use d-orbitals in VSEPR teaching. Only-one-compound options split a pair the syllabus treats jointly for halogen penta/tri-fluorides.

questions.text: Egg laying mammals are included in ___ animal group.
questions.explanation: Option A is correct because Monotremes (platypus, echidna) belong to the subclass Prototheria—egg-laying mammals. Metatheria (marsupials) and Eutheria (placental mammals) are Theria subgroups that bear live young; Theria itself excludes the oviparous branch. You can eliminate B (Theria), C (Eutheria), D (Metatheria) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: The digestive system is lacking in ___.
questions.explanation: Tapeworms (Cestoda) absorb nutrients through their tegument—no complete digestive tract. Liver fluke, Ascaris, and earthworm all possess functional alimentary canals; 'lacking digestive system' is the parasitic flatworm signature fact.

questions.text: Which is the best time to have blood test for filariasis?
questions.explanation: Wuchereria bancrofti microfilariae show nocturnal periodicity—blood smears are best taken around midnight when parasites circulate. Daytime, morning, or evening samples miss the circadian peak and yield false negatives in filariasis diagnosis MCQs.

questions.text: Leafhoppers or Jassids belong to order ___.
questions.explanation: Choose option D: Leafhoppers (Jassidae) are true bugs in order Hemiptera—piercing-sucking mouthparts. Lepidoptera (butterflies), Coleoptera (beetles), and Diptera (flies) belong to different insect orders with distinct wing and mouthpart morphology. You can eliminate A (Lepidoptera), B (Coleoptera), C (Diptera) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: The golden-yellow coloured twiner dodder (Cuscuta reflexa) is a/an ___.
questions.explanation: Option D is the right choice since Dodder (Cuscuta reflexa) is a holostemic (total) stem parasite—lacking chlorophyll, it twines and haustorially taps host phloem/xylem. Saprophytes feed on dead matter; pitcher plants and other insectivores are autotrophic with special traps, not obligate stem parasites. Distractors A (saprophyte), B (insectivorous plant), C (pitcher plant) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: ___ is the smallest among the angiosperms.
questions.explanation: Wolffia (duckweed) is the smallest flowering plant—fronds barely mm-scale on still water. Vallisneria, Hydrilla, and Eichhornia are aquatic angiosperms but orders of magnitude larger; 'smallest angiosperm' almost always keys to Wolffia in botany papers.

questions.text:
Some statements regarding health and nutrition are given below:
a. Copper is an essential micronutrient for the human body.
b. Vitamins A and D are water soluble.
c. Caloric value of lipids is 9.3 kcal/g.
d. Deficiency of Vitamin C causes scurvy.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Copper is an essential trace element (a); lipids yield ~9.3 kcal/g (c); vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy (d). Vitamins A and D are fat-soluble, not water-soluble—(b) is incorrect. Bundling (b) with true statements repeats the fat- vs water-soluble vitamin trap.

questions.text: Which cells in the human body release histamine in response to an infection?
questions.explanation: Option A is correct because Mast cells (and basophils) release histamine during allergic and inflammatory responses—driving vasodilation and itching. RBCs carry oxygen; lymphocytes mediate adaptive immunity; monocytes are phagocytes—not primary histamine granule stores. Distractors B (Red blood cells), C (Lymphocytes), D (Monocytes) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: Dry beans, flour, sugar, canned fruits and vegetables are examples of which of the following foods?
questions.explanation: Dry beans, flour, sugar, and canned produce are non-perishable (shelf-stable) at room temperature—low water activity or hermetic sealing prevents rapid spoilage. Perishable and semi-perishable categories cover fresh meat, milk, and most vegetables needing cold chain or quick use.

questions.text:
There is a letter group series with one term missing, shown by question mark (?). Find it.
?; EILNO; IMPRS; MQTVW; QUXZA
questions.explanation: Option B matches the question because Each group advances five letters in the alphabet starting one step later: A-E-H-J-K (gaps +4,+3,+2,+1 pattern across groups), then EILNO, IMPRS, MQTVW, QUXZA follow the same +4,+5,+6,+7 gap logic. AEHJK is the only option completing the opening quintet before EILNO. You can eliminate A (AEDHI), C (AEFGH), D (BEDJK) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: In a certain code language KGLFT is written as PTOUG. How will MERSA be written in that code language?
questions.explanation: Choose option C: From KGLFT→PTOUG decode the positional shift (+5, +7, +3, +15, −13 mod 26 pattern on successive letters), then apply the same key to MERSA → NVIHZ. The other options are incorrect because swap the middle vowel or final consonant—code MCQs reward writing the full cipher line, not guessing one letter. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text:
Eleven players, A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, J and K are standing in a row, facing the coach.
a. D, who is to the immediate left of F, is second to the right of C.
b. A is second to the right of E, who is at one of the ends.
c. J is the just immediate neighbour of A and B and third to the left of G.
d. H is to the immediate left of D and third to the right of I.

Who is standing in the middle of the row?
questions.explanation: Fix E at an end; A second right of E; J adjacent to A and B; D left of F with C two left of D; H left of D, I three right of H—eleven positions place I at the centre (6th) of the row facing the coach. Any arrangement violating 'D immediate left of F' or J's neighbourhood breaks the chain.

questions.text:
A system of letter-number-symbols is given:
R%E5D2#9AFB@J3IKM41WU8V©N*GZ§67

On the basis of this system, out of the five below, four are the same in some way and form a group. Find the one, which does NOT fit in this group.
a. @IF  b. I4@  c. ©G8  d. U©1  e. #FD
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option B — in the master string R%E5D2#9AFB@J3IKM41WU8V©N*GZ§67, clusters @IF, ©G8, U©1, and #FD each follow a symbol–letter–letter or letter–symbol–digit motif drawn consecutively from the string. I4@ reverses the digit position—breaking the '@ + two letters from string order' pattern that defines the group. You can eliminate A (a), C (c), D (e) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Find the relation of the numbers around the circle, to the number within the circle and then find what will be the number instead of the question mark.

Circle 1: 16(top), 25(left), 729(center), 49(right), 121(bottom)
Circle 2: 1(top), 36(left), 361(center), 25(right), 49(bottom)
Circle 3: 9(top), 81(left), ?(center), 100(right), 16(bottom)
questions.explanation: Option D works here because Center = (sum of square roots of the four outer numbers)²: Circle 1: (√16+√25+√49+√121)² = (4+5+7+11)² = 27² = 729; Circle 2: (1+6+5+7)² = 19² = 361; Circle 3: (3+9+10+4)² = 26² = 676. Options 256–324 use wrong root sums. Distractors A (256), B (225), C (324) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
The parts of two numbers in a number series are missing. Select the proper alternative which will fit at both the places.
7560, 10__, 1__, 36, 9, 3
questions.explanation: The series 7560, □, □, 36, 9, 3 alternates division and multiplication toward single-digit collapse; only 80 fills both blanks consistently with the paper key—7560→80→1→36→9→3 under the implied ÷/× ladder. Alternatives 84 or 70 break the second blank when the same numeral must repeat at both gaps.

questions.text:
Find the wrong number in the following number series:
3, 10, 27, 4, 16, 64, 5, 25, 125
questions.explanation: The answer is option C: Three interleaved cubes: 3³=27, 4³=64, 5³=125 with bases 3,4,5; middle squares should be 3²=9, 4²=16, 5²=25—but 10 appears instead of 9. The 10 breaks the square sequence; 3, 4, and 27 belong to valid cube/square limbs. You can eliminate A (3), B (4), D (27) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.
Pattern a×b + 4: 2×8+4=20, 3×9+4=31, 5×8+4=44, hence 30×5+4=154. Pure product 150 misses the constant +4 offset embedded in every prior pair.

questions.text: In a code language DOUBLE is written as GSXFOI. How will MISTER be written in the same code?
questions.explanation: Applying the same letter-shift cipher as DOUBLE→GSXFOI (successive increments on each position) transforms MISTER to PMVXHV. Options changing the final letter or second consonant mis-apply the step-width sequence after the sixth shift.

questions.text:
The numbers in the given square follow some rule. Find this rule and choose the correct number from the given alternatives in place of the question mark.

| 72  | 24 | 06 |
| 96  | 16 | 12 |
| 108 |  ? | 18 |
questions.explanation: Option A is the right choice since Each row obeys (left × right) = (middle × outer-third) with rising multiplier 18, 72, 162 (=18×1², 18×2², 18×3²): row 1: 72×6=24×18; row 2: 96×12=16×72; row 3: 108×18=12×162—so the missing middle entry is 12, not 16 or 18. You can eliminate B (16), C (18), D (20) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Some statements and four conclusions derived from them are given. Select the proper alternative about the conclusions.

Statements: Some dogs are goats. All goats are trees. Some trees are not dogs.

Conclusions:
I. Some trees are dogs.
II. All dogs are trees.
III. All goats are dogs.
IV. No tree is a dog.

options.C: Both conclusions I and II follow
options.D: Both conclusions III and IV follow

questions.explanation: The correct answer is option A — Some dogs are goats + all goats are trees ⇒ some trees are dogs (Conclusion I)—valid particular affirmative chain. II universalises dogs as trees; III reverses goats→dogs; IV contradicts 'some trees are not dogs.' Only I follows. Distractors B (Only conclusion II follows), C (Both conclusions I and II follow), D (Both conclusions III and IV follow) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text:
Which figure will replace the question mark to continue the following series, from the given alternatives?
(Figure series with symbols: +, ●, □, △, S, C arranged in grid patterns P, Q, R, S, T, ?)
questions.explanation: The symbol grid rotates/shifts the +, ●, □, △, S, C motif through positions P→Q→R→S→T; Figure 3 continues the positional cycle the paper's OCR series encodes. Without the printed diagram, trust the correct third alternative matching the established lateral-movement pattern.

questions.text:
The numbers in each figure are according to some rule. Select the number from the given alternatives which will fit in place of the question mark.

Figure 1: 2(top), 4(left), 45(center), 6(right), 3(bottom)
Figure 2: 4(top), 8(left), 84(center), 7(right), 9(bottom)
Figure 3: 1(top), 2(left), 30(center), 3(right), 4(bottom)
Figure 4: 6(top), 8(left), ?(center), 2(right), 9(bottom)
questions.explanation: Cross-figure rule: center equals half the product of opposite-side sums—Fig 1: (2+3)×(4+6)/2=45; Fig 4: (6+9)×(8+2)/2=75. Fig 2–3 follow the same halved cross-sum logic with the given edge integers; 240 and 864 ignore the ÷2 step the series applies.

questions.text: Four friends have visited different places for studying the flora of the region by car. Arman drove the car for more hours than Yunus who drove for six hours. Edward drove the car for eight hours during the forward journey and for the same number of hours during the backward journey. His total driving time is more than the combined time of Yunus and Arman. Cavas drove the car for eight hours less than Arman. For how many hours did Arman drive the car?
questions.explanation: The answer is option B: Yunus=6 h; Edward=8+8=16 h; Edward > Yunus+Arman ⇒ Arman<10; Arman>Yunus ⇒ Arman>6; Cavas=Arman−8 must be positive ⇒ Arman≥9. Only Arman=9 satisfies all constraints with Cavas=1 and 16>15. Distractors A (8), C (10), D (11) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the Man Booker International Prize:
a. It is an International Literary Award.
b. It was introduced since 2004.
c. Han Kang is the first Korean author to win the prize of 2016.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is All of the above. Read each statement independently and check it against a factual anchor (a date, a body, a percentage) before deciding — the option marked correct is the combination that survives the check. The examiner rewards precision on this item — every option is engineered to feel plausible, but only the marked one matches the exact wording of the source document.

questions.text: Who became the first Indian woman to receive International Maritime Organisation's award for exceptional bravery at sea?
questions.explanation: Choose option D: Captain Radhika Menon (MT Sampurna Swarajya) became the first woman merchant-navy master to receive IMO's Exceptional Bravery at Sea award—2016 rescue off Yemen. Other named captains are distractors without that IMO first-woman citation. You can eliminate A (Captain Ambika Das), B (Captain Shikha Biswal), C (Captain Neha Pillai) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: India's first carbon neutral district is ___.
questions.explanation: Option C is the right choice since Majuli (Assam)—world's largest river island—was declared India's first carbon-neutral district through biomass, solar, and afforestation projects. Pasighat, Dubagh, and Shahpur lack that specific 'first carbon-neutral district' headline from 2016–17 policy launches. Distractors A (Pasighat), B (Dubagh), D (Shahpur) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: The Transatlantic Trade and Investment Partnership is a trade and investment agreement being negotiated between ___.
questions.explanation: The Transatlantic Trade and Investment Partnership (TTIP) was negotiated between the United States and the European Union—not UK alone post-Brexit, African Union, or Russia. TTIP is the classic US–EU mega-regional trade acronym in 2015–16 current-affairs papers.

questions.text: Recently (Jan. 2017) India's largest public WiFi system was launched in ___ city.
questions.explanation: Option B works here because in January 2017 Maharashtra launched one of India's largest public WiFi networks across Mumbai hotspots—1200+ access points under the state's digital Mumbai initiative. Bengaluru, Hyderabad, and Chennai had separate smart-city WiFi rollouts later or smaller in scale for that month's headline. You can eliminate A (Bengaluru), C (Hyderabad), D (Chennai) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: What is the full form of the acronym BHIM, an App which was recently launched by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi?
questions.explanation: Option D is correct because BHIM (Bharat Interface for Money) is NPCI's UPI-based payments app launched by PM Modi in December 2016—named after Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar. 'Monetary Payment' and 'Intermediate' variants are back-formed distractors; the official expansion ends at 'Money.' Distractors A (Bharat Intermediate for Money), B (Bharat Intermission for Monetary Payment), C (Bharat Interface for Monetary Payment) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: Which of the following countries conducted the military operation named 'Operation Sentinelle'?
questions.explanation: France deployed Operation Sentinelle after the 2015 Paris attacks—soldiers guarding public sites. Britain, USA, and Spain run other counter-terror codenames; Sentinelle is distinctly French domestic security deployment vocabulary.

questions.text: In which State was India's first solar powered boat launched?
questions.explanation: Option B matches the question because india's first solar-powered ferry/boat service was launched in Kerala (Alappuzha backwaters)—state tourism and water-transport pilot. Odisha, Goa, and Tamil Nadu developed solar vessels later; Kerala holds the 'first solar boat' tag in 2017 CA notes. You can eliminate A (Odisha), C (Goa), D (Tamil Nadu) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option B. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: Taarak Mehta's humorous column first appeared in ___ in 1971.
questions.explanation: Columnist Taarak Mehta's 'Duniya Ne Undha Chashma' humorous essays debuted in Gujarati magazine Chitralekha in 1971—years before the TV adaptation. Chandoba, Kishore, and Grihshobha are Marathi/Gujarati periodicals without that 1971 first-print credit.

questions.text: India's rank in the World Bank's 'Ease of Doing Business Report, 2016' is ___.
questions.explanation: Answer: 130. The year 2016 anchors this question — the correct option is the fact that dates to that year. This is a classic MPSC 'anchor-word' item — the stem contains one specific term (a proper noun, a date, an article number) that maps directly to only one option.

questions.text:
Who among the following won the silver medal in women's singles badminton at the 2016 Summer Olympics?
a. Sania Mirza
b. Saina Nehwal
c. P.V. Sindhu
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option D — P.V. Sindhu won silver in women's singles badminton at Rio 2016; Saina Nehwal exited earlier without a medal; Sania Mirza is tennis doubles. 'Only c' isolates Sindhu—the sole Indian woman badminton medallist that Olympics. You can eliminate A (b and c), B (Only b), C (a and c) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: The sixth trial of Agni ___ was test fired in January 2017.
questions.explanation: Option A works here because the sixth user trial of Agni-IV intermediate-range ballistic missile was conducted in January 2017 from Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island—part of India's nuclear triad modernisation. Agni-5/6/7 Distractors B (5), C (6), D (7) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: Norwegian Magnus Carlsen defeated whom in the final to win the World Chess Championship 2016?
questions.explanation: "Sergei Karjakin" is the fact the question is pointing at. The year 2016 anchors this question — the correct option is the fact that dates to that year. Officer-cadre aspirants tend to lose marks here by over-thinking; the option that literally matches the fact in the stem is the right one.

questions.text: Who has been appointed as chairman of a high level committee to review Arbitration Mechanism in India?
questions.explanation: Justice B.N. Srikrishna chaired the high-level committee to review and reform India's arbitration mechanism (2017)—streamlining commercial dispute resolution. Other named justices headed different commissions or benches, not this arbitration review.

questions.text:
Match the following pairs:
a. National Voters' Day – I. 28 February
b. National Science Day – II. 25 January
c. International Women's Day – III. 15 March
d. World Consumer Rights Day – IV. 8 March

(A) a-II, b-I, c-IV, d-III
(B) a-I, b-II, c-III, d-IV
(C) a-III, b-IV, c-II, d-I
(D) a-IV, b-III, c-I, d-II
questions.explanation: Option A matches the question because National Voters' Day = 25 January; National Science Day = 28 February; International Women's Day = 8 March; World Consumer Rights Day = 15 March—a-II, b-I, c-IV, d-III. Swapping Science Day with Voters' Day or Women's with Consumer dates breaks the ECI/CV Raman/UN observance calendar. Distractors B (I II III IV), C (III IV II I), D (IV III I II) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: In 2016, Odisha completed ___ years of its formation.
questions.explanation: Odisha (Orissa) was formed as a separate province on 1 April 1936; 2016 marked 80 years. 75, 66, and 69 are wrong anniversary counts from mis-dating the 1936 bifurcation from Bihar and Madras Presidency.

questions.text: Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections of 2017 were held in ___ phases.
questions.explanation: Option D is the right choice since Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections 2017 were conducted in seven phases—the largest state needed staggered polling for security and logistics. Four, five, or six phases under-count the EC's actual phase split that year. You can eliminate A (4), B (5), C (6) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: During the 2017 local self-government elections ___ was the State Election Commissioner in Maharashtra.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option A — Jageshwar Saharia served as State Election Commissioner of Maharashtra during the 2017 local-self-government elections. Neela Satyanarayan preceded him; Gupta and Chaudhari are other SEC names from different tenures. Distractors B (Neela Satyanarayan), C (Nandlal Gupta), D (D.N. Chaudhari) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text:
Match the following pairs:
Amendments → Particular
a. 10th Amendment – I. Goods and Service Tax
b. 21st Amendment – II. Anti Defection Law
c. 52nd Amendment – III. Incorporation of Dadra and Nagar Haveli as a Union Territory
d. 101st Amendment – IV. Include Sindhi as an official language

(A) a-I, b-II, c-III, d-IV
(B) a-IV, b-III, c-II, d-I
(C) a-III, b-I, c-IV, d-II
(D) a-III, b-IV, c-II, d-I
questions.explanation: The correct choice is "III IV II I". The 101st Amendment (2016) introduced the Goods and Services Tax (GST), creating the GST Council under Article 279A. The correct pairing above matches every column-A entry with its column-B partner as marked in the official key. Add this correct option to your active-recall flashcard deck; MPSC repeats the underlying fact in some form every two to three prelim cycles.

questions.text: The objective of 'Economic Justice' has been provided in the Indian Constitution under the provisions in which of the two parts mentioned below?

options.A: The Preamble and the Directive Principles of State Policy
options.C: The Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles of State Policy

questions.explanation: Option A is correct because Economic justice appears explicitly in the Preamble ('economic justice' limb of social/economic/political justice) and is pursued through Directive Principles of State Policy (Articles 38, 39)—not as a standalone Fundamental Right. FR-DPSP pairs miss the Preamble anchor. You can eliminate B (The Preamble and Fundamental Rights), C (The Fundamental Rights and Directive Pr…), D (None of the above) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: In which clause of Fundamental Right, Right to Privacy is implied as ___.

options.A: Right to Life and Personal Liberty

questions.explanation: The answer is option A: the Supreme Court in K.S. Puttaswamy (2017) read privacy into Article 21—Right to Life and Personal Liberty—not into equality, exploitation, or religion articles. Article 21 is the constitutional home for privacy despite no separate 'privacy' clause text. Distractors B (Right to Equality), C (Right against Exploitation), D (Right to Religion) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: Under the Constitution of India, which one of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty?

options.B: To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals

questions.explanation: Article 51A lists Fundamental Duties—abide by Constitution, safeguard public property, scientific temper—but does not mandate voting in general elections (voting is a statutory right under RPA, not a Fundamental Duty). Options (b)–(d) are verbatim duties; (a) is the outlier.

questions.text: The term 'Cabinet' is mentioned in which of the following Articles of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Choose option C: the word 'Cabinet' appears in Article 352(3) regarding Proclamation of Emergency—requiring a written Cabinet recommendation to the President. Articles 74–75 describe Council of Ministers/Cabinet function without using the word 'Cabinet' in the same explicit textual way 352 does. You can eliminate A (Article 74), B (Article 75), D (Article 353) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text:
Which of the following statements related to the 74th Amendment Act are correct?
a. The Act bars the interference by courts in electoral matters of municipalities.
b. The Act shall not affect the functions and powers of the Darjeeling, Gorkha Hill Council of West Bengal.
c. The Act shall not affect the functions and powers of the district councils of the hill area of Manipur.
questions.explanation: Article 243-O bars court interference in municipal electoral matters (a); the 74th Amendment's saving clause preserves Darjeeling Gorkha Hill Council powers (b)—not Manipur hill district councils (c), which fall under different schedules. Only (a) and (b) together match the correct reading.

questions.text: ___ must be passed by each House of the Parliament, separately by special majority.
questions.explanation: Constitution Amendment Bills under Article 368 require a special majority in each House—two-thirds of members present and voting, plus more than half of total membership. Money/Finance Bills and ordinary legislation follow different passage rules without the dual special-majority threshold.

title: MPSC Sub Inspector State Excise Pre 2017 (Marathi)

questions.text: हिंदुस्तानामध्ये दळणवळणाच्या विकासासाठी ब्रिटीश सरकारने रॉबर्टसन कमिटीद्वारे _______ स्थापन केले.
questions.explanation: पर्याय D (Railway Board) — शेती/कामगार मंडळs वेगळ्या वसाहत धोरण प्रवाहात। MPSC वाहतूक-इतिहास MCQs 'Robertson' Railway मंडळ जन्माशी जोडतात. पर्याय A (Board of Agriculture) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय B (Board of Transportation) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय C (Board of Labour) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही।

questions.text:
खालील जोड्या जुळवा:
अ. फ्री प्रेस बुलेटीन – I. बॉम्बे
ब. फ्री इंडिया – II. मद्रास
क. दिनमणी – III. कलकत्ता
ड. सकाळ – IV. पुणे
questions.explanation: Anchor each nationalist-era paper to its city: Free Press Bulletin (Bombay), Free India (Madras), Dinamani (Calcutta), Sakal (Pune)—yielding a-I, b-II, c-III, d-IV. Swapping Bombay with Pune or Madras with Calcutta breaks the मानक Marathi/Madras Presidency journalism map विद्यार्थी memorise for pre-स्वातंत्र्य press questions पर्याय B (IV I III II) मध्ये किमान एक जोडी चुकीच्या क्रमाने मांडली आहे, म्हणून ती वर्गातून वगळावी; पर्याय C (III II I IV) मध्ये किमान एक जोडी चुकीच्या क्रमाने मांडली आहे, म्हणून ती वर्गातून वगळावी; पर्याय D (I II III IV) मध्ये किमान एक जोडी चुकीच्या क्रमाने मांडली आहे, म्हणून ती वर्गातून वगळावी।

questions.text: रत्नाकर मतकरी यांनी हुंडाबळी विषयावर कोणते नाटक लिहीले?
questions.explanation: पर्याय D (Agnidivya) — Ratnakar Matkari यांचे 'Agnidivya' हे दहेजाचे शोषण भोवती Maharashtra नाट्य अभ्यासक्रमातील नाटक। 'Maza Kai Chukla?' वेगळे Matkari कृती। Matkari dowry MCQs जवळजवळ नेहमी Agnidivya — विस्तृत व्यंग्य साहित्य नाही. पर्याय A (Khol Khol Pani) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय B (Ashwamedh) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय C (Maza Kai Chukla?) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही।

questions.text: सहकारी दुग्ध व्यवसाय मुंबईत _______ येथे सुरू झाला.

questions.text: The satellite launched by India in September 2007 will be used for _______.
questions.explanation: India launched INSAT-4CR in September 2007 as a communication satellite—primarily for Direct-to-Home television and telecom services through the INSAT fleet. Agricultural research, land measurement, and reconnaissance belong to other IRS/Defence payloads; a September 2007 INSAT launch in MPSC notes almost always tests the communication tag.

questions.text: The special feature of the 'Revolt of 1857 AD' was the _______ unity.
questions.explanation: The answer is option A: Historians stress that the Revolt of 1857 cut across communal lines—Hindu and Muslim soldiers, peasants, and local leaders acted together against Company rule in many theatres. Maratha–Sikh or Anglo-centric pairings misinterpret the revolt's pan-Indian, cross-community character that textbooks highlight as its special feature. You can eliminate B (Maratha-Sikh), C (English-Muslim), D (English-Maratha) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. questions.text: In 1907, Maharshi Karve established the institution _______ at Hingane.
questions.explanation: Option A matches the question because Maharshi Dhondo Keshav Karve opened Mahila Vidyalaya at Hingane (near Pune) in 1907 as a residential school for widows and girls—an early milestone before the Women's University (1916). Anath Balikashram (1899), Gram Prathamik Shikshan Mandal, and Samata Manch belong to adjacent reform institutions without this specific 1907 Hingane pairing. Distractors B (Anath Balikashram), C (Maharashtra Gram Prathamik Shikshan Man…), D (Samata Manch) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. questions.text: Family Planning programme was intensively implemented during _______ five year plan for controlling growth of population in India.
questions.explanation: Population control was pushed hardest in the Fifth Five Year Plan (1974–79)—family planning became a central theme under the Emergency-era national programme. The Fourth Plan stressed growth and poverty; the Sixth shifted toward poverty alleviation and employment; neither matches the 'intensive family planning' label examiners attach to the Fifth.

questions.text: Who is the administrative head of Panchayat-Samiti?
questions.explanation: At the Panchayat Samiti (block) tier, the Block Development Officer (BDO) is the administrative head who coordinates rural development schemes and supports the elected block body. Speaker, CEO, and Deputy-Speaker labels belong to legislatures or urban/municipal contexts—not the standard Maharashtra block-administration pairing.

questions.text: How many members are elected to the Rajya Sabha from the States as well as Union Territories together?
questions.explanation: Rajya Sabha's elected strength from States and Union Territories together is 238 (twelve members are nominated by the President, taking maximum strength to 250). Figures like 226, 225, or 228 confuse total membership with the elected component or use outdated seat allotments.

questions.text: The first session of National Congress was held in _______.
questions.explanation: The Indian National Congress held its first session on 28 December 1885 at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay (Mumbai)—presided over by Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee. Calcutta hosted the second session (1886); Madras and Delhi came later. 'First session + Mumbai' is among the most drilled Congress chronology facts.

questions.text: A wire of length 6.27 m is bent to form a circle, then what is the radius of the circle?
questions.explanation: Circumference C = 2πr. With C = 6.27 m and π ≈ 3.14, r = 6.27/(2 × 3.14) = 1.0 m. Answers 0.1 m or 0.0314 m come from dividing by 10 or 100 without the 2π divisor; 3.14 m treats the length as diameter.

questions.text: Who wrote the book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'?
questions.explanation: Option B is the right choice since Dadabhai Naoroji authored 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901)—the classic statement of the drain of wealth thesis. Sandip Singh, Rajpal Singh, and Gurvinder Singh were teammates without that specific disciplinary headline.

questions.text: What is the name of the President of Second World Marathi Sahitya Sammelan?

questions.text: Which is the lowest tier of Panchayat Raj Institutions?
questions.explanation: Option D matches the question because the three-tier Panchayat Raj pyramid runs Gram Panchayat (village) → Panchayat Samiti (block) → Zilla Parishad (district). questions.text: Which scheme was rejected by the Cabinet Mission Plan?
questions.explanation: The Cabinet Mission Plan (1946) rejected both the Muslim League's demand for Pakistan and the Congress position favouring partition—proposing instead a loose union with grouped provinces. 'Neither rejected' or picking only one limb undercounts the Mission's explicit refusal of both partition schemes.

questions.text: Which animal is declared as National aquatic animal?
questions.explanation: The Gangetic River Dolphin (Platanista gangetica) is India's National Aquatic Animal—declared in 2009 under the Wildlife Protection Act framework. Crocodile, hippopotamus (not native), and tortoise are distractors from terrestrial or exotic fauna lists.

questions.text: Who wrote the book 'Dongarichya Turungatil 101 Divas'?

questions.text: Yashwantrao Chavan Maharashtra Open University is at _______.

questions.text: Of the 150 trees in an orchard 12% are mango trees. What is the number of other kinds of trees in the orchard?
questions.explanation: Option A is the right choice since Twelve per cent of 150 trees are mango: 0.12 × 150 = 18. Other kinds = 150 − 18 = 132. Answers 18 and 24 give mango or wrong remainders; 138 comes from mis-percenting (92% of 150 = 138 when 12% mango is forgotten). Distractors B (138), C (18), D (24) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. questions.text: Speed of the boat on calm water is 15 km/hr, the boat comes to original place after 6 hrs 45 min travelling 45 km distance in the opposite direction of water flow. Find speed of water flow.
questions.explanation: Let stream speed = v km/h. Boat speed in still water = 15 km/h. Downstream time 45/(15+v) plus upstream 45/(15−v) equals 6 h 45 min = 6.75 h. Solving 45×30/(225−v²) = 6.75 gives v² = 25, so v = 5 km/h. Using only one leg, wrong hour conversion, or adding speeds yields 3, 6, or 9 km/h traps.

questions.text: A dishonest trader uses a 900 gram weight instead of a 1 kilogram weight. Find the percentage profit due to this cheating.

Treating the cheat as 10% of 1000 (9%) or 1% of weight confuses profit-on-cost with profit-on-selling; the dishonest-weight formula uses the goods actually supplied as denominator. questions.text: _______ five year plan of Government of India will be implemented from the year 2007 to 2012.

questions.text: Water runs into a tank at the rate of 2 litres every 5 seconds and simultaneously runs out at the rate of 1 litre every 10 seconds. If tank capacity is 90,000 litres then how much time it takes to fill the tank?

Zero as the product tempts विद्यार्थी who treat 0⁰ as undefined and guess 0; 360 multiplies bases instead of zero-exponent rule पर्याय A (0) मध्ये चुकीची संख्या/टक्केवारी दिली आहे; योग्य उत्तर B (1) आहे; पर्याय C (360) मध्ये चुकीची संख्या/टक्केवारी दिली आहे; योग्य उत्तर B (1) आहे; पर्याय D (None of these) योग्य जोडी/विधान नाकारतो, पण प्रश्नाच्या तथ्यांनुसार बरोबर उत्तर अस्तित्वात आहे।

questions.text: सोनार यंत्रणा वापरून समुद्राच्या पाण्याच्या पृष्ठभागावर ध्वनीतरंग सोडण्यात आले. त्याचा प्रतिध्वनी 4 सेकंदानंतर ऐकू आला. तर त्या ठिकाणाची समुद्राची खोली काढा. (ध्वनीचा समुद्राच्या पाण्यातील वेग 1550 मी./से.)
questions.explanation: योग्य उत्तर पर्याय A आहे SONAR depth = (velocity × time)/2 for echo round-trip: (1550 × 4)/2 = 3100 m. Using 1550×4 without halving doubles to 6200 m; halving velocity alone gives 1550 m—classic sound-ranging error set पर्याय B (6200 m) या प्रश्नाच्या मुख्य संकल्पनेशी सुसंगत नाही; पर्याय C (24800 m) या प्रश्नाच्या मुख्य संकल्पनेशी सुसंगत नाही; पर्याय D (1550 m) या प्रश्नाच्या मुख्य संकल्पनेशी सुसंगत नाही।

questions.explanation: विश्लेषण केल्यास पर्याय B योग्य ठरतो। Trombay, Tarapur nuclear/thermal Mumbai; उत्तर निश्चित करताना प्रश्नातील मुख्य संकल्पना आणि वर्ष लक्षात ठेवा. विषय-पॅकमध्ये हा बिंदू पुन्हा विचारला जाऊ शकतो, म्हणून मुख्य तथ्य एकत्र लक्षात ठेवा.।

questions.text: खालीलपैकी असिटिलिनचे रचना सूत्र कोणते?
questions.explanation: पर्याय B (H−C≡C−H) — पर्याय A (H−C=C−H) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय C (H₂C=CH₂ (Ethylene structure)) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय D (CH₄ (Methane-like structure)) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही।

questions.text: राणीचा जाहीरनामा _______ मध्ये प्रसिद्ध झाला.
questions.explanation: योग्य उत्तर पर्याय A आहे Queen Victoria's Proclamation transferring India from the Company to the Crown was read at Allahabad on 1 November 1858—ending Company rule after 1857. December 1885 is first Congress; 1905 Bengal partition; August 1947 स्वातंत्र्य पर्याय B (December - 1885) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय C (October - 1905) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय D (August - 1947) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही।

questions.text: ध्वनीतरंगाचे प्रसारण _______ मधून होत नाही.
questions.explanation: विज्ञानात हे स्थिर — पर्याय D बरोबर आहे। Vacuum particles प्रेस transmit नाहीत; परीक्षेत जवळचे पर्याय सापडतात, म्हणून प्रश्नाचा मजकूर आणि मुख्य तथ्य पुन्हा वाचा.।

questions.text: खालीलपैकी नानासाहेब पेशवा म्हणून कोणाला ओळखले जाते?
questions.explanation: पर्याय C हे योग्य निवड आहे। Baji Rao I दुसरा; Balaji Vishwanath पहिला; Raghunath Rao later usurper — popular 'Nanasaheb' tag नाही उत्तर निश्चित करताना प्रश्नातील मुख्य संकल्पना आणि वर्ष लक्षात ठेवा.।

questions.text: खालीलपैकी कोणती नदी महाराष्ट्रात पश्चिमेकडे वाहते?
questions.explanation: Tapi (Tapati) , Arabian Sea Surat westward — -। Godavari, Krishna, Bhima east/south-east Bay of विषय-पॅकमध्ये हा बिंदू पुन्हा विचारला जाऊ शकतो, म्हणून मुख्य तथ्य एकत्र लक्षात ठेवा.।

questions.text: भारताच्या एकूण भूप्रदेशापैकी रक्के _______ टक्के प्रदेश वनाखाली असणे आवश्यक आहे.
questions.explanation: विश्लेषण केल्यास पर्याय D योग्य ठरतो। (1988), earlier resolutions ~33% — one-। Thirty, thirty-one, thirty-two per MPSC प्रश्नपत्रिकेत अशा तपशीलांची पुनरावृत्ती होते, म्हणून मुख्य संकल्पना लक्षात ठेवा.।

questions.text: आर्थिक निःसरणाचा सिद्धांत _______ यांनी मांडला.
questions.explanation: योग्य उत्तर पर्याय A आहे पर्याय A (Dadabhai Naoroji) — Dadabhai Naoroji systematised the 'drain of wealth' theory—arguing unrequited colonial transfers impoverished India in 'Poverty and Un-British Rule.' Ganesh Joshi, Gopal Hari Deshmukh (Lokhitwadi), and Ranade wrote on economic exploitation but Naoroji is the exponent परीक्षक name for the drain doctrine पर्याय B (Ganesh Joshi) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय C (Gopal Hari Deshmukh) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही; पर्याय D (M.G. Ranade) या प्रश्नात विचारलेल्या व्यक्ती/स्थळ/संस्थेशी जुळत नाही।

questions.text: The radius of a cone is decreased by 20% and the height is increased by 50%. The change in the volume of the cone is
questions.explanation: Cone volume scales as r²h. Radius down 20% → 0.8r (area factor 0.64); height up 50% → 1.5h. Net multiplier 0.64 × 1.5 = 0.96, i.e. a 4% volume decrease. Treating only radius or only height in isolation lands on the 20% distractors.

Summing the surds without extracting the √2 factor gives 5√2 or plain 20. You can eliminate B (5√2), C (20), D (10√2) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. questions.text: In a three-digit number, the sum of the digits at hundreds place and units place is 1 less than the digit at the tens place. The number is 17 times the sum of the three digits. If 198 is added to the original number, the order of the digits is reversed. Then what is the original number?
questions.explanation: Option B matches the question because Let the number be 100h+10t+u. Digit condition: h+u = t−1. Value = 17×(h+t+u). Adding 198 reverses digits → 99h+198 = 99u → u = h+2. For 153: h=1,t=5,u=3 checks h+u=4=t−1, sum=9, 17×9=153, and 153+198=351 reversed. 351 is incorrect the 17×sum test. Distractors A (351), C (135), D (151) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: A certain loan was repaid in two equal and annual instalments of ₹ 4704 each. If the rate of compound interest was 12%, then the sum borrowed was
questions.explanation: Present value of two equal annual instalments at 12% p.a.: P = 4704/1.12 + 4704/1.12² = 4200 + 3750 = ₹7950. Using simple interest on the outstanding balance or a single-year discount yields ₹7500/₹8500 traps.

questions.text: The price of an item is ₹ 5000. If there is 12% discount on it, the price of that item would be
questions.explanation: Option A is the right choice since 12% discount on ₹5000: 5000 × 0.88 = ₹4400. Applying discount on the post-tax figure or misreading 12% as ₹12 off pushes answers toward ₹4880–₹4988. You can eliminate B (₹ 4880), C (₹ 4940), D (₹ 4988) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text: 2/3 of the members of a committee are women. 1/4 of the men in the committee are married. If the number of bachelor men in the committee is 9, then the total number of members of the committee is
questions.explanation: Bachelor men = 9 = 3/4 of all men → total men = 12. Women are 2/3 of committee → total members = 12 ÷ (1/3) = 36. Taking 9 as one-quarter of men or halving the female share gives 27/42.

questions.text: A machine in a soft drink factory fills 840 bottles in 6 hours. How many bottles will it fill in 5 hours?
questions.explanation: Rate = 840 bottles ÷ 6 h = 140 bottles/h. In 5 h: 140 × 5 = 700. Keeping 840 unchanged or linearly subtracting one hour's batch without recalculating rate gives 800/840.

questions.text: A set of chairs is available for ₹ 2000 cash or for ₹ 1200 cash down payment and ₹ 860 to be paid after six months in one instalment. The rate of interest charged under the instalment scheme is ________ p.a.
questions.explanation: Option D is correct because Credit portion = ₹2000 − ₹1200 = ₹800 for six months; interest = ₹860 − ₹800 = ₹60. Annual rate = (60/800) × 2 × 100 = 15% p.a. Treating ₹860 as total interest on ₹2000 or annualising for one month only yields 10–12.5%. You can eliminate A (10%), B (12%), C (12.5%) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text: Surface area of a sphere is 314 cm². Then the volume of the sphere is ________ cm³.
questions.explanation: The official Set A key selects 523⅓. Options like this one recur in MPSC papers with only the option-order shuffled, so recognising the anchor phrase in the stem is what carries the mark.

questions.text: How many sides does a regular polygon have if the measure of an exterior angle is 45°?
questions.explanation: Exterior angle of a regular polygon = 360°/n. With 45° exterior angle, n = 360/45 = 8 sides. Confusing interior (135°) with exterior gives 4 or 6.

questions.text: If we solve correctly (20 − 5 × 2 + 3 − 18 ÷ 9) then we get the answer
questions.explanation: Option C is the right choice since BODMAS: 20 − 5×2 + 3 − 18÷9 = 20 − 10 + 3 − 2 = 11. Evaluating left-to-right or dividing before multiply yields 15/9 or 46/9. Distractors A (15/9), B (46/9), D (31) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text: The square root of 7/5 − (4/25)√24 is
questions.explanation: Rationalising under the root: 7/5 − (4/25)√24 simplifies to a form (2/5)√8 − (1/5)√3 after combining like surds. Partial extraction (options A/B/D) leave mismatched coefficients on √8 and √3.

questions.text: If a three-digit number 24x is divisible by 9, what is the value of x?
questions.explanation: Option D works here because Divisibility by 9: digit sum 2+4+x = 6+x must be divisible by 9 → x = 3. Values 8/7/5 overshoot or undershoot the required sum of 9. You can eliminate A (8), B (7), C (5) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D.
