Answer Options:
questions.explanation: The correct answer is option C — atomic size increases down a group (a) and decreases across a period left to right (b). Distractors A (Only a), B (Only b), D ((a) and b incorrect) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about periodic tables.
(a) Elements in the same period can have different orbits.
(b) As we go from left to right in periods, metallic properties decrease and
non-metallic properties increase.
(c) As we go down along the group, metallic properties increase and non-
metallic properties decrease.
Answer Options:
questions.explanation: The definitive answer is (b) and c correct. The Read each statement independently and check it against a factual anchor (a date, a body, a percentage) before deciding — the option marked correct is the combination that survives the check. The MPSC pattern for questions of this type is to plant one exact fact and three plausible-looking alternatives; the fact-based option is always the answer.

questions.text:
Modern periodic table depends upon .............
(a) Properties
(b) Existence of elements triad
(c) Atomic mass
(d) none of the above
Answer Options:
questions.explanation: Option D is correct because Modern periodic law is based on atomic number — none of (a)(b)(c) alone is the answer per key. You can eliminate A (a), B (b), C (c) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: The one mole of substance means ?
questions.explanation: The answer is option B: One mole = 6.022 × 10²³ particles (Avogadro's number). Distractors A (6.022×1022), C (6.022×1024), D (6.022×1021 Question Question 1. 2 16. 1…) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text:
Observe the following statements and choose the correct statement
option.
(a) Like animals, plants have respiration, nutrition, excretion but lack of
coordinated action.
(b) Human has circulatory system while plant has transport system.
(c) Plants require more energy than animals.
Choose the correct statement/s.
questions.explanation: Statement (a) overreaches: plants do carry out respiration, nutrition, and excretion, but they also show coordinated responses through hormones, tropisms, and turgor-driven movements—so 'lack of coordinated action' is syllabus-inaccurate. Statement (c) reverses the energy picture: animals are far more metabolically active per unit mass than sessile plants. Statement (b) cleanly contrasts human circulatory flow with the plant vascular (xylem–phloem) transport system—the only limb that stands alone.

questions.text:
Observe the following statements about Diffusion and choose the option
correct is not incorrect.
(a) Inhibition is the attraction of water by a substance having water attraction.
(b) Diffusion is the movement of atoms from a more concentrated solution to a
less concentrated solution.
(c) No energy is expended in diffusion.

options.D: All of the above are correct.

questions.explanation: The answer is option D: Read 'not incorrect' as 'correct'. (a) uses the garbled label 'Inhibition' for imbibition—the passive uptake of water by dry colloids such as seeds and wood; that definition is accepted in this paper set. (b) states diffusion moves particles from higher to lower concentration along the gradient. (c) marks diffusion as passive—no metabolic ATP spend. All three limbs survive together, so rejecting any single pair overlooks the double-negative framing. You can eliminate A (Only (a) and (b)), B (Only (b) and (c)), C (Only (a) and (c)) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Swelling of raisins after keeping them in water is........... action and
reduction in size of grapes in sugar water is........... action.
questions.explanation: Option B matches the question because Pure water has higher water potential than the raisin cell sap, so water enters the grape tissue by endosmosis and the fruit swells. Concentrated sugar solution lowers external water potential; water leaves the grape by exosmosis and it shrinks. Swapping the terms (A) or inserting reverse osmosis (C) confuses direction of solvent flow with active pressure-driven filtration. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Check the correctness of the following statements and select the correct
statement/s regarding vessels in plants..
(a) Transport of water and minerals in root plants takes place through Phloem.
(b) Water and minerals flow only in unidirectional.
(c) Transport of organic compounds and other fluids takes place in many
directions.
questions.explanation: Xylem—not phloem—carries water and dissolved minerals upward from roots; statement (a) assigns the wrong tissue. Mineral mass flow in xylem is essentially unidirectional (roots → shoot), while phloem translocation of organic solutes is multidirectional (source to sink). Options keeping (a) as correct mis-map the two vascular highways.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about Arnon's and Stout (1939)
criteria for essential nutrients.
(a) Deficiency of essential nutrient elements makes it impossible for plant to
complete the vegetative or reproductive stage.
(b) Deficiency can be corrected only by supplying that particular element.
(c) Deficiency can be corrected by supplying other similar element.
(d) Must have direct influence on plant nutrition and metabolism.

options.A: Only (a), (b) and (d) are correct, (c) is incorrect
options.B: Only (a), (b) and (c) are correct, (d) is incorrect
options.C: Only (a), (c) and (d) are correct, (b) is incorrect
options.D: All of the above is correct

questions.explanation: Option A is the right choice since arnon and Stout (1939) require that deficiency blocks normal life-cycle completion (a), that only the missing element cures the disorder—not a substitute (b), and that the element act directly in nutrition/metabolism (d). Statement (c) violates the specificity rule: similar elements cannot replace a true essential. Partial triplets that retain (c) break the classical criteria list. You can eliminate B (Only (a), (b) and (c) are correct, (d) …), C (Only (a), (c) and (d) are correct, (b) …), D (All of the above is correct) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text:
Match the correct pairs.
(a) Macronutrients | i) Carbon, Hydrogen
(b) Critical elements | ii) Sulphur, magnesium
(c) Micronutrients | iii) Nitrogen, Potassium
(d) Framework elements | iv) Iron, magnesium.
questions.explanation: Lock one anchor: framework elements are C, H, O—the structural skeleton of organic matter (i). Macronutrients needed in larger amounts include N and K (iii); S and Mg also sit in the macro set (ii). Micronutrients such as Fe appear in trace doses (iv)—note Mg appears in both macro and micro lists in some texts, but the correct grid is a→ii, b→iii, c→iv, d→i. Any option placing C,H under micronutrients or Fe under framework is incorrect the pairing logic.

questions.text:
The steps of light reactions are given in the following options. Put
those alternatives in the correct order in the light reaction.
(a) Absorption of light
(b) Dissociation of oxygen from water.
(c) Formation of high energy intermediates
(d) Dissociation of water molecule.
questions.explanation: Light reactions begin with pigment absorption of photons (a), then photolysis splits water (d), releasing O₂ (b), while high-energy intermediates (ATP, NADPH) form (c). Sequences that photolyse before absorption or place intermediate formation before water split break the Z-scheme chronology memorised for MPSC botany.

questions.text:
Study the following statements regarding glycolysis.
(a) Glycolysis is a series of biochemical reactions.
(b) Glycolysis is a reaction that takes place in the nucleus and requires oxygen
(c) Glycolysis is the only activity of respiration in aerobic respirating
animals.
(d) In this process six carbon glucose is converted to three carbon
pyruvate.
questions.explanation: Option A is correct because Glycolysis is a cytosolic biochemical pathway (a) splitting one six-carbon glucose into two three-carbon pyruvate molecules (d). It is not nuclear (b), not oxygen-dependent at the glycolytic step itself, and not the sole respiration stage even in aerobes—Krebs cycle and ETS follow. You can eliminate B ((b), (c) only), C ((a), (b), (c) only), D ((a) only) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option A. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Plants use......... method for short distance transport of the element they
need and......... method for long distance transport.
questions.explanation: The answer is option B: Short-distance movement across cell membranes and cell walls uses passive/active diffusion and osmosis at the cellular scale. Long-distance bulk transport of water, minerals, and assimilates runs through xylem and phloem—translocation. Reversing the pair (A) or substituting osmosis for vascular translocation (C) collapses two distinct spatial scales. Distractors A (Translocation, diffusion), C (Translocation, osmosis), D (None of these) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements regarding Diffusion and choose the
incorrect statement option.
(a) Diffusion pressure is the ability of a liquid, gas or solid to move from an
environment of higher concentration to an environment of lower
concentration.
(b) Diffusion continues even after equilibrium has been reached.
(c) Diffusion pressure of pure water is lowest.
questions.explanation: You want the incorrect statements. (a) correctly defines diffusion down a concentration gradient—keep it. (b) is incorrect: at equilibrium net diffusion stops even if micro-scale exchange continues—'continues after equilibrium' is false. (c) is incorrect: pure water has the highest diffusion/osmotic potential, not the lowest. Option B isolates exactly those two wrong limbs.

questions.text:
Study the following statements and choose the correct option.
(a) Plants release water in the form of water vapor through the minute pores on their leaves, this is called transpiration.
(b) Water transport in the plant due to transpiration and root pressure.
(c) Phenyl mercuric acetate (PMA) and abasic acid (AB A) are artificial anti-
evaporation agent.
(d) Silicone emulsion, colorless plastic resins are natural anti-evaporation
agents.

options.D: All of the above are correct.

questions.explanation: Transpiration is foliar water-vapour loss through stomata (a), and the transpiration pull couples with root pressure in ascent of sap (b)—both stand. PMA and ABA are cited here as anti-transpirants (c). Silicone emulsions and colourless plastic resins are synthetic/antitranspirant coatings, not 'natural' agents (d)—that swap is the deliberate trap.

questions.text:
Match the correct pairs.
(a) Hygroscopic water | i) In the form of oxides
(b) Combined water | ii) In small tubes / cavities
(c) Gravitational water | iii) Firmly bound to soil particles
(d) Capillary water | iv) Sinks deeper due to gravity
questions.explanation: Option D is the right choice since Hygroscopic water is held so tightly on soil particle surfaces that roots cannot extract it (iii). Combined water is locked in soil minerals as oxides/hydroxides (i). Gravitational water drains downward beyond field capacity (iv). Capillary water occupies pore spaces and is the plant-available pool (ii). The d→iii, a→i, b→iv, c→ii grid is internally consistent; other permutations mis-assign availability. Distractors A ((i) (iii) (iv) (ii)), B ((ii) (i) (iv) (iii)), C ((i) (iii) (ii) (iv)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Observe the following statements and choose the option which is not
incorrect.
(a) The movement of solute from a solution of lower concentration to a solution
of higher concentration through a membrane is called osmosis.
(b) osmosis was termed by Abi Nollate.
(c) No energy is expended in osmosis.

options.D: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation: Double-negative again: pick the assessment that is not wrong. The paper treats (a) and (b) as correct and (c) as incorrect—key A. Coach note: exam keys sometimes garble osmosis wording; here solvent movement and Nollet's historical naming are accepted as stated, while disputing (c) matches the correct split. Options elevating (c) over (a) or (b) miss the paper's chosen partition.

questions.text:
Study the following statements and choose the option which is not correct.
(a) Flower is the functional unit of sexual reproduction in plants.
(b) Carpel and stamen are sexual organs between female plant and male plant.
(c) Meosis and fertilization are the main methods of sexual reproduction in
plants.
questions.explanation: Option D works here because the question asks which option is not correct—i.e., all statements are correct per key D. (a) Flower is the angiosperm reproductive organ. (b) Carpel (pistil) is female; stamen is male—both are floral sexual whorls. (c) Meiosis in sporogenous tissue plus double fertilisation defines sexual reproduction. Options marking any limb incorrect contradict the correct 'none wrong' stand. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text:
Study the following statements regarding the use of Auxin.
(a) Root and stem growth is promoted by auxin.
(b) Auxins help in the formation of vegetative reproduction.
(c) A artificial auxin called 2-4D is mainly used to control dicot weeds in mono-
legume fields.
(d) Auxin reduces the rate of photosynthesis by promoting senescence.

options.A: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation: Option C is correct because auxin at low concentration promotes root initiation and stem elongation (a), triggers adventitious/rooting in vegetative propagation (b), and synthetic 2,4-D serves as a selective dicot herbicide in cereal fields (c). Claiming auxin reduces photosynthesis via senescence (d) belongs to ABA/ethylene physiology, not auxin's primary syllabus role—so (d) is the outlier. Distractors A (All of the above are correct), B ((b), (c), (d) correct, (a) Incorrect), D (None of these.) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text:
Which of the following substances is affected by mosaic virus?
(a) Tobacco
(b) Potato
(c) Cucumber
(d) Rice
(e)
Cowpea
f)
Alpha-alpha
questions.explanation: The answer is option B: Tobacco mosaic virus (TMV) classically infects tobacco (a), cucumber (c), cowpea (e), and alfalfa/lucerne (f)—the correct B set. Potato and rice appear in other virus stories (PVY, RTV) but not in this paper's TMV host list. Over-inclusive

questions.text:
Match the correct pairs.
(a) Parasitic plants. | i) Pitcher plant
(b) Saprotrophic plants | ii) cuscuta, Reflesia
(c) Insectivorous | iii) Lichen
(d) Symbiotic plants | iv) Penicillium
questions.explanation: Option D matches the question because Parasitic dodder (Cuscuta) and Rafflesia live on host plants (ii). Insectivorous pitcher plant traps insects (i)—not saprotroph Penicillium (iv). Saprotrophic decomposers include moulds such as Penicillium (iv). Lichen is fungus–alga symbiosis (iii). Key D: a→ii, b→iv, c→i, d→iii; options placing Cuscuta with pitcher or Penicillium with lichen break nutrition-mode logic. You can eliminate A ((i) (ii) (iv) (iii)), B ((ii) (i) (iv) (iii)), C ((i) (iii) (ii) (iv)) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Check the correctness of the statements about growth related movements
in plants and select the correct statement option.
(a) In balsam and castor plants, the fruit bursts at the right time and the seeds
spread everywhere.
(b) Pitcher plant, venus fly trap These plants are completely dependent on
other plants for food.
(c) Cuscuta and Bandagul meet their nitrogen requirement by feeding on insects.
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: Choose option D: Explosive dehiscence in balsam (Impatiens) and castor scatters seeds mechanically (a)—true. Pitcher plant and Venus flytrap are insectivorous autotrophs supplementing nitrogen; they are not wholly dependent on other plants for food (b). Cuscuta is parasitic, not insectivorous; 'Bandagul' here points to bladderwort/Utricularia-type traps, not nitrogen from insects in Cuscuta (c). Only (a) survives. Distractors A (Only (a), (b)), B (Only (a), (b), (c)), C (Only (b), (c)) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Statement- Absxisic acid is called antigibberelins hormone.
Cause- Absxisic acid inhibits gibberellin-activated growth.

options.A: (a) and (b) are correct and (b) is the cause of (a).
options.B: (a) and (b) are correct and (b) is not a reason for (a).

questions.explanation: ABA antagonises GA-promoted growth—stem elongation, enzyme mobilisation in germination—earning the label 'anti-gibberellin' (a). Statement (b) gives the mechanism: ABA inhibition of gibberellin-activated pathways. Cause–effect pairing is valid; denying the link (B/C) or rejecting both (D) misses textbook hormone opposition.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements regarding fertilization.
(a) Each pollen tube contains two male gametes.
(b) A male gamet unites with an ovum to form a zygote.
(c) The endosperm is formed by the fusion of the second male gamete with the
secondary nucleus.
(d) The zygote develops on the stigma.
Choose the correct statement/s

options.A: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation: The correct answer is option D — Pollen tubes carry two male gametes (a). One fuses with the egg → zygote (b). The second fuses with polar nuclei → triploid endosperm (c). Zygote develops inside the ovule/embryo sac, not on the stigma (d)—stigma is only the landing pad. All except (d) are standard double-fertilisation facts. You can eliminate A (All of the above are correct), B ((b), (c), (d) correct, (a) incorrect), C ((a), (c), (d) correct, (b) incorrect) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option D. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements.
(a) Photoautotrophs use light as energy to produce living food.
(b) Chemotrophs produce food using energy produced by living chemical
reactions.
(c) Scientists Ruben and Kamen proved that the oxygen released in
photosynthesis is obtained from water.

options.D: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation: The correct answer is All of the above are correct. Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose; the overall equation is 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂, driven by chlorophyll in chloroplasts. Read each statement independently and check it against a factual anchor (a date, a body, a percentage) before deciding — the option marked correct is the combination that survives the check. This is a classic MPSC 'anchor-word' item — the stem contains one specific term (a proper noun, a date, an article number) that maps directly to only one option.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements.
(a) No energy is expended in diffusion.
(b) Energy is expended in plant osmosis.
(c) No energy is expended in osmosis processes in the cells of the human body.

options.A: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation: Diffusion is passive—no ATP (a). Active transport energises many plant osmotic adjustments at membranes, so 'energy expended in plant osmosis' (b) is accepted in this item. Human cell osmosis across erythrocyte membranes is likewise passive at the basic level (c). Denying (b) or (c) splits what the paper bundles as all correct.

questions.text:
Match the elements and their deficiency diseases.
(a) Nitrogen | i) Leaf spotting
(b) Sulfur | ii) Production of chlorophyll
(c) Potassium | iii) Late flowering
(d) Iron | iv) Activates nitrogen metabolism enzymes
(e)
Molybdenum.
v) Participation in photosynthesis and respiration
questions.explanation: The answer is option C: N deficiency → stunted growth and delayed/late flowering (iii). S deficiency → leaf chlorosis/spots (i). K participates in stomatal opening, enzyme activation, and photosynthesis-linked processes (v). Fe is essential for chlorophyll synthesis and enzyme systems (ii). Mo activates nitrate reductase and nitrogen metabolism (iv). Key C: a-iii, b-i, c-v, d-ii, e-iv. You can eliminate A ((a) - (i), (b) - (ii), (c) - (iii), (d)…), B ((a) - (iii), (b) - (i), (c) - (ii), (d)…), D ((a) - (v), (b) - (iv), (c) - (iii), (d)…) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Study the following statements and choose the option of the correct
statement.
(a) The process of transporting food to each part of a plant is called translocation.
(b) Translocation is unidirectional.
(c) ATP is required for translocation as energy is expended.
(d) Excess food except amino acids is stored in roots, fruits, seeds.

options.D: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation: Option B matches the question because Translocation is phloem transport of assimilates to sinks (a). It is multidirectional—root storage, fruit filling, spring remobilisation—not strictly one-way (b is wrong). Active loading/unloading spends ATP (c). Excess carbohydrate is stored as starch in roots, fruits, and seeds—not 'except amino acids' phrasing aside, storage organs hold non-protein reserves (d). B keeps a,c,d and drops unidirectional (b). Distractors A (Only (a), (b), (c) correct (d) incorrect), C (Only (a), (b), (d) correct (c) incorrect), D (All of the above are correct) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text: Roots use the ........... water in the soil.
questions.explanation: Roots absorb capillary water held in soil pore spaces at field capacity—the intermediate pool between hygroscopic (too tight) and gravitational (drains away). Hygroscopic and combined water are unavailable; gravitational water moves too fast for sustained uptake.

questions.text:
Study the following statements regarding photosynthesis and select
the correct statement option.
(a) Photosynthesis requires respiration of energy in the form of light rays.
(b) Synthesis is highest under red light.
(c) Photosynthesis does not occur in yellow and infrared.

options.D: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is a light-driven endergonic process (a). Red wavelengths (~660 nm) peak in chlorophyll absorption and show high quantum yield (b). Yellow and far-red/infrared are poorly absorbed by chlorophyll—minimal photosynthesis (c). All three limbs align with action-spectrum facts; splitting them mis-reads the spectrum chart.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements regarding reproduction in plants and
choose the option which is not incorrect.
(a) Plants reproduce both sexually and asexually.
(b) Root, stem, leaf, bud are involved in vegetative reproduction in plants.
(c) Plants undergo meosis like animals.

options.D: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation: The correct answer is option D — Plants reproduce sexually (seed/flower) and asexually (vegetative organs) (a). Roots (sweet potato), stems (potato, ginger), leaves (Bryophyllum), buds all propagate vegetatively (b). Meiosis precedes spore/pollen/egg formation in the sexual cycle—parallel to animals (c). All three stand; denying meiosis in plants (common trap) is incorrect angiosperm life-cycle basics. Distractors A ((a), (b) only), B ((b), (c) only), C ((a), (c) only) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements regarding cytokinin.
(a) School and Miller discovered cytokinin while they were culturing tobacco
plant tissue.
(b) Cytokinin is derived from the purine thiamine.
(c) Cytokinin is found in plants where cell division takes place.

options.D: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation: Skoog and Miller discovered cytokinin from autoclaved herring sperm/coconut milk during tobacco tissue culture (a). Cytokinin is an adenine/purine derivative—not thiamine (b is wrong). It concentrates in meristems, young fruits, and dividing tissues (c). Key A: accept (a,c), reject mis-named precursor (b).

questions.text:
Match the correct pairs.
(a) Hosts on branches | i) Orbanche, Reflecia
(b) Hosts on roots
(ii) Santalum album
(c) Incomplete host on branches
(iii) Amarvel
(d) Incomplete fertilization on roots. (iv) Mistletoe
questions.explanation: Option A is correct because amarvel (Cuscuta) twines on branches (iii). Root parasites include Orobanche and Rafflesia (i). Mistletoe (Viscum) is a partial stem parasite on branches (iv). Sandalwood (Santalum) is a root hemiparasite (ii). Key A: a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii. Options swapping sandalwood to branch host or Amarvel to root is wrong parasitism ecology. Store the reasoning behind the answer, not just the letter, because topic packs revisit the same idea in different forms.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements regarding Kreb’s series and select
the correct statement option.
(a) Sir Hans Kreb was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1953 for his
discovery of Kreb’s series.
(b) Kreb’s cycle is also known as TCA cycle.
(c) Transport of H+ ions across the cell membrane is essential for the formation
of ATP.

options.D: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation: The answer is option D: Hans Krebs elucidated the citric-acid cycle—TCA/Krebs cycle—in mitochondrial matrix (b); Nobel recognition for metabolism work is syllabus-linked to him (a). Proton gradient across the inner mitochondrial membrane drives chemiosmotic ATP synthesis (c)—also true in ETS context. All three are accepted here; cherry-picking only two drops valid bioenergetics. Distractors A (Only (a), (b) correct, (c) incorrect), B (Only (b), (c) correct, (a) incorrect), C (Only (a), (c) correct, (b) incorrect) look plausible but do not follow from the facts stated in the question. Keep the name, formula, and unit together in your notes — that helps you spot incomplete distractors quickly.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements and choose the option which is not correct.
(a) Photochemical phase takes place in the thalloid in chlorophyll.
(b) Energy is basically converted in a light reaction.
(c) Dark reaction takes place in stroma in chlorophyll.
(d) Proteins are produced in dark reaction reactions.
questions.explanation: Photochemical phase occurs in thylakoid/granal membranes (a). Light reactions convert radiant energy to chemical carriers (b). Calvin cycle runs in stroma (c). Dark reactions fix CO₂ into sugars—not protein manufacture (d); proteins need ribosomal translation. Key A: a,b,c stand; (d) is the incorrect limb about protein synthesis in Calvin cycle.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements and select the correct statement
option.
(a) Wheat, rice, barley are examples of C4 plant.
(b) Maize, sugarcane, sorghum are examples of C3 plants.
(d) Pineapple, onion, garlic are examples of CAM plants.

options.D: All of the above are correct

questions.explanation: Choose option C: Wheat, rice, barley are classic C3 plants—statement (a) is false. Maize, sugarcane, sorghum are C4—(b) is false. Pineapple, onion, garlic use CAM (crassulacean acid metabolism)—(d) is the sole correct line. Option C ('all incorrect except c') matches; note the paper labels CAM as statement (d) even though (c) is missing from the stem text. You can eliminate A (All are incorrect except (a)), B (All are incorrect except (b)), D (All of the above are correct) — each one conflicts with the principle or calculation that leads to option C. MPSC papers often recycle this type of detail, so read the question carefully before you commit to an option.

questions.text:
Match the correct pairs.
(a) Radical | i) Hair like threads at root tip
(b) plumule | ii) Part growing towards the ground
(c) Tap-root | iii) Sub-roots to roots
(d) Root hair | iv) Above ground growing part
questions.explanation: Option D is the right choice since Radicle is the embryonic root that grows downward (ii). Plumule is the shoot apex rising above ground (iv). Tap-root system forms the primary root with branches (iii). Root hairs are epidermal extensions for absorption (i). Key D: a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i. Options pairing plumule with downward growth or root hair with aerial parts invert seedling geography. If the question asks what is incorrect, identify the false statement first and then match it to the answer choice.

questions.text:
Select the correct option below about anti-evaporative absxisic acid.
(a) Promote aging
(b) Reducing the rate of photosynthesis by reducing chlorophyll in leaf

(b) They have openings on the body called ostiums while larger openings on the

(c) Osculum acts like mouth while ostium acts like anus.
questions.explanation: The answer is option C: Every true sponge sits in Porifera—(a) is a clean phylum–group match. Water enters through numerous small incurrent pores (ostia) and leaves through the large excurrent opening (osculum)—(b) is anatomically sound. Statement (c) reverses flow logic: the osculum is the exit ('ex-current'), not the mouth analogue, and ostia are entry pores, not an anal opening. Only (a) and (b) survive. Fish hearts are typically two-chambered (one auricle, one ventricle), not three—(b) is incorrect. All fishes are poikilothermic (cold-blooded)—(c) is incorrect. Only (a) and (d) remain. questions.text:
